title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
瞻之在前忽焉在後
朱溓
同考試官教諭吳批論語一題作者不泛則滯明贍
詳整如此篇者詎可得耶錄之不專以其文爾
同考試官學正胡批述先難之故萬世如見亦善發
顏子之蘊者乎
考試官訓導夏批辭副乎理邃於文者
===
考試官訓導閔批渾厚醇粹大非他作所及
大賢之嘆聖道擬之而不可為象也蓋道有可
象非道之妙也然則聖人之道大賢亦安能遽
得其象於前後之間也哉昔顏子學既有得述
其先難之故而嘆之至此若曰吾夫子之聖也
其見諸身固無適而非道而其為道也亦何往
而非妙哉故方吾求道之初欲有以彷彿之也
而極目以瞻之徘徊之際亦嘗會無形於有形
宛與我而相值焉欲有以擬議之也而凝眸以
banxin: 福建鄉試錄二十二
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

瞻之在前，忽焉在後。

朱溓

同考試官教諭吳批：論語一題，作者不泛則滯。明贍詳整如此篇者，詎可得耶？錄之不專以其文爾。

同考試官學正胡批：述先難之故，萬世如見，亦善發顏子之蘊者乎！

考試官訓導夏批：辭副乎理，邃於文者。

考試官訓導閔批：渾厚醇粹，大非他作所及。

大賢之嘆聖道，擬之而不可為象也。蓋道有可象，非道之妙也。然則聖人之道，大賢亦安能遽得其象於前後之間也哉？昔顏子學既有得，述其先難之故，而嘆之至此，若曰：吾夫子之聖也，其見諸身，固無適而非道；而其為道也，亦何往而非妙哉？故方吾求道之初，欲有以彷彿之也，而極目以瞻之，徘徊之際，亦嘗會無形於有形，宛與我而相值焉；欲有以擬議之也，而凝眸以
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“When I look for it, it is before me; suddenly it is behind me.”

Zhu Lian 朱溓

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: On this topic from the Analects, writers tend either to be vague or to become bogged down. Where could one find another essay as lucid, ample, thorough, and orderly as this? It is not solely for its literary qualities that I select it for inclusion.

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: In recounting the reasons for the initial difficulties, it makes them seem visible even ten thousand generations later. Does it not also admirably bring out what lay within Master Yan’s mind!

Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: The language matches the principle: a writer of profound literary attainment.

Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: Substantial, rich, pure, and refined—far beyond the reach of other compositions.

The great worthy’s sigh over the Way of the sage arose because, though he sought to conceive it, he could not give it an image. For insofar as the Way can be represented in an image, that is not its subtlety. How, then, could even the great worthy readily grasp an image of the sage’s Way somewhere between before and behind? In former times, after Master Yan had made progress in learning, he recounted the reasons for his initial difficulties and sighed over them in these terms, as though saying:

“As for our Master’s sageliness, wherever it manifests itself in his person, there is assuredly nothing that is not the Way. And as for that Way, where is it ever without subtlety? Thus, when I first sought the Way, I wished to gain some inkling of it and strained my eyes to look for it. As I lingered in contemplation, I did at times apprehend the formless within what had form, as though it had come directly before me. I wished to conceive and consider it, and fixed my gaze in order to…”

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
視之俯仰之餘亦嘗契無象於有象恍與我而
相參焉就之若見其可親也嚮之若見其可往
也而夫子之道有著於吾前矣據之若見其可
守也憑之若見其可依也而夫子之道有形於
吾目矣夫瞻之在前吾以道在是矣然力未及
於精詳也而已遽失其似時方屬於頃刻也而
已遂忘其初向之彷彿而在前者忽焉復在吾
之後相值也卒與我而相違悵悵然徒自立於
混茫之地顧何所親而亦何所往耶向之擬議
而在前者忽焉又出吾之後相參也竟與我而
相失皇皇然徒自處於蒙昧之所將孰為守而
亦孰為依耶是則在前而又在後若得而又若
遺恍惚不可為象如此是可以易心求之哉雖
然聖人可學而至也畏其難而自沮可乎由博
文約禮循序而進以至欲罷不能既竭吾才則
卓爾之域可馴致矣此顏子已試之明驗也先
儒謂顏子發聖人之蘊教萬世無窮其此章之
謂乎後之學聖人者宜服膺而勿失
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 二十三
punctuated: 視之，俯仰之餘，亦嘗契無象於有象，恍與我而相參焉。就之，若見其可親也；嚮之，若見其可往也，而夫子之道有著於吾前矣。據之，若見其可守也；憑之，若見其可依也，而夫子之道有形於吾目矣。夫瞻之在前，吾以道在是矣。然力未及於精詳也，而已遽失其似；時方屬於頃刻也，而已遂忘其初。向之彷彿而在前者，忽焉復在吾之後；相值也，卒與我而相違。悵悵然徒自立於混茫之地，顧何所親，而亦何所往耶？向之擬議而在前者，忽焉又出吾之後；相參也，竟與我而相失。皇皇然徒自處於蒙昧之所，將孰為守，而亦孰為依耶？是則在前而又在後，若得而又若遺，恍惚不可為象如此，是可以易心求之哉？雖然，聖人可學而至也，畏其難而自沮可乎？由博文約禮，循序而進，以至欲罷不能，既竭吾才，則卓爾之域可馴致矣。此顏子已試之明驗也。先儒謂顏子發聖人之蘊，教萬世無窮，其此章之謂乎？後之學聖人者，宜服膺而勿失。
translation_en:
…gaze upon it. In the course of looking down and up, I once apprehended the formless within what has form, as though it had come into communion with me. Approaching it, I seemed to see something I could draw close to; turning toward it, I seemed to see somewhere I could proceed. Thus the Master’s Way became manifest before me. Taking hold of it, I seemed to see something I could keep; leaning upon it, I seemed to see something I could rely on. Thus the Master’s Way took shape before my eyes.

When I gazed upon it and found it before me, I thought the Way was here. Yet before my efforts could attain precision and thoroughness, I had already abruptly lost its likeness; scarcely a moment had passed, and I had already forgotten how it first appeared. What had earlier seemed dimly present before me was suddenly behind me again. Having met me, it ultimately drew away from me. Disconsolate, I merely stood in a realm of obscurity: what could I draw close to, and where could I go? What I had earlier tried to conceive and describe as being before me suddenly appeared behind me once more. Having come into communion with me, it ultimately eluded me. Anxious and unsettled, I merely remained in a place of ignorance: what could I keep, and what could I rely on? Thus it is before me and then behind me; I seem to grasp it and then seem to lose it. So elusive that no image can capture it—could one seek it with a careless mind?

Nevertheless, sagehood can be attained through learning. Can one shrink back in discouragement out of fear of its difficulty? By broadening one’s learning through cultural studies and restraining oneself through ritual propriety, one advances in due order until one cannot stop even if one wishes to. Once I have exhausted my abilities, that loftily outstanding realm can gradually be attained. This is clear evidence from what Master Yan (Yan Zi) himself had already put to the test. Earlier Confucian scholars said that Master Yan disclosed the sage’s innermost profundities and taught the myriad generations without end. Were they speaking of this chapter? Those in later ages who seek to emulate the sage should take it to heart and never let it slip away.

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
夫微之顯誠之不可揜如此夫
楊萼
同考試官教諭沈批中庸精粹之理無出此者
是作獨能以精粹之語發之可以為式矣
同考試官教諭杜批發明陰陽合散之理不餘一
辭錄之以範膚淺之學
考試官訓導夏批理到辭到
考試官訓導閔批說理之文惟有此篇
中庸結言鬼神之隱而見者一本於實理之為
===
也蓋隱而能見鬼神之德盛矣謂不本於實理
而能若是也哉中庸十六章發明道之費隱而
有及于此蓋謂鬼神之德固極其盛而其所以
盛也要必有其本者在焉是故其為體也以形
求之泯焉若無而不可得于其形斯天下之至
幽者也以聲擬之杳焉若寂而不可得于其聲
斯天下之至隱者也其微如此然効其能於兩
間而天地之功賴之以成一往一來而物之終
始有不能遺其情狀蓋炳有可見者焉昭其靈
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 二十四
punctuated:
夫微之顯，誠之不可揜如此夫！
楊萼
同考試官教諭沈批：中庸精粹之理，無出此者。是作獨能以精粹之語發之，可以為式矣。
同考試官教諭杜批：發明陰陽合散之理，不餘一辭，錄之以範膚淺之學。
考試官訓導夏批：理到，辭到。
考試官訓導閔批：說理之文，惟有此篇。
中庸結言鬼神之隱而見者，一本於實理之為也。蓋隱而能見，鬼神之德盛矣，謂不本於實理而能若是也哉？中庸十六章發明道之費隱，而有及于此。蓋謂鬼神之德固極其盛，而其所以盛也，要必有其本者在焉。是故其為體也，以形求之，泯焉若無，而不可得于其形，斯天下之至幽者也；以聲擬之，杳焉若寂，而不可得于其聲，斯天下之至隱者也。其微如此，然効其能於兩間，而天地之功賴之以成，一往一來，而物之終始有不能遺，其情狀蓋炳有可見者焉；昭其靈
translation_en:
“How manifest is the subtle! Such is the impossibility of concealing sincerity!”
Yang E 楊萼
Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: “Nothing surpasses this passage in expressing the essential principles of the Doctrine of the Mean. This composition alone can elucidate them in language of corresponding refinement. It may serve as a model.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Du, Instructor: “It elucidates the principles of the conjunction and dispersal of yin and yang without a single superfluous phrase. It is recorded here to provide a standard for those whose learning is superficial.”
Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: “The reasoning is fully realized, and so is its expression.”
Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: “Among compositions explaining principle, this essay alone stands out.”
The Doctrine of the Mean concludes by saying that the manifestation of ghosts and spirits, though hidden, is rooted entirely in the operation of real principle. Hidden yet able to manifest themselves: abundant indeed is the potency of ghosts and spirits! Could they achieve this without being rooted in real principle? Chapter sixteen of the Doctrine of the Mean elucidates the Way’s pervasive operation and hidden subtlety, and thus touches upon this matter. Its meaning is that the potency of ghosts and spirits is indeed supremely abundant, yet this abundance must necessarily have a foundation.
Thus, as to their constitution: seek them through form, and they vanish as though nonexistent, ungraspable in any form—this is the utmost obscurity under Heaven. Try to apprehend them through sound, and they are remote as though silent, ungraspable in any sound—this is the utmost hiddenness under Heaven. Such is their subtlety. Yet they exert their powers between Heaven and Earth, and the work of Heaven and Earth depends upon them for its accomplishment. In their alternating departure and arrival, the ending and beginning of things cannot dispense with them; their workings are thus brilliantly apparent to view. They manifest their numinous power …

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
於六合而造化之迹因之以著一屈一伸而物
之始終自不能外其功效蓋灼有可觀者焉夫
鬼神之微而能顯者果何以哉亦惟誠焉而已
耳蓋鬼神一陰陽也陰陽一實理也於穆之表
孰綱維是倏而合倏而散莫非純一不二者以
為之本範圍之內孰根柢是合而凝散而盡莫
非真實無妄者以為之基故其體既實而用自
行往來相推含之而愈光無為而無不為也發
越之盛塞乎兩間而不能以自秘否則與物不
===
相值矣烏能如是其顯哉徳既實而效自著屈
伸相感翕之而愈闢無在而無不在也昭明之
迹彌乎六合而不能以自藏否則於物無所攝
矣烏能若此其顯哉是則體之微者隱也用之
顯者費也中庸即鬼神之徳之盛以明道之全
體其意深矣抑嘗因是而考之誠者造化之樞
紐雖天地之大所弗能違者而况於鬼神乎知
鬼神本於誠則知有無動靜通一無二而道有
可求者後世不知乎此徇無者淪於空執有者
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 二十五
punctuated:
於六合，而造化之迹因之以著；一屈一伸，而物之始終自不能外其功效，蓋灼有可觀者焉。夫鬼神之微而能顯者，果何以哉？亦惟誠焉而已耳。蓋鬼神，一陰陽也；陰陽，一實理也。於穆之表，孰綱維是？倏而合，倏而散，莫非純一不二者以為之本。範圍之內，孰根柢是？合而凝，散而盡，莫非真實無妄者以為之基。故其體既實，而用自行；往來相推，含之而愈光，無為而無不為也。發越之盛，塞乎兩間，而不能以自秘；否則與物不相值矣，烏能如是其顯哉？徳既實，而效自著；屈伸相感，翕之而愈闢，無在而無不在也。昭明之迹，彌乎六合，而不能以自藏；否則於物無所攝矣，烏能若此其顯哉？

是則體之微者，隱也；用之顯者，費也。《中庸》即鬼神之徳之盛，以明道之全體，其意深矣。抑嘗因是而考之：誠者，造化之樞紐，雖天地之大所弗能違者，而况於鬼神乎？知鬼神本於誠，則知有無動靜，通一無二，而道有可求者。後世不知乎此，徇無者淪於空，執有者
translation_en:
…throughout the six directions, and through it the workings of creation and transformation become manifest. With each contraction and expansion, the beginnings and endings of things cannot fall outside its efficacy: there is indeed something clearly observable here. How is it that ghosts and spirits, though subtle, can become manifest? It is solely through sincerity, that is, their utter reality. For ghosts and spirits are simply yin and yang, and yin and yang are simply real principle. Beyond the profound mystery, what holds all this together? Suddenly gathering and suddenly dispersing, all takes as its foundation that which is wholly one and undivided. Within the compass of the cosmos, what gives all this its root? Gathering and congealing, dispersing and coming to an end, all takes as its basis that which is genuine and without falsity. Thus, since their substance is real, their functioning proceeds of itself. Coming and going impel one another; the more their light is contained, the more radiant it becomes. They act without deliberate action, yet leave nothing undone. Their abundant manifestation fills the space between heaven and earth and cannot remain concealed. Otherwise, they would have no encounter with things: how could they be so manifest? Since their potency is real, its effects become evident of themselves. Contraction and expansion respond to one another; the more they draw inward, the more widely they unfold. They abide in no particular place, yet there is nowhere they are absent. The traces of their radiance extend throughout the six directions and cannot remain hidden. Otherwise, they would have no sway over things: how could they be manifest in this way?

Thus, the subtlety of their substance is what is hidden; the manifestation of their functioning is what is all-pervasive. The Doctrine of the Mean takes the abundant potency of ghosts and spirits to illuminate the Way in its entirety: its meaning is profound indeed. Yet I have also pursued the matter further on this basis: sincerity is the pivot of creation and transformation. Even heaven and earth, great as they are, cannot depart from it; how much less can ghosts and spirits? To know that ghosts and spirits are rooted in sincerity is to know that being and nonbeing, movement and stillness, are united as one, without duality, and that the Way can be sought therein. Later generations have not understood this. Those who pursue nonbeing sink into emptiness; those who cling to being…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
泥於迹而其所謂鬼神亦異於是矣此邪說所
以惑世而誣民也子思引孔子之言固已明乎
道體而其以闢邪扶敎之意亦有不可誣者歟
日月有明容光必照焉
方召南
同考試官訓導徐批此題塲中類為所窘是篇詞
氣灝發若不經思而理自足審非無本者也
同考試官敎諭吳批說理之言深沉雅飭所以為難
耳錄之
===
考試官訓導夏批能委曲通孟子𫥨意明𤽜可式
考試官訓導閔批理致之詞雄勁之筆足範後學
大賢論二曜之著而無微不及者以見聖道之
有本也蓋日月二曜天象之至著者也而光無
遺照焉非其明之有本而能然乎孟子論孔子
之道而此則言其有本也如此意謂不觀聖道
之有本固未知其所以為大不觀日月之有明
又寧知其所以有本哉故陽本明也日則秉陽
之精而明於晝陰雖晦也月則受日之光而明
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 二十六
punctuated:
泥於迹，而其所謂鬼神亦異於是矣。此邪說所以惑世而誣民也。子思引孔子之言，固已明乎道體，而其以闢邪扶敎之意，亦有不可誣者歟！

日月有明，容光必照焉。
方召南

同考試官訓導徐批：此題塲中類為所窘，是篇詞氣灝發，若不經思而理自足，審非無本者也。

同考試官敎諭吳批：說理之言，深沉雅飭，所以為難耳。錄之。

考試官訓導夏批：能委曲通孟子𫥨意，明𤽜可式。

考試官訓導閔批：理致之詞，雄勁之筆，足範後學。

大賢論二曜之著而無微不及者，以見聖道之有本也。蓋日月二曜，天象之至著者也，而光無遺照焉，非其明之有本而能然乎？孟子論孔子之道，而此則言其有本也如此。意謂不觀聖道之有本，固未知其所以為大；不觀日月之有明，又寧知其所以有本哉？故陽本明也，日則秉陽之精而明於晝；陰雖晦也，月則受日之光而明
translation_en:
…become mired in outward traces, and what they call ghosts and spirits likewise differs from what is described here. This is how heterodox teachings delude the world and deceive the people. In quoting Confucius, Zisi certainly made clear the substance of the Way; surely his intention to refute heterodoxy and uphold the teaching is also undeniable!

“The sun and moon possess brightness; wherever light can enter, they invariably illuminate it.”
By Fang Zhaonan.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor: Candidates in the examination generally found themselves at a loss with this topic. This essay’s language and force flow forth abundantly, as though composed without deliberation, yet its reasoning is complete in itself. It certainly does not lack a foundation.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: Language that expounds principles must be profound, poised, elegant, and disciplined: that is what makes it difficult. Include this essay in the record.

Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: It comprehensively conveys Mencius’s intent [?]; it is lucid [?] and worthy of emulation.

Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: Its language conveys the purport of the principles, and its writing is powerful and vigorous. It suffices as a model for later students.

The great worthy discusses how the two luminaries are manifest and reach even the smallest recesses, thereby showing that the Way of the sage has a foundation. The sun and moon, the two luminaries, are the most conspicuous of celestial phenomena, yet their light leaves nothing unilluminated. Could they accomplish this unless their brightness had a foundation? Mencius discusses the Way of Confucius, and here he speaks in this manner of its having a foundation. His meaning is that, unless one considers the foundation of the sage’s Way, one cannot understand what makes it great; and unless one considers the brightness of the sun and moon, how could one understand what gives it a foundation? Thus yang is inherently bright: the sun holds the essence of yang and shines by day. Although yin is dark, the moon receives the sun’s light and shines…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
於夜揭中天而行而群陰爲之屏伏有以發皜
皜之輝懸層霄而麗而列宿爲之隱藏有以流
皎皎之素貞明之道在宇宙而常新有目者之
所共覩也其明也孰加焉久照之體終萬古而
有耀有見者之所共仰也其明也孰尚焉惟日
月有明如此是以九州四海何廣大也舉其所
下臨之地八方萬國何遼邈也皆其所旁燭之
鄉是惟無隙則已一有隙焉而光即抵之未有
不遇之而成色者是惟無間則已一有間焉而
===
光即投之未有不借之而增彩者乘虛生白其
餘光之所被有以破暗室之幽矣夫豈照於此
而遺於彼乎自牖通明其餘輝之所及有以啓
豐蔀之蔽矣又豈照於大而遺於小乎是則明
之有本如此此日月之所以爲日月也孔子之
道之大而夫豈無其本哉雖然孟子之於孔子
始以登山觀海爲言繼以日月觀瀾爲言其論
亦極於高遠而無繼矣然豈徒爲是嚮仰者之
言哉蓋嘗致力於是而獨會於心故不覺其嘆
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 二十七
punctuated: 於夜。揭中天而行，而群陰爲之屏伏，有以發皜皜之輝；懸層霄而麗，而列宿爲之隱藏，有以流皎皎之素。貞明之道，在宇宙而常新，有目者之所共覩也，其明也孰加焉？久照之體，終萬古而有耀，有見者之所共仰也，其明也孰尚焉？惟日月有明如此，是以九州四海，何廣大也，舉其所下臨之地；八方萬國，何遼邈也，皆其所旁燭之鄉。是惟無隙則已，一有隙焉，而光即抵之，未有不遇之而成色者；是惟無間則已，一有間焉，而光即投之，未有不借之而增彩者。乘虛生白，其餘光之所被，有以破暗室之幽矣，夫豈照於此而遺於彼乎？自牖通明，其餘輝之所及，有以啓豐蔀之蔽矣，又豈照於大而遺於小乎？是則明之有本如此，此日月之所以爲日月也。孔子之道之大，而夫豈無其本哉？雖然，孟子之於孔子，始以登山觀海爲言，繼以日月觀瀾爲言，其論亦極於高遠而無繼矣。然豈徒爲是嚮仰者之言哉？蓋嘗致力於是，而獨會於心，故不覺其嘆
translation_en:
…at night. Rising into mid-heaven and moving onward, it makes the gathered darkness retreat and lie subdued, sending forth its radiant brilliance; suspended in the lofty heavens in splendor, it makes the ranks of stars disappear, diffusing its clear white light. Their constant illumination remains ever fresh throughout the universe, witnessed by all who have eyes: what can surpass their brightness? Their enduring capacity to shine retains its radiance through all ages, admired by all who can see: what can exceed their brightness? Since the sun and moon possess such brightness, the Nine Provinces and Four Seas, vast though they are, are all lands beneath their gaze; the eight directions and myriad states, distant though they are, are all regions reached by their light. Only where there is no crevice does the matter end; wherever a crevice exists, their light reaches it, and nothing fails to acquire color upon meeting it. Only where there is no opening does the matter end; wherever an opening exists, their light enters it, and nothing fails to gain greater brilliance by borrowing from it. Entering empty spaces and producing brightness, even their residual light dispels the gloom of a dark room wherever it falls. How could they illuminate this place and neglect that one? Admitting brightness through a window, even their residual radiance opens up the obscurity of dense screening wherever it reaches. How could they illuminate what is great and neglect what is small? Such is the rootedness of their brightness; this is what makes the sun and moon what they are. Could the greatness of Confucius’s Way possibly lack such a root?

Nevertheless, when speaking of Confucius, Mencius began with climbing mountains and observing the sea, then went on to the sun and moon and observing the billows. His discussion reached the utmost heights and distances, beyond which nothing could follow. Yet were these merely the words of an admirer? He had devoted himself to this Way and attained a distinctive inward understanding of it; thus, without realizing it, his admiration…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
之至此耳觀于下文又曰君子之志於道不成
章不達此造道而有得者之言軻之達於孔子
幾矣是雖爲學者設得非亦以自喻也歟
易
健而說决而和
廖世昭
同考試官教諭沈批夫子賛易義甚明正場
中作者能語其精微者寡爾此作於夬之善處發明詳盡且
詞氣粹然蓋邃於易者也
===
同考試官教諭杜批夬之得中場中作者往往
能言而未了其義且冗贅可厭此作辭鬯理盡真佳士也
考試官訓導夏批典重精詳宜錄以爲程式
考試官訓導閔批易義似此絕少
彖傳賛夬之德以見夫决之善也甚矣决陰之
難也而夬之卦德有以備其善焉宜彖傳指以
示人也歟吾夫子賛易之意蓋謂夬以决陰爲
義夬以得中爲善今此卦之德下體乾也其德
爲健上體兌也其德爲說健而且說吾知其秉
banxin: 福建鄉試錄二十八
punctuated:
之至此耳。觀于下文，又曰：「君子之志於道，不成章不達。」此造道而有得者之言，軻之達於孔子幾矣。是雖爲學者設，得非亦以自喻也歟？

易
健而說，决而和。
廖世昭

同考試官教諭沈批：「夫子賛易，義甚明正。場中作者能語其精微者寡爾。此作於夬之善處發明詳盡，且詞氣粹然，蓋邃於易者也。」

同考試官教諭杜批：「夬之得中，場中作者往往能言，而未了其義，且冗贅可厭。此作辭鬯理盡，真佳士也。」

考試官訓導夏批：「典重精詳，宜錄以爲程式。」

考試官訓導閔批：「易義似此絕少。」

彖傳賛夬之德，以見夫决之善也。甚矣，决陰之難也！而夬之卦德有以備其善焉，宜彖傳指以示人也歟？吾夫子賛易之意，蓋謂夬以决陰爲義，夬以得中爲善。今此卦之德，下體乾也，其德爲健；上體兌也，其德爲說。健而且說，吾知其秉
translation_en:
…that his admiration should reach such a pitch. Looking at the text below, we find it also says: “The gentleman sets his purpose upon the Way; unless he completes an ordered pattern, he does not advance.” These are the words of someone who has approached the Way and gained something from it. Ke [Mengzi] had nearly attained the understanding of Confucius. Although these words were addressed to learners, might they not also describe himself?

Book of Changes
“Strong yet joyous; resolute yet harmonious.”
Liao Shizhao

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: “The Master's elucidation of the Changes is exceedingly clear and correct in meaning. Few writers in the examination hall can articulate its subtleties. This essay explains fully and in detail what makes Guai [Breakthrough] good; moreover, its diction and tone are pure. Its author is surely deeply versed in the Changes.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Du, Instructor: “Writers in the examination hall can often speak of Guai's attaining the mean, yet fail to comprehend its meaning; their writing is also tiresomely prolix. This essay is fluent in expression and exhaustive in explaining the principle. Its author is truly an excellent scholar.”

Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: “Dignified, weighty, precise, and thorough. It should be recorded as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: “Expositions of the Changes like this are exceedingly rare.”

The Commentary on the Judgments elucidates the virtues of Guai to reveal what is good in resolute action. How difficult it is to eliminate yin! Yet the virtues of the hexagram Guai provide all that is needed to accomplish this well. Is it not fitting that the Commentary on the Judgments should point them out to instruct people? Our Master, in elucidating the Changes, surely means that Guai signifies eliminating yin, and that its excellence lies in attaining the mean. Now, as for this hexagram's virtues: its lower trigram is Qian, whose virtue is strength; its upper trigram is Dui, whose virtue is joy. Strong and also joyous, I know that it holds to …

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
純陽之性惕厲常存於一心而有以自強妙天
德之全志氣常伸於萬物而無所係累靜焉專
一其惡惡之心蓋有確乎而不可拔者健孰加
焉然又襟度寛平坦然樂易而可親不怒而威
則威不在於猛矣吾何為而壯吾之煩氣象優
裕怡然温厚而可接不惡而嚴則嚴不在於暴
矣吾何為而厲吾之色若然則其說之德又有
以濟夫健之所不及矣德果何偏乎夫健則自
能决矣說則自能和矣决而且和吾知其黨雖
===
將盡也猶慮其復蔓而去之必决心雖無比也
猶恐其若濡而决之必勇動焉直遂其去惡之
勢蓋有斷然而不可易者决孰尚焉然又藏其
用於自治之時從容不迫而求之必中其情是
可羣也而亦可以渙其羣何乖戾之有密其機
於有厲之際順適自如而制之必得其要非無
異也而不以立其異何繆妄之有若然則其和
之善又有以成夫决之所用矣德又何偏乎卦
有其德聖人舉而賛之厥旨深矣大抵君子小
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 二十九
punctuated: 純陽之性，惕厲常存於一心，而有以自強；妙天德之全，志氣常伸於萬物，而無所係累。靜焉專一，其惡惡之心，蓋有確乎而不可拔者，健孰加焉？然又襟度寛平，坦然樂易而可親。不怒而威，則威不在於猛矣，吾何為而壯吾之煩？氣象優裕，怡然温厚而可接。不惡而嚴，則嚴不在於暴矣，吾何為而厲吾之色？若然，則其說之德又有以濟夫健之所不及矣，德果何偏乎？夫健則自能决矣，說則自能和矣。决而且和，吾知其黨雖將盡也，猶慮其復蔓，而去之必决；心雖無比也，猶恐其若濡，而决之必勇。動焉直遂，其去惡之勢，蓋有斷然而不可易者，决孰尚焉？然又藏其用於自治之時，從容不迫，而求之必中其情。是可羣也，而亦可以渙其羣，何乖戾之有？密其機於有厲之際，順適自如，而制之必得其要。非無異也，而不以立其異，何繆妄之有？若然，則其和之善又有以成夫决之所用矣，德又何偏乎？卦有其德，聖人舉而賛之，厥旨深矣。大抵君子小
translation_en:
…the nature of pure yang: vigilance and apprehension remain constantly in his heart, enabling him to strengthen himself. He wondrously embodies the fullness of Heaven’s virtue; his resolve and vital spirit extend constantly among the myriad things, without entanglement or encumbrance. In stillness he is single-minded: his hatred of evil is firm and ineradicable. What could surpass such vigor? Yet his disposition is broad and even, composed, cheerful, easygoing, and approachable. He inspires awe without anger, so his awesomeness does not reside in fierceness. Why should I intensify my vexation [?]? His bearing is poised and generous, pleasantly warm and congenial. He is stern without being harsh, so his sternness does not reside in violence. Why should I make my countenance severe? Thus his virtue of joy also remedies what vigor alone cannot accomplish. How, then, could his virtue be one-sided?

Vigor naturally enables resolution; joy naturally enables harmony. With resolution joined to harmony, I know that although their faction is nearly exhausted, he still fears that it may spread again, and therefore must be resolute in removing it. Although his heart has no partisan attachments, he still fears that it may falter, and therefore must be courageous in making the break. In movement he proceeds directly: his momentum in removing evil is decisive and unalterable. What could surpass such resolution? Yet while putting himself in order, he conceals the exercise of his power; unhurried and unpressed, he investigates them so as unfailingly to ascertain their true circumstances. They can form a group, yet their group can also be dispersed. What perversity is there in this? At a time of danger, he keeps his plans secret, acting with natural ease and ensuring that his measures to control them grasp the essential point. It is not that there are no differences, but he does not thereby insist upon his difference. What error or recklessness is there in this? Thus the excellence of his harmony also brings the exercise of resolution to fulfillment. How, again, could his virtue be one-sided?

The hexagram possesses these virtues, and the Sage brings them forward and praises them. Profound indeed is his meaning! Generally speaking, the gentleman and the petty…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
人勢不兩立然以正去邪宜無不勝之理但君
子之待夫小人也常恕而小人之伺夫君子者
甚密一或不謹鮮不及矣此聖人於陰陽消長
之間每致其意焉而不苟也噫有是責而當是
事者其亦知所慎也哉
是故變化云為吉事有祥象事知器占事
知來天地設位聖人成能人謀鬼謀百
姓與能
丘養浩
===
同考試官教諭沈 批 此題上言畫前之易正是天地
之能處聖人作易乃所以成其能耳場中作者類多漫說若不相
關獨此篇發揮明白是宜錄出
同考試官教諭杜 批 聖人成能處必如此說方與
上文相應蓋嘗用心於易者
考試官訓導夏 批 理精詞到邃於易學者也
考試官訓導閔 批 得潔靜精微之旨
造化之易妙夫用聖人之易顯其用蓋易之未
作而其理已見於造化矣聖人著之易以示人
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 三十
punctuated:
人勢不兩立，然以正去邪，宜無不勝之理。但君子之待夫小人也常恕，而小人之伺夫君子者甚密，一或不謹，鮮不及矣。此聖人於陰陽消長之間，每致其意焉而不苟也。噫！有是責而當是事者，其亦知所慎也哉！
是故變化云為，吉事有祥；象事知器，占事知來。天地設位，聖人成能；人謀鬼謀，百姓與能。
丘養浩
同考試官教諭沈批：此題上言畫前之易，正是天地之能處，聖人作易乃所以成其能耳。場中作者類多漫說，若不相關，獨此篇發揮明白，是宜錄出。
同考試官教諭杜批：聖人成能處，必如此說，方與上文相應，蓋嘗用心於易者。
考試官訓導夏批：理精詞到，邃於易學者也。
考試官訓導閔批：得潔靜精微之旨。
造化之易妙夫用，聖人之易顯其用。蓋易之未作，而其理已見於造化矣。聖人著之易以示人
translation_en:
…and petty men cannot coexist in positions of power. Yet when uprightness is used to remove evil, there should be no reason why it cannot prevail. However, the gentleman always treats petty men with forbearance, while petty men watch the gentleman exceedingly closely. If he is careless even once, he will seldom escape their reach. This is why the sage always attends carefully to the waxing and waning of yin and yang, never treating it casually. Ah! Those who bear this responsibility and confront such affairs should surely know where caution is required!
“Thus, amid changes and transformations, speech and action, auspicious affairs have their omens. By representing affairs through images, one understands implements; by divining about affairs, one knows what is to come. Heaven and Earth establish their positions, and the sage brings their capacities to fulfillment. Counsel is sought from men and from spirits, and the common people share in these capacities.”
Qiu Yanghao
Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, an Instructor: The opening of this topic speaks of the Changes before the hexagram lines were drawn: this is precisely where the capacities of Heaven and Earth reside. The sage’s creation of the Book of Changes was simply the means of bringing those capacities to fulfillment. Most candidates in the examination hall discussed the matter vaguely, as though the two were unrelated. This essay alone expounds it clearly and therefore deserves to be included in the record.
Comment by Associate Examiner Du, an Instructor: The passage about the sage bringing these capacities to fulfillment must be explained in this way if it is to correspond to the preceding text. The author has evidently devoted thought to the Book of Changes.
Comment by Examiner Xia, an Assistant Instructor: His reasoning is refined and his language fully adequate: he is deeply versed in the study of the Book of Changes.
Comment by Examiner Min, an Assistant Instructor: He has grasped the purport of purity and stillness, subtlety and refinement.
The Changes inherent in creation are wondrous in their operation; the sage’s Book of Changes makes that operation manifest. For before the Book of Changes was composed, its principles were already evident in creation. The sage set them down in the Book of Changes to show people…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
其用不有以顯於天下哉大傳論乾坤而推言
及此蓋謂乾坤之用固皆本於健順然亦於造
化之理有足徵焉者以其理之顯者言之剛柔
相推一變一化而消長之機以寓動靜相感或
云或爲而得失之象以明是非其顯而易見者
乎以其理之微者言之福之將至事雖未成而
其兆爲之先見善之將来迹雖未著而其幾爲
之先萌是非其微而難明者乎變化云爲有象
可擬也以之而象夫事考迹以觀其變執古以
===
御乎今則其理之一定而不可易者已默藏於
吾心矣吉事有祥有理可推也以之而占夫事
探賾以索其隱由微以察其著則理之將來而
不可測者蓋已昭晣於吾目矣夫造化自然之
易如此苟非聖人作易何以顯其用乎是故輕
清成象者天也穹然而位于上重濁成形者地
也隤然而位于下天地之間但能示人以顯微
之理而已而亦不能以告人也聖人作易立其
象而制乎變則有以研乎天下之幾象變所示
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 三十一
punctuated: 其用不有以顯於天下哉？大傳論乾坤而推言及此，蓋謂乾坤之用固皆本於健順，然亦於造化之理有足徵焉者。以其理之顯者言之，剛柔相推，一變一化，而消長之機以寓；動靜相感，或云或爲，而得失之象以明。是非其顯而易見者乎？以其理之微者言之，福之將至，事雖未成，而其兆爲之先見；善之將来，迹雖未著，而其幾爲之先萌。是非其微而難明者乎？變化云爲，有象可擬也。以之而象夫事，考迹以觀其變，執古以御乎今，則其理之一定而不可易者，已默藏於吾心矣。吉事有祥，有理可推也。以之而占夫事，探賾以索其隱，由微以察其著，則理之將來而不可測者，蓋已昭晣於吾目矣。夫造化自然之易如此，苟非聖人作易，何以顯其用乎？是故輕清成象者，天也，穹然而位于上；重濁成形者，地也，隤然而位于下。天地之間，但能示人以顯微之理而已，而亦不能以告人也。聖人作易，立其象而制乎變，則有以研乎天下之幾。象變所示
translation_en:
…would its operation not thereby be made manifest throughout the world? The Great Commentary discusses Qian and Kun and extends its argument to this point. It means that the operation of Qian and Kun is indeed rooted in strength and compliance, yet there is also ample evidence for it in the principles of creation and transformation. Speaking of what is manifest in these principles: the firm and yielding impel one another, changing and transforming, and therein lies the mechanism of waxing and waning; movement and stillness respond to one another, in speech or action, and thereby the images of gain and loss become clear. Are these not the manifest aspects, readily perceived? Speaking of what is subtle in these principles: when blessings are about to arrive, although the event has not yet come to fruition, its portents appear beforehand; when good is about to come, although its traces are not yet apparent, its incipient signs emerge beforehand. Are these not the subtle aspects, difficult to discern?

Changes and transformations, speech and action, have images through which they can be represented. By using these to represent affairs, examining traces to observe their changes, and grasping antiquity to govern the present, the principles that are fixed and unalterable are already silently lodged within my mind. Auspicious events have favorable omens, and there are principles from which inferences can be drawn. By using these to divine affairs, probing complexities to seek out what is hidden, and proceeding from the subtle to discern what becomes manifest, the future workings of principle, otherwise unfathomable, are already clear before my eyes.

Such are the spontaneous changes of creation and transformation. Had the sages not composed the Book of Changes, how could its operation have been made manifest? Thus, what is light and clear and takes on images is Heaven, vaulted above; what is heavy and turbid and takes on form is Earth, settled below. Heaven and Earth can only display to people the principles of the manifest and the subtle; they cannot explain them to people. The sages composed the Book of Changes, establishing its images and regulating changes, thereby providing a means to investigate the incipient workings of all under Heaven. What the images and changes reveal…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
皆天地之能也繫其辭而定夫占則有以極天
下之深辭占所示亦天地之能也不皆有賴於
聖人而成哉由是明則有人也而謀之以决其
疑幽則有鬼也而謀之以致其用吾見百姓之
愚其疑者固因之以决而能知夫趨避之方其
怠者亦因之以勉而有得於鼓舞之妙豈不有
以與其能哉是則天地之易賴聖人以顯而聖
人之易本天地以作此天地無全功而聖人所
以能成位乎兩間也歟抑又論之易理固散見
===
于天地而具于書然近取諸身本無不備但百
姓日用而不知耳乾坤雖極天下之健順亦局
於所稟而不能以會其全此上文所以論其能
事而作易之功必以歸之聖人也然則易非啓
天地之秘而發聖人之蘊者邪學者欲希賢希
聖而希天必本於易而反身之功亦自有不可
缺者夫
書
一日二日萬幾
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 二十二
punctuated:
皆天地之能也。繫其辭而定夫占，則有以極天下之深；辭占所示，亦天地之能也。不皆有賴於聖人而成哉？由是，明則有人也，而謀之以决其疑；幽則有鬼也，而謀之以致其用。吾見百姓之愚，其疑者固因之以决，而能知夫趨避之方；其怠者亦因之以勉，而有得於鼓舞之妙。豈不有以與其能哉？是則天地之易賴聖人以顯，而聖人之易本天地以作，此天地無全功，而聖人所以能成位乎兩間也歟？抑又論之，易理固散見于天地而具于書，然近取諸身，本無不備，但百姓日用而不知耳。乾坤雖極天下之健順，亦局於所稟，而不能以會其全。此上文所以論其能事，而作易之功必以歸之聖人也。然則易非啓天地之秘，而發聖人之蘊者邪？學者欲希賢、希聖而希天，必本於易，而反身之功亦自有不可缺者夫！

書
一日二日萬幾
translation_en:
…all are the capacities of Heaven and Earth. By appending the statements and determining the prognostications, the sage provided a means to fathom the deepest things under Heaven. What the statements and prognostications reveal are likewise the capacities of Heaven and Earth. Do these not all depend upon the sage for their fulfillment? Thus, in the visible realm there are human beings, whom one consults to resolve doubts; in the unseen realm there are spirits, whom one consults to bring their efficacy into operation. I observe that even among the ignorant common people, those in doubt rely upon this to reach decisions and learn what to pursue and what to avoid; the indolent likewise gain encouragement through it and experience its marvelous power to inspire action. Does this not enable them to participate in those capacities? Thus the Changes of Heaven and Earth depend upon the sage to become manifest, while the sage’s Book of Changes was composed on the basis of Heaven and Earth. Is this not why Heaven and Earth cannot accomplish the whole work alone, and why the sage can establish his place between them?

To discuss this further: the principles of the Changes are indeed manifest throughout Heaven and Earth and fully contained in the book. Yet if we look close at hand, within ourselves, there is inherently nothing lacking; it is merely that the common people make use of them daily without knowing it. Although Qian and Kun exemplify the utmost vigor and compliance under Heaven, they too are confined to their respective endowments and cannot bring the whole together. This is why the preceding passage discusses their capacities, yet necessarily attributes the achievement of composing the Book of Changes to the sage. Does not the Book of Changes, then, disclose the secrets of Heaven and Earth and reveal what lies within the sage? Those who study, aspiring to become worthies, sages, and ultimately to accord with Heaven, must take the Changes as their foundation; and the work of examining themselves is likewise indispensable!

Book of Documents
“In one day or two days, there are ten thousand incipient affairs.”

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
林應驄
同考試官訓導徐批幾之一字皐陶欲舜儆
戒之意正在於此場中作者多畧而不講間有說者又冗
贅可厭此篇理明詞暢深得人臣勸戒之體故録之以式後學
同考試官教諭吴批幾字意義最難模寫是
篇鋪叙明白而詞氣渾厚真有得於皐陶進戒之旨者是宜録出
考試官訓導夏批皐陶告舜之意發明殆盡佳作也
考試官訓導閔批講能發題意黜浮臆說者可
以讀矣
===
當至淺之時有至衆之務大臣告君之深意也
蓋一日二日時之至淺者也而幾務之來且至
萬焉人君其可一日而不謹哉昔皐陶陳知人
之謨于舜至此謂夫君人者必勤儉率諸侯而
兢業以自處者何哉誠以自朝至中自中至昃
時之所經僅一日之期耳晷刻之推移何有於
浹旬之久耶是固至近矣明而既晦晦而復明
日之所歷斯二日而已耳辰候之代謝何有乎
彌月之多耶是亦至淺矣夫時止一日宜無足
banxin: 福建鄉試録三十三
punctuated:
林應驄。

同考試官訓導徐批：幾之一字，皐陶欲舜儆戒之意正在於此。場中作者多畧而不講，間有說者，又冗贅可厭。此篇理明詞暢，深得人臣勸戒之體，故録之以式後學。

同考試官教諭吴批：幾字意義最難模寫，是篇鋪叙明白，而詞氣渾厚，真有得於皐陶進戒之旨者，是宜録出。

考試官訓導夏批：皐陶告舜之意，發明殆盡，佳作也。

考試官訓導閔批：講能發題意，黜浮臆說者，可以讀矣。

當至淺之時，有至衆之務，大臣告君之深意也。蓋一日二日，時之至淺者也，而幾務之來且至萬焉，人君其可一日而不謹哉？昔皐陶陳知人之謨于舜，至此謂夫君人者必勤儉率諸侯，而兢業以自處者，何哉？誠以自朝至中，自中至昃，時之所經僅一日之期耳，晷刻之推移，何有於浹旬之久耶？是固至近矣。明而既晦，晦而復明，日之所歷斯二日而已耳，辰候之代謝，何有乎彌月之多耶？是亦至淺矣。夫時止一日，宜無足
translation_en:
Lin Yingcong.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor: The single word ji—the incipient developments in affairs—is precisely where Gao Yao’s intention to urge vigilance upon Shun lies. Most candidates in the examination passed over it without explanation; the few who did explain it were tediously verbose. This essay’s reasoning is clear and its language fluent. It thoroughly captures the proper manner in which a minister should counsel and admonish his ruler, and is therefore recorded as a model for later students.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: The meaning of the word ji is most difficult to convey. This essay expounds it clearly, with language of depth and vigor. It truly grasps the purport of Gao Yao’s admonition and deserves to be included in the record.

Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: It brings out almost exhaustively the meaning of Gao Yao’s counsel to Shun. An excellent composition.

Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: Its exposition brings out the meaning of the topic and rejects superficial conjectures. It merits reading.

Within the briefest span of time there are the most numerous affairs: this is the profound meaning of the great minister’s counsel to his ruler. One day or two days is a very short time, yet the incipient affairs that arise may number as many as ten thousand. Can a ruler go even one day without vigilance? Long ago, Gao Yao presented to Shun his counsel on discerning men’s abilities. At this point, why did he say that a ruler must lead the feudal lords through diligence and frugality, and conduct himself with reverent vigilance? Truly, from morning to noon, and from noon until the sun declines, the time elapsed amounts to only a single day. How could the passage of these hours and moments equal the length of a full ten days? This is indeed a very short interval. Light gives way to darkness, and darkness gives way to light again: the days that have passed amount to only two. How could this succession of times and periods equal the duration of a full month? This, too, is a very brief span. Now, when the time is only a single day, there should be nothing sufficient to…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
慮者然人主置身兆庶之上事幾之來盖動以
萬計而有常勤之務時止二日似無可患者然
人君聨属天下之大事幾之至盖將以萬計而
有必親之政乾綱總於一人而天下之政制之
在始所以煩淵衷勞宸斷者常循環而無窮政
柄歸於九五而天下之事爲之在豫所以宏廟
謨勤聖慮者常相續而不絶大而紀綱法度之
施四海之休戚繫焉苟毫髪幾微之不察則藏
於細者必形於大而或以貽患於天下必兢業
===
焉爲大於其細可也夫可以一日之近而偷安
乎小而條教號令之布生民之休戚存焉苟頃
刻謹畏之不存則隱於易者每至於難或以基
禍於邦家必兢業焉圖難於其易可也又可以
二日之淺而玩愒乎吁人主以一身居天下之
尊而不敢一日忽天下之務則君身克謹而羣
臣咸有所取法矣又何治功之不可成哉宜臯
陶以是而警之也嗟夫君至於舜至矣盡矣不
可以復加矣何有於逸欲而不兢業於心哉顧
banxin: 福建鄉試録 三十六
punctuated: 慮者，然人主置身兆庶之上，事幾之來，盖動以萬計，而有常勤之務。時止二日，似無可患者，然人君聨属天下之大，事幾之至，盖將以萬計，而有必親之政。乾綱總於一人，而天下之政，制之在始，所以煩淵衷、勞宸斷者，常循環而無窮；政柄歸於九五，而天下之事，爲之在豫，所以宏廟謨、勤聖慮者，常相續而不絶。大而紀綱法度之施，四海之休戚繫焉，苟毫髪幾微之不察，則藏於細者必形於大，而或以貽患於天下。必兢業焉，爲大於其細，可也。夫可以一日之近而偷安乎？小而條教號令之布，生民之休戚存焉，苟頃刻謹畏之不存，則隱於易者每至於難，或以基禍於邦家。必兢業焉，圖難於其易，可也。又可以二日之淺而玩愒乎？吁！人主以一身居天下之尊，而不敢一日忽天下之務，則君身克謹，而羣臣咸有所取法矣，又何治功之不可成哉？宜臯陶以是而警之也。嗟夫！君至於舜，至矣，盡矣，不可以復加矣，何有於逸欲而不兢業於心哉？顧
translation_en:
…cause for concern. Yet the ruler stands above the teeming multitude, and the critical matters that arise commonly number in the tens of thousands; thus there are duties requiring constant diligence. A span of only two days might seem to offer no cause for anxiety. Yet the ruler holds together the vast realm, and the critical matters that come before him will number in the tens of thousands; thus there are affairs of government he must attend to personally. Supreme authority is concentrated in one man, and the realm’s government must be ordered from the outset. Hence the matters that trouble his profound thoughts and tax his imperial judgment recur endlessly. The governing power rests with the sovereign, and the realm’s affairs must be attended to in advance. Hence the matters that call for far-reaching court deliberations and diligent imperial consideration follow one another without interruption.

In great matters, such as the implementation of governing principles, laws, and institutions, the well-being or suffering of all within the Four Seas is at stake. If the slightest incipient development escapes scrutiny, what lies concealed in small things will necessarily manifest itself in great ones and may bring calamity upon the realm. The ruler must be vigilant and diligent, attending to great matters while they are still small. How could he indulge in ease merely because a single day is so brief? In lesser matters, such as the promulgation of directives and commands, the well-being or suffering of the people is at stake. If caution and reverence lapse even for a moment, what lies hidden in easy matters often develops into difficulty and may lay the foundation for disaster in the state. The ruler must be vigilant and diligent, planning for difficulties while they are still easy. How, then, could he idle away his time merely because two days form so short a span?

Ah! If the ruler, occupying alone the most exalted position in the realm, dares not neglect its affairs for even a single day, then he will maintain due caution in his own conduct, and all his ministers will have an example to follow. What achievement in government could then remain beyond reach? It was fitting that Gao Yao should admonish him with these words. Alas! In Shun, rulership had reached its utmost perfection; nothing further could be added. How could he have harbored a desire for ease and pleasure, failing to remain vigilant and diligent at heart? Yet…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
皐陶陳謨必至於此者蓋有說也何者古之大
臣不以世之已治而忘儆戒之心不以君之既
聖而忘責難之意茲有虞之世所以為不可及
也嗚呼以舜為君而有臣如此天下安得而不
治乎
監于先王成憲其永無愆惟說式克欽承
旁招俊乂列于庶位王曰嗚呼說四海
之內咸仰朕德時乃風股肱惟人良臣
惟聖昔先正保衡作我先王乃曰予弗
===
克俾厥后惟堯舜其心愧耻若撻于市
一夫不獲則曰時予之辜佑我烈祖格
于皇天爾尚明保予罔俾阿衡專美有
商惟后非賢不乂惟賢非后不食其爾
克紹乃辟于先王永綏民說拜稽首曰
敢對揚天子之休命
陳騰鸞
同考試官訓導徐 批 高宗傅說交相責望與
所以自期待之意作者類能言之率繁蕪可厭此作文理
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 三十五
punctuated:
皐陶陳謨必至於此者，蓋有說也。何者？古之大臣不以世之已治而忘儆戒之心，不以君之既聖而忘責難之意，茲有虞之世所以為不可及也。嗚呼！以舜為君，而有臣如此，天下安得而不治乎？

監于先王成憲，其永無愆。惟說式克欽承，旁招俊乂，列于庶位。王曰：「嗚呼！說，四海之內咸仰朕德，時乃風。股肱惟人，良臣惟聖。昔先正保衡作我先王，乃曰：『予弗克俾厥后惟堯舜，其心愧耻若撻于市。』一夫不獲，則曰：『時予之辜。』佑我烈祖，格于皇天。爾尚明保予，罔俾阿衡專美有商。惟后非賢不乂，惟賢非后不食。其爾克紹乃辟于先王，永綏民。」說拜稽首曰：「敢對揚天子之休命。」

陳騰鸞

同考試官訓導徐批：高宗、傅說交相責望與所以自期待之意，作者類能言之，率繁蕪可厭。此作文理
translation_en:
…There was surely a reason why Gao Yao, in presenting his counsels, went this far. What was it? The great ministers of antiquity did not forget the need for vigilance and admonition merely because the realm was already well governed; nor did they forget their resolve to demand difficult accomplishments of their ruler merely because he was already a sage. This is why the age of Youyu was unsurpassable. Ah! With Shun as ruler and ministers such as these, how could All under Heaven fail to be well governed?

“Look to the established statutes of the former kings, and you will forever be without fault.” Yue reverently carried out these instructions, seeking out men of outstanding talent far and wide and placing them in the various offices. The king said: “Ah, Yue! All within the Four Seas look up to my virtue: this is the result of your guidance. As arms and legs make a complete person, so good ministers make a sage ruler. In former times, the former chief minister Baoheng assisted our former king. He said: ‘If I cannot make my sovereign a Yao or a Shun, I feel as ashamed at heart as if I had been flogged in the marketplace.’ If even one man failed to find his proper place, he said: ‘This is my fault.’ He assisted our illustrious ancestor, whose virtue reached August Heaven. May you wisely protect me, and not allow Aheng alone to enjoy glory in the house of Shang. Without worthy men, a sovereign cannot govern; without a sovereign, worthy men cannot receive their sustenance. May you enable your ruler to carry on the work of the former kings and bring enduring peace to the people.” Yue bowed and knocked his head to the ground, saying: “I venture to acknowledge and extol the Son of Heaven’s gracious command.”

Chen Tengluan.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor: Writers generally manage to express the expectations Gaozong and Fu Yue placed upon one another, and what each expected of himself, but their treatments are mostly tiresomely verbose and cluttered. The composition and reasoning of this essay…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
明淨且有照應取之以冠本房
同考試官教諭吳批長題貴簡明而厭冗雜
此作鋪叙嚴整得當時君臣相期自任之意允宜高薦
考試官訓導夏批明潔可觀蓋純於璧經者
考試官訓導閔批此作簡嚴必老學之士宜寘高選
觀有商之君臣重致相望之意而皆有以自任
焉蓋商之君臣莫聖於成湯伊尹也然高宗傅
說之交相告勉得不以此責望而復致自任也
哉昔傅說勉高宗進學及此謂夫吾君德雖造
===
於罔覺法必監于先王彼脩己治人先王成法
固歷萬世而無弊矣君必視以為準遵而行之
斯克永世而無過焉然君德苟至于無愆則說
用能敬承其意于以明揚俊民而列于庶位敷
求哲人而布于衆職以人事君德愈懋矣高宗
遜嘆之以為天下之大咸仰我德而無間焉者
實汝之風有以動之而致然也然欲慰天下之
望在汝盡輔聖之功蓋人不自成也必手足備
而後成君不自聖也必良臣輔而後聖昔伊尹
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 三十六
punctuated:
明淨，且有照應，取之以冠本房。

同考試官教諭吳批：長題貴簡明而厭冗雜，此作鋪叙嚴整，得當時君臣相期自任之意，允宜高薦。

考試官訓導夏批：明潔可觀，蓋純於璧經者。

考試官訓導閔批：此作簡嚴，必老學之士，宜寘高選。

觀有商之君臣重致相望之意，而皆有以自任焉。蓋商之君臣莫聖於成湯、伊尹也，然高宗、傅說之交相告勉，得不以此責望而復致自任也哉？昔傅說勉高宗進學，及此謂夫吾君德雖造於罔覺，法必監于先王。彼脩己治人，先王成法固歷萬世而無弊矣。君必視以為準，遵而行之，斯克永世而無過焉。然君德苟至于無愆，則說用能敬承其意，于以明揚俊民而列于庶位，敷求哲人而布于衆職，以人事君，德愈懋矣。高宗遜嘆之，以為天下之大，咸仰我德而無間焉者，實汝之風有以動之而致然也。然欲慰天下之望，在汝盡輔聖之功。蓋人不自成也，必手足備而後成；君不自聖也，必良臣輔而後聖。昔伊尹
translation_en:
…clear and lucid, with its parts responding to one another. I select it to head the papers in this examination section.

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: A long topic calls for concision and clarity and admits no tedious clutter. This composition develops its argument with rigor and order, capturing the mutual expectations and personal responsibilities of the ruler and minister of that time. It certainly deserves a high recommendation.

Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor, comments: Clear, clean, and well worth reading. Its author is evidently thoroughly versed in the classic [?].

Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor, comments: This composition is concise and rigorous. Its author must be a seasoned scholar and should be placed among the highest selections.

Observe how the ruler and minister of Shang earnestly expressed their mutual expectations, each taking responsibility upon himself. Among the rulers and ministers of Shang, none surpassed Cheng Tang and Yi Yin in sageliness. Yet when Gaozong and Fu Yue admonished and encouraged one another, could they fail to hold one another to this standard and renew their own commitments? Formerly, when Fu Yue urged Gaozong to advance in learning, he reached this point and said: “Although my lord’s virtue has attained a state in which its workings are unconscious, in taking models he must look to the former kings. Their established methods for cultivating oneself and governing others could endure ten thousand generations without defect. My lord must regard them as his standard and follow them in practice; only thus can he remain free from error forever. If my lord’s virtue indeed becomes faultless, then I, Yue, can reverently carry out his intentions, openly promoting outstanding men and placing them in the various posts, searching widely for wise men and assigning them to the many offices. By serving my lord through the provision of worthy men, I shall help his virtue flourish still further.”

Gaozong responded with humble admiration, saying: “That all throughout the vast realm look up to my virtue without dissent is truly because your influence has moved them and brought this about. Yet to satisfy the expectations of all under Heaven, you must fulfill your work of assisting your ruler to become a sage. A person does not become complete by himself: only with hands and feet fully supplied is he complete. A ruler does not become a sage by himself: only with the assistance of worthy ministers does he become a sage. Formerly, Yi Yin…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
保衡作我先王以為堯舜其君予之心也君不
堯舜則有愧于心若撻之于市焉堯舜其民予
之志也一民不獲則自咎于身若納之溝中焉
故能篤棐左右以佑我先王懋著厥功以格于
上帝爾當明以保我亦致我而為烈祖可也可
使尹而獨美於商乎且君非賢臣寧虛其位而
已不與共治也臣非賢君寧晦吾迹而已不與
共食也爾其克紹乃辟于先王不殊於尹之事
君焉綏安兆民於永久不異於尹之治民焉說
===
於是拜稽首而言曰克紹乃辟乃致君之休命
也永綏兆民乃澤民之美命也吾必對之於已
而揚之於衆務使君為堯舜而後吾之責始塞
耳務俾民為唐虞而後吾之心始慊耳噫君臣
交相責望既欲以成湯伊尹為準的而又皆自
任之無嫌所謂上下交而德業成豈非有商之
極盛乎考之高宗之於傅說始得之其事異繼
命之其任重終望之其意深而說也卒能輔導
高宗進學脩德而無愧於成湯使高宗為商之
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 三十七
punctuated:
保衡作我先王，以為堯舜。其君，予之心也；君不堯舜，則有愧于心，若撻之于市焉。堯舜其民，予之志也；一民不獲，則自咎于身，若納之溝中焉。故能篤棐左右，以佑我先王，懋著厥功，以格于上帝。爾當明以保我，亦致我而為烈祖可也。可使尹而獨美於商乎？且君非賢臣，寧虛其位而已，不與共治也；臣非賢君，寧晦吾迹而已，不與共食也。爾其克紹乃辟于先王，不殊於尹之事君焉；綏安兆民於永久，不異於尹之治民焉。
說於是拜稽首而言曰：「克紹乃辟，乃致君之休命也；永綏兆民，乃澤民之美命也。吾必對之於已，而揚之於衆，務使君為堯舜，而後吾之責始塞耳；務俾民為唐虞，而後吾之心始慊耳。」
噫！君臣交相責望，既欲以成湯、伊尹為準的，而又皆自任之無嫌。所謂上下交而德業成，豈非有商之極盛乎？考之高宗之於傅說，始得之，其事異；繼命之，其任重；終望之，其意深。而說也卒能輔導高宗進學脩德，而無愧於成湯，使高宗為商之
translation_en:
…the Guardian (Baoheng) raised our former king to the stature of Yao and Shun. ‘To make my ruler a Yao or a Shun is my heartfelt purpose. If my ruler falls short of Yao and Shun, I feel shame in my heart, as though I were being flogged in the marketplace. To make his people like the people of Yao and Shun is my resolve. If even one person fails to find his proper place, I blame myself, as though I had thrust him into a ditch.’ Thus he could give devoted assistance at the king’s side and support our former king, gloriously manifesting his achievements so that they reached the Lord on High. You should exercise your discernment to safeguard me and likewise bring me to equal our illustrious ancestor. Can we allow Yi Yin alone to enjoy such distinction in Shang? Moreover, unless a minister is worthy, a ruler would rather leave his post vacant than share government with him; unless a ruler is worthy, a minister would rather remain in obscurity than share in his sustenance. You should enable your sovereign to carry on the legacy of the former king, just as Yin served his ruler; bring lasting peace to the myriad people, just as Yin governed the people.
Yue thereupon bowed, touching his head to the ground, and said: ‘To enable your sovereign to carry on that legacy is an auspicious command to bring the ruler to perfection; to bring lasting peace to the myriad people is a splendid command to bestow blessings upon them. I shall answer it in my own person and proclaim it before the multitude. I must make my ruler a Yao or a Shun before my responsibility can be fulfilled; I must make the people like those of Tang and Yu before my heart can be satisfied.’
Ah! Ruler and minister held one another to high expectations. They wished to take Cheng Tang and Yi Yin as their standards, and both unhesitatingly assumed these responsibilities themselves. This is what is meant by those above and below being in communion, so that virtue and achievement are perfected. Was this not the height of Shang’s flourishing? Examining Gaozong’s relationship with Fu Yue: when he first obtained his services, the circumstances were extraordinary; when he subsequently charged him with his duties, the responsibilities were weighty; and in the expectations he finally expressed, his intentions were profound. Yue ultimately succeeded in helping and guiding Gaozong to advance his learning and cultivate his virtue, so that he need feel no shame before Cheng Tang, making Gaozong one of Shang’s…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
令主說亦為商之賢佐明君賢相兩無愧焉赫
赫厥聲濯濯厥靈之盛有由然矣後世得其書
讀之猶可想見於數千載之上
詩
眾維魚矣旐維旟矣
朱溓
同考試官教諭吳批此題塲中士子多記舊
文千篇一律無可去取晚得此卷會傳意成文而詞足以發
之當是作手
===
同考試官學正胡批理明詞暢一結尤出人意
表是可錄也已
考試官訓導夏批寫出牧人之夢宛然在目可
以占子之善說詩矣
考試官訓導閔批語新而意盡可取
盛時牧人之夢隨感而皆有異也夫夢人而為
魚夢旐而為旟是固皆出於意象之外者也牧
人之夢有是焉夫豈徒然也哉無羊之詩牧事
有成而作也至此若曰當牧事有成之日正牧
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 三十八 仁
punctuated:
令主，說亦為商之賢佐，明君賢相，兩無愧焉。赫赫厥聲，濯濯厥靈之盛，有由然矣。後世得其書讀之，猶可想見於數千載之上。

詩
眾維魚矣，旐維旟矣。
朱溓

同考試官教諭吳批：此題塲中士子多記舊文，千篇一律，無可去取。晚得此卷，會傳意成文，而詞足以發之，當是作手。

同考試官學正胡批：理明詞暢，一結尤出人意表，是可錄也已。

考試官訓導夏批：寫出牧人之夢，宛然在目，可以占子之善說詩矣。

考試官訓導閔批：語新而意盡，可取。

盛時牧人之夢，隨感而皆有異也。夫夢人而為魚，夢旐而為旟，是固皆出於意象之外者也。牧人之夢有是焉，夫豈徒然也哉？《無羊》之詩，牧事有成而作也。至此若曰：當牧事有成之日，正牧
translation_en:
…an excellent ruler of Shang, while Yue likewise became a worthy minister of Shang: neither fell short as an enlightened ruler and a worthy chief minister. There was thus a reason for the grandeur of their “resplendent renown and brilliant spiritual power.” Later generations, obtaining and reading this text, can still envision them across several thousand years.

Book of Odes
“The multitudes were fish; the tortoise-and-snake banners were falcon banners.”
Zhu Lian 朱溓

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: On this topic, many candidates in the examination hall reproduced old compositions from memory. A thousand essays followed a single pattern, leaving no basis for accepting one and rejecting another. Late in the process I obtained this script. It grasps the meaning of the commentary and fashions it into an essay, with language adequate to express it. Its author must be an accomplished writer.

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: The reasoning is clear and the language fluent. The conclusion, especially, surpasses expectations. This certainly merits selection.

Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: You portray the herdsmen’s dream so vividly that it seems to stand before our eyes. From this one can discern your skill in expounding the Odes.

Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: The language is fresh and the meaning fully expressed. It merits acceptance.

In a flourishing age, the herdsmen’s dreams contain extraordinary things in response to what moves them. To dream of people becoming fish, and of tortoise-and-snake banners becoming falcon banners—these surely lie beyond ordinary imagining. Such things occur in the herdsmen’s dreams: could they possibly be without significance? The ode “No Sheep” (Wu yang) was composed when the work of tending livestock had achieved success. At this point it seems to say: when the work of tending livestock had achieved success, it was precisely when the herdsmen…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
人有暇之時而爲夢也果何如哉故靈萬物而
獨秀於兩間人也而魚則鱗族之微耳人與魚
豈其同類者哉牧人夢與天地相爲流通夢人
維人固常也而非異矣然而示諸恍惚之間則
人非人也而爲魚焉飾以冠屨者乃鬐鬣其形
華以襟裾者皆鱗介其属儀容之楚楚也其遂
波濤而上下者乎咲言之啞啞也其游江湖而
煦濡者乎而族類之蕃育固有潑潑以適者矣
人與物有定形而夢之所及何嘗有定形哉具
===
===
四游而特建於郊野者旐也而旟則州里所建
焉旐與旟豈其同用者哉牧人夢與陰陽相爲
會合夢旐維旐亦常也而非異矣然而見諸彷
彿之際則旐非旐也而爲旟焉畫爲龜蛇者乃
鳥隼其章象著玄武者寔朱雀其制甲而爲息
伏也其乘風雲而摶擊者乎跗而為蜿蜒也其
凌霄漢而翱翔者乎而州里之彩繪固有翩翩
以舉者矣旐與旟有定制也而夢之所及何嘗
有定制哉吁夢雖兆於牧人之微而應則及乎
banxin: 福建鄉試録 三十九
punctuated:
人有暇之時，而爲夢也，果何如哉？故靈萬物而獨秀於兩間，人也；而魚則鱗族之微耳。人與魚，豈其同類者哉？牧人夢與天地相爲流通，夢人維人，固常也，而非異矣。然而示諸恍惚之間，則人非人也，而爲魚焉。飾以冠屨者，乃鬐鬣其形；華以襟裾者，皆鱗介其属。儀容之楚楚也，其遂波濤而上下者乎？咲言之啞啞也，其游江湖而煦濡者乎？而族類之蕃育，固有潑潑以適者矣。人與物有定形，而夢之所及，何嘗有定形哉？
具四游而特建於郊野者，旐也；而旟則州里所建焉。旐與旟，豈其同用者哉？牧人夢與陰陽相爲會合，夢旐維旐，亦常也，而非異矣。然而見諸彷彿之際，則旐非旐也，而爲旟焉。畫爲龜蛇者，乃鳥隼其章；象著玄武者，寔朱雀其制。甲而爲息伏也，其乘風雲而摶擊者乎？跗而為蜿蜒也，其凌霄漢而翱翔者乎？而州里之彩繪，固有翩翩以舉者矣。旐與旟有定制也，而夢之所及，何嘗有定制哉？吁！夢雖兆於牧人之微，而應則及乎
translation_en:
…a time when the herdsmen were at leisure. What, then, were their dreams like? It is humankind that possesses the greatest spiritual intelligence among all creatures and stands preeminent between Heaven and Earth; fish are merely lowly members of the scaly tribe. How could humans and fish belong to the same kind? The herdsmen’s dreams communicated with Heaven and Earth. To dream of people simply as people would certainly be ordinary, nothing strange. Yet in the indistinct visions presented to them, people were no longer people, but fish. Those adorned with caps and shoes took on forms with fins and bristling dorsal spines; those resplendent in robes all belonged to the scaly kind. Those once so neat in bearing and appearance—were they now rising and falling with the waves? Those once laughing and talking merrily—were they now swimming through rivers and lakes, moistening one another? Their kind multiplied, darting about in carefree contentment. Humans and other creatures have fixed forms, but when has the realm of dreams ever had fixed forms?
The banner furnished with four streamers and erected specifically in the suburban countryside is the zhao, bearing a tortoise and snake; the yu, bearing a falcon, is erected in districts and villages. How could the zhao and yu have the same use? The herdsmen’s dreams accorded with yin and yang. To dream of a zhao simply as a zhao would likewise be ordinary, nothing strange. Yet in those hazy visions, the zhao was no longer a zhao, but a yu. What had been painted as tortoises and snakes now bore the emblems of birds and falcons; what had displayed the Dark Warrior now took the form of the Vermilion Bird. Those that rested concealed within their shells—were they now riding wind and cloud to strike their prey? Those that crept and wound along on their feet [?]—were they now soaring through the lofty heavens? The painted banners of the districts and villages fluttered as they rose. The zhao and yu have fixed designs, but when has the realm of dreams ever had fixed designs? Ah! Though the dream’s omen appeared to lowly herdsmen, its fulfillment extended to…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
天下之大太卜占之而推為富庶之祥宜矣抑
考厲王暴虐周室板蕩民靡有黎具禍以燼而
生靈之淪斁將盡矣降此蟊賊稼穡卒痒而中
國之具贅卒荒矣而宣王承其餘烈遇災知懼
側身脩行天下喜於王化復行百姓見憂故民
困甦而流離集天意回而國事殷富庶之祥兆
於牧人之夢良亦不偶是知人事脩於下則和
氣應於上雖樵童牧竪亦能獻吉夢以增中興
之勝槩讀是詩者宜併合雲漢之章而觀之
===
作之屏之其菑其翳脩之平之其灌其栵
啓之辟之其檉其椐攘之剔之其檿其
柘
謝寬
同考試官教諭吳批題本平淡作者類急章
句所窘典雅舂容僅見此篇宜錄之以式後學
同考試官學正胡批塲中作此題者多冗襍
塵腐令人厭觀整潔如此篇者絕少故用錄之
考試官訓導夏批太王一時闢國氣象摹寫
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 四十
punctuated:
天下之大，太卜占之而推為富庶之祥，宜矣。抑考厲王暴虐，周室板蕩，民靡有黎，具禍以燼，而生靈之淪斁將盡矣。降此蟊賊，稼穡卒痒，而中國之具贅卒荒矣。而宣王承其餘烈，遇災知懼，側身脩行，天下喜於王化復行，百姓見憂，故民困甦而流離集，天意回而國事殷。富庶之祥兆於牧人之夢，良亦不偶。是知人事脩於下，則和氣應於上，雖樵童牧竪，亦能獻吉夢以增中興之勝槩。讀是詩者，宜併合《雲漢》之章而觀之。

作之屏之，其菑其翳；脩之平之，其灌其栵；啓之辟之，其檉其椐；攘之剔之，其檿其柘。

謝寬

同考試官教諭吳批：題本平淡，作者類急章句所窘，典雅舂容，僅見此篇，宜錄之以式後學。

同考試官學正胡批：塲中作此題者，多冗襍塵腐，令人厭觀。整潔如此篇者絕少，故用錄之。

考試官訓導夏批：太王一時闢國氣象，摹寫
translation_en:
…the vast realm under Heaven. It was fitting that the Grand Diviner should interpret this as an auspicious sign of wealth and a flourishing population. Consider, however, King Li’s brutality: the royal house of Zhou was shaken by disorder; none of the people remained secure, and all suffered calamity until they were reduced to ashes. The living were sinking into ruin and approaching extinction. These crop-devouring pests descended, and all the crops were afflicted; the central lands were altogether burdened with affliction and ultimately laid waste [?]. King Xuan inherited the aftermath of these evils. Confronted with calamity, he knew fear, humbled himself, and cultivated his conduct. All under Heaven rejoiced that royal moral transformation was again taking effect and that the common people were objects of royal concern. Thus the people recovered from their distress, and the displaced gathered again; Heaven’s disposition turned favorable, and the affairs of state flourished. That signs of wealth and a flourishing population appeared in the herdsmen’s dreams was surely no coincidence. From this we know that when human affairs are put in order below, harmonious energies respond above. Even woodcutting boys and young herdsmen can offer auspicious dreams that enhance the splendid achievements of a dynastic restoration. Readers of this poem should consider it together with the ode “The Milky Way” (Yunhan).

They cut and cleared them—the standing dead trees and the fallen timber; they trimmed and leveled them—the shrubs and thickets; they opened and cleared the ground—the tamarisks and ju trees; they removed and pruned them—the wild mulberries and zhe trees.

Xie Kuan

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: The topic itself is plain. Writers generally seem constrained by their anxious attention to phrasing [?]. Only this piece displays classical elegance and measured ease. It should be recorded as a model for later students.

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, School Director: Among those who addressed this topic in the examination hall, many produced prolix, miscellaneous, stale compositions that were tiresome to read. Pieces as orderly and clean as this were exceedingly rare; therefore we have selected it for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: The grandeur of King Tai’s founding of his state at that time is depicted…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
殆盡傑作也可敬可敬
考試官訓導閔批筆健語莊是繩尺文字可取
隨物性而致開闢之功此賢君立國然也蓋人
事脩而後天意可承也周人開國而漸見於林
木之治如此王業其嗣而興乎昔詩人叙太王
太伯王季之德至此謂夫我太王當遷岐定居
之始正隨山刋木之時其所以開闢者何如哉
故夫枯木宜去其茂而密者未易以盡除也則
因其勢而治焉拔之使起屏之使去并其根株
===
條幹而盡棄者皆夫生意已絶爲菑與翳也是
寧有穢襍而復存者哉脩之使通平之使理求
其疎密直正之皆宜者乃其叢列而生爲灌與
栵也是復有參錯而不治者哉夫於菑翳灌栵
而皆致力焉則山林之險僻者自是有可通之
道彼徂矣岐其駸駸乎人物之會乎不特此也
凡木可無其美而材者不可以不畜也則順其
宜而治之故恐其爲蓊鬱也啓闢之以除其類
不使之駢附而起者則檉也而檉之外又有椐
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 四十一
punctuated:
殆盡，傑作也，可敬可敬！

考試官訓導閔批：筆健語莊，是繩尺文字，可取。

隨物性而致開闢之功，此賢君立國然也。蓋人事脩而後天意可承也。周人開國，而漸見於林木之治如此，王業其嗣而興乎？昔詩人叙太王、太伯、王季之德，至此謂夫我太王當遷岐定居之始，正隨山刋木之時，其所以開闢者何如哉？故夫枯木宜去，其茂而密者未易以盡除也，則因其勢而治焉。拔之使起，屏之使去，并其根株條幹而盡棄者，皆夫生意已絶，爲菑與翳也。是寧有穢襍而復存者哉？脩之使通，平之使理，求其疎密直正之皆宜者，乃其叢列而生，爲灌與栵也。是復有參錯而不治者哉？夫於菑、翳、灌、栵而皆致力焉，則山林之險僻者，自是有可通之道。彼徂矣岐，其駸駸乎人物之會乎？不特此也，凡木可無，其美而材者不可以不畜也，則順其宜而治之。故恐其爲蓊鬱也，啓闢之以除其類，不使之駢附而起者，則檉也，而檉之外又有椐。
translation_en:
…almost exhaustively. A masterful composition—admirable, admirable!

Examiner Min, an Assistant Instructor, comments: The writing is vigorous and the language dignified. This composition supplies a standard to follow and merits selection.

To accomplish the opening of the land by following the nature of things: thus does a worthy ruler establish his state [?]. For only after human affairs have been put in order can Heaven’s intent be received and fulfilled. When the people of Zhou founded their state, its beginnings gradually became evident in their management of the woodland in this way. Would not the royal enterprise then arise through their successors? In recounting the virtues of King Tai, Taibo, and Wang Ji, the poet reaches this point and speaks of our King Tai at the beginning of his migration to Qi and settlement there. This was precisely the time for following the hills and cutting down trees. How, then, did he open up the land?

Dead trees ought to be removed, but where growth was luxuriant and dense, it was not easy to clear everything away. He therefore managed it according to its condition. Those he pulled up to uproot them and cleared away to remove them, discarding roots, stumps, branches, and trunks alike, were trees whose vitality had already ceased—the standing deadwood and fallen trees. Could any foul and tangled growth still have remained? Those he trimmed to open passages and leveled to bring order, seeking the proper spacing and straightness of growth, were the shrubs and shoots growing in clusters and rows. Could any confused and intermingled growth still have been left untended? Once effort had been devoted to all the deadwood, fallen trees, shrubs, and shoots, paths could be opened through the rugged and remote mountain forests. As they “went to Qi,” was it not swiftly becoming a gathering place for people and all manner of things?

Nor was this all. Ordinary trees might be dispensed with, but fine trees useful for timber had to be preserved and nurtured. He therefore tended them according to their particular needs. Fearing that they would grow too thickly, he opened and cleared spaces to thin their kind, preventing them from growing crowded together. Such were the cheng tamarisks; and besides the tamarisks there were also ju shrubs…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
焉蓋非吾山林之植者皆剪伐以去之矣憂其
過繁冗也攘剔之以助其成必欲其挺拔而茂
者則檿也而檿之外又有柘焉蓋利吾民生之
用者又培植以養之矣夫於檉据檿柘而皆從
事焉則林木之深阻者自是成有夷之行天作
高山其勃勃乎都邑之風乎是知太王於營建
之始而已弘開國之規其上承天命下啟王業
而中以慰歸市者之望真有不苟然者矣雖然
周自后稷以来凡三造而營于岐君子勤德小
===
人勤力其精神風采已大異於去邠踰梁之日
及乎太伯王季之賢文王之聖而王業始定其
於險阻蓋備嘗之故詩人每深致其意焉嗣君
其皆知之否乎使其皆知之而皆念之則岐雖
世為周有可矣
春秋
公會齊人宋人救鄭莊公二十八年
魏廷美
同考試官教諭閻批此題場中作者多取魯人書
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 四十三
punctuated:
焉。蓋非吾山林之植者，皆剪伐以去之矣。憂其過繁冗也，攘剔之以助其成，必欲其挺拔而茂者，則檿也，而檿之外又有柘焉。蓋利吾民生之用者，又培植以養之矣。夫於檉据檿柘而皆從事焉，則林木之深阻者，自是成有夷之行。天作高山，其勃勃乎都邑之風乎！是知太王於營建之始，而已弘開國之規。其上承天命，下啟王業，而中以慰歸市者之望，真有不苟然者矣。雖然，周自后稷以来，凡三造而營于岐。君子勤德，小人勤力，其精神風采已大異於去邠踰梁之日。及乎太伯、王季之賢，文王之聖，而王業始定。其於險阻，蓋備嘗之，故詩人每深致其意焉。嗣君其皆知之否乎？使其皆知之而皆念之，則岐雖世為周有，可矣。

春秋

公會齊人、宋人救鄭。莊公二十八年。

魏廷美

同考試官教諭閻批：此題場中作者，多取魯人書
translation_en:
…there as well. Whatever did not belong among the plantings of our mountains and forests was cut down and removed. Concerned that the trees might grow excessively dense, they cleared and pruned them to help their growth. Those they particularly wished to grow tall and luxuriant were the mountain mulberries, and besides these there were also silkworm thorns. Whatever served the needs of our people's livelihood was planted and nurtured. By attending to the tamarisks, ju trees [?], mountain mulberries, and silkworm thorns alike, they made level paths through the deep, obstructing woods. Heaven made the lofty mountain: how vigorously the life of a capital flourished there! Thus we know that, from the very beginning of construction, King Tai had already laid out a broad plan for founding a state. Above, he received Heaven's mandate; below, he opened the way for the royal enterprise; and amid these endeavors he fulfilled the hopes of those who came to his markets. Truly, none of this was done carelessly.

Nevertheless, from Hou Ji onward, Zhou underwent three foundations before establishing itself at Qi. The gentlemen labored at virtue, and the common people labored with their strength. Their spirit and bearing were already greatly changed from the days when they left Bin and crossed Liang. Only with the worthiness of Tai Bo and King Ji, and the sageliness of King Wen, was the royal enterprise firmly established. They had experienced every hardship and obstacle; hence the poets repeatedly expressed their feelings about this with great depth. Do succeeding rulers all understand it? If they all understood it and kept it in mind, Qi could indeed remain Zhou's possession for generations.

Spring and Autumn Annals

“The duke met with men of Qi and men of Song to relieve Zheng.” Twenty-eighth year of Duke Zhuang.

Wei Tingmei

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
救二意桓公主兵漫不省作何說蓋不考伐鄭諸傳故爾又或以
救為與諸侯殊不知終桓之編諸侯會盟救伐美惡一歸之桓以後
盟主大然然也此篇見之真而筆法嚴整録之
考試官訓導于夏批題一句而包數義子發之無
餘蘊矣
考試官訓導于閔批得謹嚴之體
春秋紀伯主制以用兵與其善而著其盛也此
鄭之役書人書救而先齊於宋以主兵所以致
意於桓者深矣昔楚子元無故以車六百乘伐
===
鄭於是齊桓公首赴其難而魯也宋也咸與焉
是役也語將則節鉞不假手上卿語師則羽旄
未煩乎大衆休養兵力重愛民命所謂節制之
師是已春秋將不稱將師不稱師而以微者之
詞書意蓋如此然果何以言其善邪蓋救災恤
患於義為急桓自北杏以來惓焉不忘情於諸
侯今也扳連姻國解鄭於純門之困倡合隣邦
止鄭於桐丘之奔兼道而趨戡定其禍亂刻日
而至綏輯其散亡如風雨而覆之帡幪如饑渴
banxin: 福建鄉試錄四十三
punctuated:
救二意，桓公主兵漫不省作何說，蓋不考伐鄭諸傳故爾。又或以救為與諸侯，殊不知終桓之編，諸侯會盟救伐，美惡一歸之桓，以後盟主大然然也。此篇見之真，而筆法嚴整，録之。
考試官訓導于夏批：題一句而包數義，子發之無餘蘊矣。
考試官訓導于閔批：得謹嚴之體。
春秋紀伯主制以用兵，與其善而著其盛也。此鄭之役，書人，書救，而先齊於宋以主兵，所以致意於桓者深矣。昔楚子元無故以車六百乘伐鄭，於是齊桓公首赴其難，而魯也、宋也咸與焉。是役也，語將，則節鉞不假手上卿；語師，則羽旄未煩乎大衆。休養兵力，重愛民命，所謂節制之師是已。春秋將不稱將，師不稱師，而以微者之詞書，意蓋如此。然果何以言其善邪？蓋救災恤患，於義為急。桓自北杏以來，惓焉不忘情於諸侯。今也扳連姻國，解鄭於純門之困；倡合隣邦，止鄭於桐丘之奔。兼道而趨，戡定其禍亂；刻日而至，綏輯其散亡。如風雨而覆之帡幪，如饑渴
translation_en:
…the two ideas of “relief” [and the preceding point]. They give no thought to how to explain Duke Huan’s command of the troops. This is because they have not examined the various commentaries on the attack upon Zheng. Some also take “relief” as expressing approval of the regional lords. They entirely fail to understand that throughout the entries concerning Huan, whether the regional lords meet, covenant, relieve, or attack, all praise and blame accrue to Huan alone. With subsequent covenant leaders it was generally likewise [?]. This essay perceives the matter truly, and its manner of writing is rigorous and orderly; I have selected it for inclusion.
Examiner and Assistant Instructor Yu Xia comments: “The topic consists of a single sentence yet encompasses several meanings. You have brought them out, leaving nothing unexplored.”
Examiner and Assistant Instructor Yu Min comments: “It achieves a careful and rigorous style.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals records how the hegemon exercised control in employing troops, approving his goodness and displaying his preeminence. In this campaign concerning Zheng, it writes “men” and “relieve,” and places Qi before Song to indicate command of the troops. Profound indeed is the significance it thereby attaches to Huan. Formerly, Ziyuan of Chu, without cause, attacked Zheng with six hundred chariots. Duke Huan of Qi was the first to hasten to its aid in distress, and Lu and Song both took part.
In this campaign, as regards command, the insignia of authority and the battle-axe were not entrusted to chief ministers; as regards the forces, the feathered standards did not call great multitudes into service. Conserving military strength and deeply cherishing the lives of the people: this was what is called an army governed by measured restraint. The Spring and Autumn Annals does not designate the commanders as commanders or the armies as armies, but records them using a term for men of lesser rank. Such, presumably, is its intent.
Yet on what grounds can we speak of his goodness? Relieving disaster and succoring distress are urgent obligations of righteousness. Since Beixing, Huan had devotedly kept the regional lords in his thoughts. Now he drew together states connected by marriage, releasing Zheng from its predicament at Chunmen; he took the lead in uniting neighboring states, forestalling Zheng’s flight to Tongqiu. Traveling at twice the usual pace, he quelled its calamity and disorder; arriving on the appointed day, he pacified and gathered together its scattered and fugitive people. It was as though, amid wind and rain, he covered them with a protective shelter; as though, amid hunger and thirst…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
而濟之食飲如塗炭而登之衽席後此弦之滅
溫之滅黃之滅公若不睹不聞方之今日有相
薰蕕者焉桓武之社得免丘墟溱洧之郊不爲
草莽大率賴之也故救不經見者多矣此特書
救於伐之下非與其善而何抑又何以言其盛
邪蓋安内攘外於事爲美桓自盟幽以來隱然
已屬望於諸侯今也鄭祀垂絕而存風采歆動
乎中夏楚師潛宵而遁威聲聳惕乎外夷人望
之尊俛首歸依上公之貴傾心推戴如衣裳之
===
===
有冠冕如衆山之有泰嶽如百川之有河瀆前
此郕之伐鄭之伐徐之伐公徒旅進旅退方之
今日有相霄壤者焉九合之業此其權輿一匡
之勳此其根柢大率見之矣故兵以爵序常也
此特升齊於宋之上非著其盛而何大抵春秋
諸侯牛羊使人秦越相視爲盟主者亦不知所
有事擁虚器爾若桓者絶無而僅有者也然則
擅興兵甲無貶乎中國衰微夷狄猾夏鄭在王
畿之内曾無投鼠之忌君子之予桓文其得已
banxin: 福建鄕試錄 四十四
punctuated: 而濟之食飲，如塗炭而登之衽席。後此弦之滅、溫之滅、黃之滅，公若不睹不聞，方之今日，有相薰蕕者焉。桓武之社得免丘墟，溱洧之郊不爲草莽，大率賴之也。故救不經見者多矣，此特書救於伐之下，非與其善而何？抑又何以言其盛邪？蓋安内攘外，於事爲美。桓自盟幽以來，隱然已屬望於諸侯。今也鄭祀垂絕而存，風采歆動乎中夏；楚師潛宵而遁，威聲聳惕乎外夷。人望之尊，俛首歸依；上公之貴，傾心推戴。如衣裳之有冠冕，如衆山之有泰嶽，如百川之有河瀆。前此郕之伐、鄭之伐、徐之伐，公徒旅進旅退，方之今日，有相霄壤者焉。九合之業，此其權輿；一匡之勳，此其根柢，大率見之矣。故兵以爵序，常也。此特升齊於宋之上，非著其盛而何？大抵春秋諸侯，牛羊使人，秦越相視，爲盟主者亦不知所有事，擁虚器爾。若桓者，絶無而僅有者也。然則擅興兵甲，無貶乎？中國衰微，夷狄猾夏，鄭在王畿之内，曾無投鼠之忌。君子之予桓文，其得已
translation_en:
…and succoring them with food and drink; as though lifting them from mire and burning coals onto comfortable bedding. Later, when Xian, Wen, and Huang were destroyed, the duke acted as though he neither saw nor heard. Compared with his conduct on this occasion, the difference was like that between fragrant and foul-smelling plants. That the altars of Dukes Huan and Wu of Zheng escaped becoming ruins, and that the countryside along the Zhen and Wei rivers did not become wilderness, was largely owing to this rescue. There were many rescues that went unrecorded in the Classic. Here, however, it specifically records “rescue” after “attack”: what could this mean except approval of his good deed?

Yet how can we also say that this shows his ascendancy? Bringing peace within and repelling threats from without are admirable achievements. Since the covenant at You, Duke Huan had already quietly become the focus of the regional lords’ hopes. Now the ancestral sacrifices of Zheng, on the verge of extinction, were preserved, and his bearing stirred admiration throughout the Central States. The army of Chu slipped away by night, and his military renown struck awe and fear into the foreign peoples beyond. Those exalted in public esteem bowed their heads and pledged allegiance; even those holding the eminent rank of senior duke wholeheartedly acclaimed him. He was like the ceremonial cap completing a set of robes, like Mount Tai among the mountains, like the Yellow River among the hundred streams. Previously, in the attacks on Cheng, Zheng, and Xu, the duke had merely advanced and withdrawn with the others. Compared with his conduct on this occasion, the difference was like that between heaven and earth. Here was the beginning of his achievement in assembling the lords nine times; here was the foundation of his service in setting the realm to rights. Its broad outlines were already apparent. Ordinarily, armies are listed according to their rulers’ noble ranks. Here, however, Qi is specifically raised above Song: what could this mean except to display his ascendancy?

For the most part, the regional lords of the Spring and Autumn period drove people like cattle and sheep and regarded one another with the indifference of Qin and Yue. Even those who led the covenants did not understand their proper duties, merely holding an empty emblem of authority. Someone like Duke Huan was all but unheard of, a rare exception. But then, should he not be censured for taking up arms on his own authority? The Central States were weak and declining, and the Yi and Di were throwing the Xia lands into disorder. Zheng lay within the royal domain, yet its attackers felt none of the restraint of someone who would throw at a rat but fears damaging the vessel beside it. When the gentleman accords approval to Dukes Huan and Wen, could he have refrained…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
哉其不得已哉
晉侯齊師宋師秦師及楚人戰于城濮楚
師敗績〔僖公二十八年〕會于蕭魚〔襄公〕
〔十一年〕
倪組
同考試官教諭閻批強貳譎誠學者類能言
之而發揮明盡文采炳蔚是篇不可不録也
考試官訓導夏批說楚鄭文悼如斷案然乎其
有得於權衡衮斧之法歟
===
考試官訓導閔批麟經健筆此卷為優
春秋貶強夷而勝之以譎者在所畧貶貳國而
感之以誠者在所美此城濮之楚人之蕭魚之
鄭受之貶其強也貳也而所以處之之道在正
譎誠偽之間君子不足於晉文而多乎悼公有
以哉且城濮之戰何為乎晉文公合三國以禦
楚因其請戰而戰也考諸經楚當以稱將稱師
之常詞書之而一無所書人之者何蓋自子玉
執政虎視中原其欲逐逐蠶食諸姬為害駸駸
banxin: 福建鄉試錄四十五
punctuated:
哉？其不得已哉？

晉侯、齊師、宋師、秦師及楚人戰于城濮，楚師敗績。〔僖公二十八年〕會于蕭魚。〔襄公〕〔十一年〕

倪組

同考試官教諭閻批：強、貳、譎、誠，學者類能言之，而發揮明盡，文采炳蔚，是篇不可不録也。

考試官訓導夏批：說楚、鄭、文、悼，如斷案然乎？其有得於權衡衮斧之法歟？

考試官訓導閔批：《麟經》健筆，此卷為優。

《春秋》貶強夷，而勝之以譎者在所畧；貶貳國，而感之以誠者在所美。此城濮之楚人之、蕭魚之鄭受之貶，其強也，貳也，而所以處之之道，在正譎誠偽之間。君子不足於晉文，而多乎悼公，有以哉！且城濮之戰何為乎？晉文公合三國以禦楚，因其請戰而戰也。考諸經，楚當以稱將稱師之常詞書之，而一無所書，人之者何？蓋自子玉執政，虎視中原，其欲逐逐，蠶食諸姬，為害駸駸
translation_en:
…? Or was it something they could not help doing?

“The Lord of Jin, the army of Qi, the army of Song, and the army of Qin fought against the men of Chu at Chengpu. The army of Chu suffered a crushing defeat.” 〔Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi〕 “They met at Xiaoyu.” 〔Duke Xiang〕〔Eleventh year〕

Ni Zu

Comment by Associate Examiner Yan, Instructor: Students generally can discuss aggressiveness, divided allegiance, deception, and sincerity. But this essay develops these matters with clarity and thoroughness, and its literary brilliance is splendid. It cannot be omitted from the record.

Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: Does his discussion of Chu and Zheng, and of Dukes Wen and Dao, not resemble the adjudication of a case? Has he grasped the method of weighing judgments and bestowing praise and censure?

Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: Vigorous writing on the Classic of the Unicorn—the Spring and Autumn Annals. This paper is outstanding.

The Spring and Autumn Annals censures aggressive barbarians, but passes lightly over those who defeat them through deception; it censures states of divided allegiance, but praises those who move them through sincerity. Here, Chu’s designation as “men” at Chengpu and the censure received by Zheng at Xiaoyu [?] concern their aggressiveness and divided allegiance respectively. The methods used to deal with them, however, must be judged by the distinctions between uprightness and deception, sincerity and falsehood. There is good reason why the gentleman finds Duke Wen of Jin wanting but accords Duke Dao high praise!

Now, why was the battle of Chengpu fought? Duke Wen of Jin joined with three states to resist Chu and fought in response to its request for battle. Examining the Classic, Chu ought to have been recorded using the customary wording that names its commander and designates its army. Yet neither appears. Why does it call them merely “men”? Ever since Ziyu took charge of government, he had eyed the Central Plain like a tiger. His desires were relentlessly acquisitive: he was nibbling away at the states of the Ji lineage, and the harm he caused was spreading ever more rapidly…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
今之請戰無乃泓之餘氛益熾邪故人之者懲
其不恪貶也然使晉能抑鋒止銳修文告布詞
命大有以屈服其志善矣乃蒙馬而犯曳柴而
遁誘其軍橫而擊之夾而攻之詭譎萬變而一
鼓成擒三日館穀楚雖帶甲四十萬莫之能攖
功則高矣奚有於道義哉嗚呼鬼方之伐遠矣
春秋時有仗義執言而楚卒納欵者何八公顧
不能邪經所以不揚其事略之者以此若蕭魚
之會何爲乎晉悼公率諸侯以伐鄭因其請會
===
而會也考諸經鄭當以如師如會之常詞書之
而一無所書沒之者何蓋自子駟獻謀君臣上
下無一定之從犧牲玉帛爲二境之待今之請
會安知亳之故轍不蹈邪故沒之者謂其不可
信貶也然使晉徒挾數用術劫以威籠以智一
無以警動其心陋矣乃納彼斥候禁彼侵掠出
其囚赦而禮之遣而歸之真誠一孚而爾無我
虞我無爾詐鄭自是二十四年莫之復叛功固
偉矣奚假於詐力哉嗚呼東方之思遠矣春秋
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 四十八
punctuated:
今之請戰，無乃泓之餘氛益熾邪？故人之者，懲其不恪，貶也。然使晉能抑鋒止銳，修文告，布詞命，大有以屈服其志，善矣。乃蒙馬而犯，曳柴而遁，誘其軍，橫而擊之，夾而攻之，詭譎萬變，而一鼓成擒。三日館穀，楚雖帶甲四十萬，莫之能攖。功則高矣，奚有於道義哉？嗚呼！鬼方之伐遠矣，春秋時有仗義執言而楚卒納欵者，何八公顧不能邪？經所以不揚其事，略之者，以此。
若蕭魚之會，何爲乎？晉悼公率諸侯以伐鄭，因其請會而會也。考諸經，鄭當以如師、如會之常詞書之，而一無所書。沒之者何？蓋自子駟獻謀，君臣上下無一定之從，犧牲玉帛爲二境之待。今之請會，安知亳之故轍不蹈邪？故沒之者，謂其不可信，貶也。然使晉徒挾數用術，劫以威，籠以智，一無以警動其心，陋矣。乃納彼斥候，禁彼侵掠，出其囚，赦而禮之，遣而歸之。真誠一孚，而爾無我虞，我無爾詐。鄭自是二十四年，莫之復叛。功固偉矣，奚假於詐力哉？嗚呼！東方之思遠矣，春秋
translation_en:
…In their present request for battle, was not the lingering spirit of the battle at Hong blazing still more fiercely? Thus, calling them merely “men” punishes their lack of respect: it is a demotion. Yet had Jin been able to restrain its fighting edge, compose proclamations, and issue formal declarations sufficient to subdue their resolve, that would have been good. Instead, they covered their horses and charged, dragged brushwood and retreated, lured out the enemy army, struck it from the flank, and attacked it from both sides. With countless deceitful maneuvers, they captured the enemy at a single beating of the drums. For three days they lodged and ate in the enemy camp. Though Chu had four hundred thousand armored troops, none could withstand them. The achievement was great indeed, but what did it have to do with moral principle and righteousness? Alas! The campaign against Guifang lay in the distant past. Yet in the Spring and Autumn period there was someone who upheld righteousness and spoke with just cause, so that Chu ultimately submitted. Why, then, could the “eight dukes” [?] not do so? This is why the Classic does not exalt this affair but treats it cursorily.
As for the meeting at Xiaoyu, what brought it about? Duke Dao of Jin led the feudal lords in an attack on Zheng and held the meeting in response to Zheng’s request. Examining the Classic, one finds that Zheng should have been recorded with the customary phrases “went to the army” or “went to the meeting”; yet nothing of the kind was written. Why was it suppressed? Ever since Zisi offered his counsel, ruler and ministers, high and low, had maintained no fixed allegiance, keeping sacrificial animals, jade, and silk ready for whichever of the two neighboring powers they might have to receive. With this present request for a meeting, how could one know that they would not follow the old tracks of Bo again? Thus, suppressing their participation declares them untrustworthy: it is a demotion. Yet had Jin merely resorted to calculations and stratagems, intimidated them with might, and ensnared them with cleverness, without doing anything to awaken their hearts, that would have been base. Instead, Jin brought in their scouts [?], prohibited incursions and plundering against them, released their captives, pardoned them and treated them courteously, and sent them home. Once genuine sincerity established trust, it became a matter of “you shall not deceive me, and I shall not cheat you.” For twenty-four years thereafter, Zheng never again rebelled against Jin. The achievement was indeed magnificent: what need was there to borrow the aid of deceit and force? Alas! The longing of the eastern lands lay in the distant past. In the Spring and Autumn…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
時有禮招德懷而鄭卒受盟者何人公豈多讓
邪春秋所以特書其事美之者以此是則譎而
不正文公以之誠而不偽悼公有焉先儒謂文
非桓匹又曰悼公有君子之資信夫抑悼誠愈
於文歟書錄文侯之命捍王于艱錫以秬鬯為
東周賢侯侯其源也文公其流也悼公其委也
論者必先河而後海
禮記
大樂必易大禮必簡
鄭漳
同考試官學正陳批題甚冠冕場中作者類不
歸重制作且於易簡處發揮欠明惟此篇詞贍意足脫去凡近故
錄以為讀禮經者式
考試官訓導夏批經旨通明筆力勁健禮學似此者絕少
考試官訓導閔批說理之文明白條暢允為傑作
和之至者有不勞序之至者有不煩蓋大樂乃
和之至大禮則序之至也禮樂之制作既極於
和序則其易簡之妙亦自然而然矣樂記君子
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 四十七
punctuated:
時，有禮招德懷而鄭卒受盟者何？人公豈多讓邪？《春秋》所以特書其事美之者以此。是則譎而不正，文公以之；誠而不偽，悼公有焉。先儒謂文非桓匹，又曰悼公有君子之資，信夫！抑悼誠愈於文歟？《書》錄《文侯之命》，捍王于艱，錫以秬鬯，為東周賢侯。侯其源也，文公其流也，悼公其委也。論者必先河而後海。

禮記
大樂必易，大禮必簡。
鄭漳

同考試官學正陳批：題甚冠冕，場中作者類不歸重制作，且於易簡處發揮欠明。惟此篇詞贍意足，脫去凡近，故錄以為讀禮經者式。

考試官訓導夏批：經旨通明，筆力勁健，禮學似此者絕少。

考試官訓導閔批：說理之文明白條暢，允為傑作。

和之至者有不勞，序之至者有不煩。蓋大樂乃和之至，大禮則序之至也。禮樂之制作既極於和序，則其易簡之妙亦自然而然矣。《樂記》君子
translation_en:
…in that age, why was it that Zheng ultimately accepted the covenant when summoned through ritual propriety and won over through virtue? Would Duke [Ren?] have yielded much precedence to him? [?] This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals specially records the affair to commend him. Thus Duke Wen employed cunning without uprightness, whereas Duke Dao possessed sincerity without deceit. Earlier Confucian scholars said that Duke Wen was no match for Duke Huan, and also that Duke Dao had the qualities of a gentleman. How true! Yet did Dao truly surpass Wen? The Book of Documents records the “Charge to the Marquis of Wen”: he defended the king in adversity and was bestowed with black-millet sacrificial liquor, becoming a worthy marquis of the Eastern Zhou. The marquis was the source; Duke Wen, the continuing stream; and Duke Dao, its confluence. Those who discuss them must consider the river before the sea.

Record of Rites
“Great music must be easy; great rites must be simple.”
By Zheng Zhang.

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, an Instructor: The topic is most imposing. Candidates in the examination generally failed to place due emphasis on the institution of rites and music, and their exposition of ease and simplicity lacked clarity. This essay alone has ample expression and fully developed ideas, rising above the commonplace. It is therefore recorded as a model for students of the ritual classic.

Comment by Examiner Xia, an Assistant Instructor: The meaning of the classic is thoroughly and clearly understood, and the writing is vigorous. Such learning in ritual is exceedingly rare.

Comment by Examiner Min, an Assistant Instructor: The exposition of principle is lucid, coherent, and fluent. This is indeed an outstanding work.

In the utmost harmony there is freedom from toil; in the utmost order there is freedom from complication. Great music is the perfection of harmony, and great rites are the perfection of order. Once the institution of rites and music has attained the utmost harmony and order, their wondrous ease and simplicity arise naturally of themselves. The gentleman in the Record of Music …

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
謂夫制作之本固出於吾身制作之妙自合於
造化是故王者之撫世本諸性情之蘊達於聲
容之間以昭一代之成功者此大樂也其間節
奏之備綴兆之陳似亦勞矣然樂之極其和者
自首至尾皆懽欣之所流通相倡而相和者有
周流同化之妙或俯而或仰者有絪縕交密之
機優柔平中而終九成之韻夫何有於懣懣也
從容雅正而具萬舞之觀亦何有於勉強也是
猶萬物之生皆乾元所致而妙功化於無迹矣
===
其易也為何如王者之御極觀其會通之理著
為典則之儀以飾一代之盛治者此大禮也其
間儀文之盛度數之詳似亦繁矣然禮之極其
序者自始至終皆嘉美之所發越親疎異等一
物各付物之宜貴賤殊位一高下散殊之妙循
其自然而節文乎天理固無所謂紛擾也行所
無事而儀則乎人事亦無所謂瑣屑也是猶萬
化之成一坤元之所為而泯雕琢於無形矣其
簡也為何如是則禮樂之大其妙如此此其所
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 四十八
punctuated: 謂夫制作之本，固出於吾身；制作之妙，自合於造化。是故王者之撫世，本諸性情之蘊，達於聲容之間，以昭一代之成功者，此大樂也。其間節奏之備，綴兆之陳，似亦勞矣。然樂之極其和者，自首至尾，皆懽欣之所流通。相倡而相和者，有周流同化之妙；或俯而或仰者，有絪縕交密之機。優柔平中而終九成之韻，夫何有於懣懣也？從容雅正而具萬舞之觀，亦何有於勉強也？是猶萬物之生，皆乾元所致，而妙功化於無迹矣。其易也為何如？王者之御極，觀其會通之理，著為典則之儀，以飾一代之盛治者，此大禮也。其間儀文之盛，度數之詳，似亦繁矣。然禮之極其序者，自始至終，皆嘉美之所發越。親疎異等，一物各付物之宜；貴賤殊位，一高下散殊之妙。循其自然而節文乎天理，固無所謂紛擾也；行所無事而儀則乎人事，亦無所謂瑣屑也。是猶萬化之成，一坤元之所為，而泯雕琢於無形矣。其簡也為何如？是則禮樂之大，其妙如此，此其所
translation_en:
…says that the foundation of instituting rites and music indeed comes from our own persons, while the subtle excellence of these institutions naturally accords with the creative processes of Heaven and Earth. Thus, when a king governs the world, he draws upon the inner resources of human nature and feelings and gives them expression in sounds and movements, thereby displaying the accomplishments of his age: this is great music. Its complete rhythms and arrayed dancing positions may seem to entail toil. Yet music that attains the utmost harmony is, from beginning to end, a continuous flow of joy.
