punctuated: 而作之，以收天下大順之功，則必有制作之本者而後能之也，又豈徒區區辨音律者之擬哉？執事發策下詢，而有及于樂，請述所聞以告，可乎？嘗考之《樂記》，有知聲、知音、知樂之等，而品以禽獸、衆庶、君子之别，其旨固微矣。近世方氏以吾夫子與季札為君子之知樂，蓋亦有見矣。然夫子在齊之所聞，既已莫之可考，而季札聘魯之所觀，實有足徵者。札於諸風、雅、頌以及乎象舞，皆致夫深賛之詞，可也；而獨於小雅，嘆其為周之衰。文中子疑豳風，烏乎樂必知與二南相誤故也；而獨於小雅，反謂為周之盛者，誠以小雅者周道盛衰之會也。季札之所言，蓋當時親見夫周道之衰，而不覩乎文武成康之盛也。文中子之所言，蓋謂文武之餘烈未忘，而天下猶宗周也。眉山蘇氏有曰：「必合二子之說，而小雅之道備。」其言得之矣。自是而後，知樂者益鮮，然
translation_en:
…and put it into practice to achieve the perfect harmony of all under Heaven, one must first possess the foundations for creating music. How could someone whose abilities extend merely to distinguishing tones and pitch standards hope to equal this? You, honored examiners, have issued policy questions seeking our views, and have touched upon music. May I set forth what I have learned?

I have examined the Record of Music: it distinguishes between knowing sounds, knowing musical tones, and knowing music, assigning these respectively to beasts and birds, the common people, and the gentleman. Its meaning is indeed subtle. Master Fang of more recent times identified our Master Confucius and Ji Zha as gentlemen who understood music; this, too, shows insight. What Confucius heard in Qi can no longer be ascertained, but what Ji Zha witnessed on his diplomatic visit to Lu can indeed be verified. It was fitting that Ji Zha offered profound praise for the Airs, the Odes, and the Hymns, and even for the Xiang dance. Yet of the Lesser Odes alone he lamented that they represented Zhou’s decline. Wenzhongzi questioned the Airs of Bin; the text here is unclear, apparently referring to a confusion with the Two Southern Sections [?]. Yet of the Lesser Odes alone he said, conversely, that they represented Zhou’s flourishing. This is truly because the Lesser Odes stand at the juncture of the flourishing and decline of the Zhou Way.

Ji Zha spoke as he did because he personally witnessed the decline of the Zhou Way in his own time, but had not seen the flourishing ages of Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang. Wenzhongzi’s statement meant that the enduring achievements of Kings Wen and Wu had not been forgotten, and that all under Heaven still acknowledged Zhou as their sovereign. Master Su of Meishan said: “Only by combining the explanations of these two masters can the meaning of the Lesser Odes be fully understood.” His words have grasped the matter. Thereafter, those who understood music became increasingly rare. Yet…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
在晉則有荀勗焉得牛鐸於趙人而聲律
以諧故當時有暗解之稱其時又有阮咸
焉得玉尺於田夫而校量無異故當時有
神解之譽魏之陳仲孺依準以調八音而
輕重不失其倫隋之萬寶常扣器以成宮
商而高下曲盡其妙張文收之得玉磬於
潤州也知其為黃鍾之闕楊收之見古鍾
於岑陽也識其為姑洗之角他若信都芳
則仰觀雲色而知乎律管之飛灰王維則
===
俯按樂圖而知為霓裳之三疊之數子者
皆精於音律而超出乎鏗鏘節奏之表固
非眾庶之知音可及矣然或昧於所本而
未造乎探本窮源之地比之季札之知德
者有間焉凡此猶皆就樂以論者至如司
馬遷之為律書也其始雖不言律而言兵
不言兵之用而言兵之偃然又繼以文帝
偃兵息民以致召和之說蓋以天地之氣
正而律可造即所謂風氣正而十二律定
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 七十七
punctuated: 在晉則有荀勗焉，得牛鐸於趙人而聲律以諧，故當時有暗解之稱。其時又有阮咸焉，得玉尺於田夫而校量無異，故當時有神解之譽。魏之陳仲孺依準以調八音，而輕重不失其倫；隋之萬寶常扣器以成宮商，而高下曲盡其妙。張文收之得玉磬於潤州也，知其為黃鍾之闕；楊收之見古鍾於岑陽也，識其為姑洗之角。他若信都芳，則仰觀雲色而知乎律管之飛灰；王維則俯按樂圖，而知為霓裳之三疊。之數子者，皆精於音律，而超出乎鏗鏘節奏之表，固非眾庶之知音可及矣。然或昧於所本，而未造乎探本窮源之地，比之季札之知德者有間焉。凡此猶皆就樂以論者。至如司馬遷之為律書也，其始雖不言律而言兵，不言兵之用而言兵之偃，然又繼以文帝偃兵息民以致召和之說。蓋以天地之氣正而律可造，即所謂風氣正而十二律定
translation_en:
…In the Jin there was Xun Xu, who obtained a cattle bell from a man of Zhao and thereby brought the pitches into harmony; hence his contemporaries credited him with an intuitive understanding. At that time there was also Ruan Xian, who obtained a jade measuring rule from a farmer and found, on comparison, that the measurements did not differ; hence his contemporaries praised his inspired understanding. Chen Zhongru of the Wei used a pitch standard to tune the eight classes of musical instruments, keeping their relative strength in proper order. Wan Baochang of the Sui struck vessels to produce the gong and shang notes, fully realizing the subtleties of high and low pitches. When Zhang Wenshou obtained a jade chime stone in Runzhou, he recognized that it supplied what was missing in the Huangzhong pitch. When Yang Shou saw an ancient bell in Cenyang, he recognized it as the jue note of the Guxian mode. Others included Xindu Fang, who looked up at the colors of the clouds and knew when the ashes would fly from the pitch pipes, and Wang Wei, who looked down at a picture of musical performance and recognized the third section of Rainbow Skirts. These men [?] were all expert in musical pitches, and their understanding extended beyond ringing sounds and rhythmic patterns; it was certainly beyond the musical discernment of ordinary people. Yet some were unclear about the underlying foundations and had not reached the point of tracing things to their roots and fathoming their sources. They fell short of Ji Zha’s ability to discern virtue.

All these examples still concern discussions confined to music itself. As for Sima Qian’s composition of the Treatise on the Pitch Pipes, although he began by speaking of warfare rather than pitch standards, and of laying down arms rather than employing them, he followed this with an account of how Emperor Wen laid down arms and gave the people repose, thereby bringing about harmony. His premise was that pitch standards could be established when the vital energies of Heaven and Earth were correctly ordered. This is precisely what is meant by the saying that when the winds and vital energies are correctly ordered, the twelve pitch standards become settled…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
者陳氏謂其知制律之本不亦宜乎諸葛
亮治蜀雖曰干戈方勤於一隅設施未及
於天下然能左右昭烈出興漢討賊之師
爲仗義執言之舉天地之大義已明天下
之人心亦服所謂名正言順而事成者王
通謂其可興禮樂豈不信乎夫何文帝謙
讓未遑而昭烈中道崩殂後世之觀者蓋
不能無憾於斯矣然幸道未墜也有宋大
儒若晦庵朱子西山蔡氏應時以出而師
===
友之間倡明道學又以其暇力著爲通解
鍾律律呂新書二編自今觀之蔡氏之爲
新書也起於黃鍾終於度量權衡二十三
篇之間大抵皆古人已試之成法而叅以
已意簡約周盡而無遺憾焉朱子因之爲
鍾律也起於陰陽辰位相生次序終於黃
鍾生十一律數法一十三篇之中大率多
蔡氏所著之成規而更互演繹尤爲明邃
而有可觀焉然則二書之在天下誠爲六
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 七十八
punctuated:
者，陳氏謂其知制律之本，不亦宜乎？諸葛亮治蜀，雖曰干戈方勤於一隅，設施未及於天下，然能左右昭烈，出興漢討賊之師，爲仗義執言之舉。天地之大義已明，天下之人心亦服，所謂名正言順而事成者。王通謂其可興禮樂，豈不信乎？夫何文帝謙讓未遑，而昭烈中道崩殂？後世之觀者，蓋不能無憾於斯矣。
然幸道未墜也，有宋大儒若晦庵朱子、西山蔡氏，應時以出，而師友之間倡明道學，又以其暇力著爲《通解鍾律》《律呂新書》二編。自今觀之，蔡氏之爲《新書》也，起於黃鍾，終於度量權衡，二十三篇之間，大抵皆古人已試之成法，而叅以已意，簡約周盡而無遺憾焉。朱子因之爲《鍾律》也，起於陰陽辰位相生次序，終於黃鍾生十一律數法，一十三篇之中，大率多蔡氏所著之成規，而更互演繹，尤爲明邃而有可觀焉。然則二書之在天下，誠爲六
translation_en:
…Master Chen said that he understood the basis for establishing the pitch standards: was this not fitting? When Zhuge Liang governed Shu, although warfare still occupied him in one corner of the realm and his measures had not yet extended throughout the world, he nevertheless assisted Emperor Zhaolie in sending forth armies to restore the Han and punish rebels, undertaking a cause that upheld righteousness and proclaimed its just grounds. The great righteousness of Heaven and Earth was thereby made manifest, and the hearts of the people throughout the realm were won over. This exemplified the saying that when names are correct, words accord with them, and affairs succeed. Wang Tong said that he could revive rites and music: was this not true? Yet why did Emperor Wen defer modestly and find no opportunity, while Emperor Zhaolie died midway through his undertaking? Those of later generations who consider this cannot but feel regret.
Fortunately, however, the Way had not fallen into oblivion. Great Confucian scholars of the Song, such as Master Zhu of Hui’an and Master Cai of Xishan, emerged in response to their times. As teachers and friends, they elucidated the Learning of the Way, and with their remaining time and energy compiled two works: Bell Pitches in the Comprehensive Explanation (Tongjie Zhonglü) and New Treatise on the Pitch Standards (Lülü Xinshu). Viewed from the present, Master Cai’s New Treatise begins with the Yellow Bell pitch and ends with length, capacity, and weight measures. Its twenty-three chapters consist largely of established methods already tested by the ancients, supplemented with his own ideas. Concise yet comprehensive, it leaves nothing to be regretted. Master Zhu drew upon it to compose Bell Pitches, beginning with the positions of yin and yang among the twelve earthly branches and the sequence by which pitches generate one another, and ending with numerical methods by which the Yellow Bell generates the other eleven pitches. Its thirteen chapters largely follow the established patterns set out by Master Cai, developing and elucidating them in relation to one another. They are especially clear and profound, and well worth studying. Thus, these two books, available to the world, truly serve as aids to the Six…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
經之輔翼而可以補樂音之殘缺者矣我
太祖高皇帝創業于先
列聖相承繼統于後累葉重光甄陶天下百五
十餘年正積德久而禮樂可興之時也二
儒之書尚俟
聖天子采而用之因今而求之古循俗而入于
雅將見
和平之治可成而三代之樂亦可復見于
今日矣執事不以為妄進而教之雖曰未能
===
願學焉
第四問
鄭璋
同考試官學正陳批五策援經據史若千金之
市随取而無不足者此篇於老成之智養才之望品藻明審而其模
寫忠槩之大歷歷如在錄之以見尚友之志云
考試官訓導夏批老成處疑决變要自素養
而彈壓之望不可誣也此策筆力遒勁而諸賢英偉之烈發揚
殆盡高薦何忝
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 七十九
punctuated:
經之輔翼，而可以補樂音之殘缺者矣。我太祖高皇帝創業于先，列聖相承繼統于後，累葉重光，甄陶天下百五十餘年，正積德久而禮樂可興之時也。二儒之書，尚俟聖天子采而用之，因今而求之古，循俗而入于雅，將見和平之治可成，而三代之樂亦可復見于今日矣。執事不以為妄，進而教之，雖曰未能，願學焉。
第四問
鄭璋
同考試官學正陳批：五策援經據史，若千金之市，随取而無不足者。此篇於老成之智、養才之望，品藻明審，而其模寫忠槩之大，歷歷如在。錄之以見尚友之志云。
考試官訓導夏批：老成處疑决變，要自素養，而彈壓之望不可誣也。此策筆力遒勁，而諸賢英偉之烈發揚殆盡，高薦何忝？
translation_en:
…as aids to the [Six] Classics, capable of making good the deficiencies in musical knowledge. Our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the dynasty, and the successive sage emperors thereafter inherited the throne. Through generations of renewed glory, they have molded the realm for more than a hundred and fifty years. This is precisely a time when virtue has long accumulated and rites and music can flourish. The books of these two scholars still await the sage Son of Heaven’s adoption and use. By proceeding from the present to seek out antiquity, and following customary practice toward classical refinement, we shall see peaceful and harmonious government achieved, and the music of the Three Dynasties may once more appear in our own day. If you, honored sir, do not consider these words presumptuous, grant me further instruction. Though I cannot yet accomplish this, I am willing to learn.
Fourth Question
Zheng Zhang
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, School Instructor: “These five policy essays invoke the Classics and draw upon the histories, like someone shopping with a thousand pieces of gold: whatever he chooses, his resources never fall short. In this essay, his assessments of the wisdom of seasoned men and the hopes for nurturing talent are clear and discerning. His portrayal of their great loyal spirit is so vivid that they seem present before us. We record it to show his aspiration to take the worthy men of antiquity as his friends.”
Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: “Seasoned men’s ability to resolve doubts and decide how to meet crises must derive from long cultivation; their reputation for keeping disorder in check cannot be gainsaid. This policy essay is written with vigorous force and brings out almost fully the heroic and splendid achievements of these worthies. How could he be unworthy of a high recommendation?”

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官訓導閔批前二試已知子之奇而此策
文思沛乎與先賢光大之氣若競爽然者得士如此無負科目
也已
對人君任天下之重必有以圖天下之務
人臣成天下之務必有以負天下之望蓋
天下之大事與所謂大疑者其爲幾至要
爲責至難而爲功亦至大也人才閱世之
淺深繫國之輕重而治亂因以占之故周
章疎謬者非練達之士而安危之幾毅然
===
有立者必其更事多而思慮熟者耳蓋嘗
考夫易之大過言大過之時非有大過人
之才不能濟也詩曰雖無老成人尚有典
刑言老成之重於典刑也故太公奮跡磻
溪而成燮伐之功畢公弼亮四世而重保
釐之任是皆所謂老成之才而濟大過之
時者也有國者其猶得不加意於若人哉
愚請得而條陳之夫抱關夷門侯生似可
鄙矣然信陵執轡而建救趙之謀少不如
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 八十
punctuated:
考試官訓導閔批：前二試已知子之奇，而此策文思沛乎，與先賢光大之氣若競爽然者。得士如此，無負科目也已。

對：人君任天下之重，必有以圖天下之務；人臣成天下之務，必有以負天下之望。蓋天下之大事與所謂大疑者，其爲幾至要，爲責至難，而爲功亦至大也。人才閱世之淺深，繫國之輕重，而治亂因以占之。故周章疎謬者非練達之士，而安危之幾毅然有立者，必其更事多而思慮熟者耳。蓋嘗考夫《易》之《大過》，言大過之時，非有大過人之才不能濟也。《詩》曰：「雖無老成人，尚有典刑。」言老成之重於典刑也。故太公奮跡磻溪，而成燮伐之功；畢公弼亮四世，而重保釐之任。是皆所謂老成之才，而濟大過之時者也。有國者，其猶得不加意於若人哉？愚請得而條陳之。夫抱關夷門，侯生似可鄙矣；然信陵執轡，而建救趙之謀。少不如
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: From the first two examination sessions I already knew your exceptional ability. In this policy essay, your literary inspiration flows abundantly, seemingly vying in brilliance with the expansive spirit of the worthies of old. To obtain a scholar like this truly fulfills the purpose of the examinations.

Answer: A ruler bears the weighty responsibility for all under Heaven and must therefore have the means to plan its affairs. A minister brings those affairs to completion and must therefore have the means to shoulder the expectations of all under Heaven. The great affairs of the realm and what are called its great uncertainties involve junctures of utmost importance, responsibilities of utmost difficulty, and achievements of utmost magnitude. The depth or shallowness of a talented man's experience determines his importance to the state, and from this one may foretell order or disorder. Thus, those who are flustered, careless, and mistaken are not men of seasoned judgment. Those who stand resolutely at a juncture between safety and peril must be men who have experienced much and deliberated thoroughly.

I have examined the hexagram Great Exceeding in the Book of Changes: it explains that, in times of extraordinary strain, only someone whose talents greatly exceed those of others can bring deliverance. The Book of Odes says: “Though there are no old and accomplished men, the exemplary standards still remain.” This speaks of the importance of seasoned men in relation to exemplary standards. Thus Taigong rose from obscurity at Panxi and achieved success in the concerted campaign; the Duke of Bi assisted and enlightened four generations of rulers and bore the weighty charge of protecting and governing. These were all men of what is called seasoned talent, who brought deliverance in times of extraordinary strain. Can those who rule a state possibly fail to give particular attention to such men?

May I venture to set out the examples one by one. As a gatekeeper at Yimen, Master Hou might have seemed beneath consideration. Yet Lord Xinling took the reins for him, and he devised the plan to rescue Zhao. In youth, not the equal of…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
人燭之武信無能矣然秦伯請盟而紓鄭
侯之難王翦動衆六十萬一舉而破荆楚
豈恇怯之所能趙充國留屯十二事全策
而制先零固好謀而有濟神龍之初唐之
宗廟已爲周矣張柬之提兵禁衞中宗之
位已正而上陽之號遂尊天寶之末唐之
王室已如贅矣郭子儀建節朔方兩京之
績既收而涇陽之盟彌固淮蔡之役成計
幾於見沮裴度身親戎務而僭亂以之削
===
平真宗之立羣小幾於造變呂端首折異
謀而大位以之鎮定新法既行致鄭公之
解郡元祐之薦煩彥博而再來然或屢疏
大事而注天子之思或獨著風裁而起遠
人之敬其所以屬當時之望者重矣正色
立朝乃王曾之大節重厚如勃實韓琦之
大忠然或感動兩宮而左右畏憚或歷任
三朝而繫國安危其所以任社稷之重者
力矣自今觀之士生其時以才則周以智
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 八十一
punctuated: 人，燭之武信無能矣，然秦伯請盟，而紓鄭侯之難。王翦動衆六十萬，一舉而破荆楚，豈恇怯之所能？趙充國留屯十二事，全策而制先零，固好謀而有濟。神龍之初，唐之宗廟已爲周矣，張柬之提兵禁衞，中宗之位已正，而上陽之號遂尊。天寶之末，唐之王室已如贅矣，郭子儀建節朔方，兩京之績既收，而涇陽之盟彌固。淮蔡之役，成計幾於見沮，裴度身親戎務，而僭亂以之削平。真宗之立，羣小幾於造變，呂端首折異謀，而大位以之鎮定。新法既行，致鄭公之解郡；元祐之薦，煩彥博而再來。然或屢疏大事，而注天子之思；或獨著風裁，而起遠人之敬。其所以屬當時之望者重矣。正色立朝，乃王曾之大節；重厚如勃，實韓琦之大忠。然或感動兩宮，而左右畏憚；或歷任三朝，而繫國安危。其所以任社稷之重者力矣。自今觀之，士生其時，以才則周，以智
translation_en:
…others, Zhu Zhiwu seemingly had no abilities indeed; yet the Earl of Qin requested a covenant, relieving the Marquis of Zheng of his peril. Wang Jian mobilized six hundred thousand men and shattered Jing-Chu in a single campaign: could a timid man have accomplished this? Zhao Chongguo submitted twelve points in favor of keeping troops stationed to cultivate the land, and through a comprehensive strategy subdued the Xianling. He was indeed fond of planning and effective in carrying plans through.

At the beginning of the Shenlong era, the ancestral temples of Tang had already become those of Zhou. Zhang Jianzhi led troops of the palace guard; Emperor Zhongzong was restored to his rightful throne, while the sovereign at Shangyang received an honored title. At the end of the Tianbao era, the Tang royal house had become like a useless appendage. Guo Ziyi took up military command in Shuofang; having achieved the recovery of the two capitals, he further secured the covenant at Jingyang. During the campaign against Huai and Cai, an already settled plan nearly met with obstruction. Pei Du personally directed military affairs, and the usurping rebels were thereby suppressed. At Emperor Zhenzong’s accession, a clique of petty men nearly fomented an upheaval. Lü Duan took the lead in thwarting their rival scheme, and the imperial throne was thereby secured.

Once the New Policies were implemented, the Duke of Zheng was induced to relinquish his prefectural post; a recommendation during the Yuanyou era troubled Yanbo to return once more. Yet one repeatedly submitted memorials on great affairs, drawing the emperor’s thoughtful attention; the other displayed an exemplary bearing that inspired respect among people from afar. Weighty indeed were the qualities that made them the focus of their contemporaries’ hopes. To stand at court with a grave and upright demeanor was Wang Zeng’s great integrity; to be steadfast and substantial like Bo was Han Qi’s great loyalty. One moved the occupants of both palaces, so that their attendants regarded him with apprehensive respect; the other served through three reigns, with the security or peril of the state bound up with his person. Powerful indeed were the qualities that enabled them to bear the weight of the altars of soil and grain. Viewed from the present, these men, born into their respective times, were comprehensive in their abilities, and in wisdom…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
則審以成天下之事則大矣而後世猶不
能無異論者何也愚嘗慨夫勇如王翦以
怯見棄而卒自衒其能智如侯生以術見
用而乃幸售其謀諸武旣誅大義不容以
不正賢如柬之顧貽反噬之慘勲庸旣顯
晚節不可以不脩賢如裴度乃為自安之
計之數子者智有餘而養則未純才可資
而望或不足是故君子所以有遺憾也若
夫令公之忠貫金石而讒邪之間消信行
===
蠻貊而反側之變弭而先儒許之為大臣
者豈無所據乎魏公之再决大策奠天下
之危疑矢心徇國畧一身之成敗而先儒
擬之為間氣者抑有所見乎鄭公之两使
點虜五辭起復忠義之氣爭光日月而史
稱其有仁人之利者此也潞公之四代元
臣累秉鈞軸公忠之烈聞于四夷史贊其
有大臣之槩者是也之四子者養旣深而
德則厚才旣全而望攸隆取人三代而下
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 八十□
punctuated:
則審，以成天下之事則大矣。而後世猶不能無異論者，何也？愚嘗慨夫勇如王翦，以怯見棄，而卒自衒其能；智如侯生，以術見用，而乃幸售其謀。諸武旣誅，大義不容以不正，賢如柬之，顧貽反噬之慘；勲庸旣顯，晚節不可以不脩，賢如裴度，乃為自安之計。之數子者，智有餘而養則未純，才可資而望或不足，是故君子所以有遺憾也。
若夫令公之忠貫金石，而讒邪之間消；信行蠻貊，而反側之變弭，而先儒許之為大臣者，豈無所據乎？魏公之再决大策，奠天下之危疑，矢心徇國，畧一身之成敗，而先儒擬之為間氣者，抑有所見乎？鄭公之两使點虜，五辭起復，忠義之氣爭光日月，而史稱其有仁人之利者，此也。潞公之四代元臣，累秉鈞軸，公忠之烈聞于四夷，史贊其有大臣之槩者，是也。之四子者，養旣深而德則厚，才旣全而望攸隆。取人三代而下
translation_en:
…in judgment they were discerning, and in accomplishing the affairs of the realm their achievements were great. Yet why have later generations still been unable to agree in their assessments? I have often lamented that someone as courageous as Wang Jian was dismissed as timid and ultimately advertised his own ability; that someone as shrewd as Hou Sheng was employed for his stratagems, yet merely had the good fortune to have his plan accepted. Once the members of the Wu clan had been executed, the great principles of righteousness had to be upheld; yet even someone as worthy as Jianzhi brought upon himself the tragedy of a counterattack. Once meritorious achievements were established, integrity in later life still required cultivation; yet even someone as worthy as Pei Du devised plans for his own security. These men had intelligence to spare, but their self-cultivation was not entirely pure; their talents could be put to use, but their standing sometimes fell short. This is why the gentleman finds grounds for regret in them.
As for the Lord Commandant, his loyalty penetrated metal and stone, dissolving the estrangement sown by slanderers and evildoers; his trustworthiness prevailed among the Man and Mo peoples, quelling the disturbances of the disaffected. Could earlier Confucian scholars have lacked grounds for recognizing him as a great minister? The Duke of Wei twice settled momentous questions of state, bringing stability amid peril and uncertainty throughout the realm. He pledged himself to serve his country, disregarding his personal success or failure. Surely earlier Confucian scholars had some insight when they likened him to a rare embodiment of Heaven and Earth’s vital force? The Duke of Zheng twice went as envoy to the enemy [?] and five times declined recall to office during mourning. The spirit of his loyalty and righteousness rivaled the sun and moon in brilliance. This is why the histories said that he possessed the beneficence of a humane man [?]. The Duke of Lu was a senior minister under four sovereigns and repeatedly held the reins of government. His outstanding public devotion and loyalty were known among the peoples of the four quarters. This is why the histories praised him as possessing the bearing of a great minister. These four men had cultivated themselves deeply, and their virtue was substantial; their talents were complete, and their standing was consequently exalted. In selecting men from the ages after the Three Dynasties…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
此其優者耳至於區區智謀之末如燭之
武者何足以為士哉抑嘗論老成之有益
於天下也譬如蓍龜之為信楩枏之為材
求而用之天下之事無不濟也違而棄之
天下之事無不悖也故人君遇之必隆其
禮任之必竭其忠蓋有倚其夙昔之望而
不責其造次之功者矣嗚呼太公尚父之
號畢公父師之尊誠非致文貌於一朝一
夕之閒而已此固圖任老成之意也愚生
===
芹曝之誠願為
今日獻焉謹對
第五問
廖世昭
同考試官教諭沈批策本時務塲中答者多
草草蹈襲以應故事不然漫為大言無徴於用良為可厭今
觀此篇用事引證區處精切蓋亦識古今事勢者末復以
教化立說尤出人數倍得士如此可以薦矣
同考試官教諭杜批意語明秀格製典古較
banxin: 福建鄉試錄八十三
punctuated:
此其優者耳。至於區區智謀之末，如燭之武者，何足以為士哉？抑嘗論老成之有益於天下也，譬如蓍龜之為信、楩枏之為材，求而用之，天下之事無不濟也；違而棄之，天下之事無不悖也。故人君遇之必隆其禮，任之必竭其忠，蓋有倚其夙昔之望而不責其造次之功者矣。嗚呼！太公尚父之號，畢公父師之尊，誠非致文貌於一朝一夕之閒而已，此固圖任老成之意也。愚生芹曝之誠，願為今日獻焉。謹對。

第五問
廖世昭

同考試官教諭沈批：策本時務，塲中答者多草草蹈襲以應故事；不然，漫為大言，無徴於用，良為可厭。今觀此篇，用事引證，區處精切，蓋亦識古今事勢者。末復以教化立說，尤出人數倍。得士如此，可以薦矣。

同考試官教諭杜批：意語明秀，格製典古，較
translation_en:
…these are simply the outstanding ones. As for petty, peripheral feats of clever scheming, such as those of Zhu Zhiwu, how could they suffice to qualify someone as a worthy scholar? I have also reflected on how seasoned men benefit the realm. They are as trustworthy as the divining milfoil and tortoise shell, and as useful as the timber of pian and nan trees. Seek them out and employ them, and every undertaking in the realm will succeed; disregard and discard them, and every undertaking will go awry. Thus, a ruler must treat them with the utmost ceremonial respect and, in employing them, draw fully upon their loyal service. He may indeed rely on their long-established reputation without demanding achievements in haste. Alas! The title “Revered Father” bestowed on the Grand Duke, and the honor accorded the Duke of Bi as “Father and Preceptor,” were certainly more than outward courtesies extended for a single morning or evening. They expressed a determination to seek out and entrust responsibilities to seasoned men. With the sincerity of one offering humble celery and the warmth of the sun, I, an unworthy student, wish to present these thoughts to the present sovereign. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Fifth Question
Liao Shizhao

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: Policy questions are grounded in current affairs. Most candidates in the examination hall hastily repeat familiar formulations merely to fulfill the customary requirement. Otherwise, they indulge in grand pronouncements with no demonstrated practical value. This is truly tiresome. In this essay, however, the use of historical precedents and supporting evidence, and the proposed handling of affairs, are precise and pertinent. The author evidently understands the circumstances of affairs both past and present. At the end, he further grounds his argument in moral instruction, surpassing others several times over. A scholar of this caliber is worthy of recommendation.

Comment by Associate Examiner Du, Instructor: The ideas and language are lucid and elegant; the form and composition are classical and antique. In assessing …

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
時大務摘發呈露而無餘秘非胷中素有尺度疇克有是
㦤古人以匹夫而懷抱天下之憂乎殆有見乎徒羡讀書
考試官訓導夏批考究詳明議論高遠真俊
傑之士也他日拜大廷往以有爲自効於
君民者是用錄之以俟
考試官訓導閔批用事的而立論確當是素抱
經濟大略者
對治世者必審夫善俗之幾而舉夫制變
之要焉天下之生久矣未有無弊之事亦
===
未有無患之時抑豈終無拯之之術與禦
之之法哉亦惟曰深求其故而預爲之備
爾是蓋推之天下而皆然者矧一方乎執
事下詢末學乃有憂於延邵之人才泉漳
之風俗鹽法之困滯貢賦之逋負而於寢
兵郵荒之故尤加之意焉此正愚生之所
欲言也敢舉其詳以對昔胡瑗之在蘇湖
立二齋而法教行陸贄之告德宗用明恕
而訟獄正劉晏出而緡筭增李渤請而攤
banxin: 福建鄉試八十四
punctuated:
時大務，摘發呈露而無餘秘，非胷中素有尺度，疇克有是？㦤古人以匹夫而懷抱天下之憂乎！殆有見乎徒羡讀書。
考試官訓導夏批：考究詳明，議論高遠，真俊傑之士也。他日拜大廷，往以有爲自効於君民者，是用錄之以俟。
考試官訓導閔批：用事的而立論確，當是素抱經濟大略者。
對：治世者必審夫善俗之幾，而舉夫制變之要焉。天下之生久矣，未有無弊之事，亦未有無患之時，抑豈終無拯之之術與禦之之法哉？亦惟曰深求其故，而預爲之備爾。是蓋推之天下而皆然者，矧一方乎？執事下詢末學，乃有憂於延邵之人才、泉漳之風俗、鹽法之困滯、貢賦之逋負，而於寢兵郵荒之故尤加之意焉。此正愚生之所欲言也，敢舉其詳以對。昔胡瑗之在蘇湖，立二齋而法教行；陸贄之告德宗，用明恕而訟獄正；劉晏出而緡筭增；李渤請而攤
translation_en:
…the major affairs of the day: he brings them to light and lays them bare, leaving nothing hidden. Unless he had long possessed sound standards of judgment, who could achieve this? Like the ancients, does he, though a common man, harbor concern for all under Heaven [?]? He seems to possess insight beyond merely admiring book learning [?].
Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: His investigations are detailed and clear, and his arguments lofty and far-reaching. He is truly a man of outstanding talent. In days to come, he will attend the imperial court and go forth to demonstrate his worth through service to ruler and people. Accordingly, we select his essay in anticipation of this.
Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: His use of historical precedents is precise and his arguments sound. He must be someone who has long cherished broad plans for statecraft.
Reply: Those who govern the world must examine the critical opportunities for improving customs and grasp the essentials of responding to change. Human life under Heaven has endured for a long time. There has never been an undertaking free of abuses, nor an age free of troubles. Yet could there ever be no means of remedying them and no method of warding them off? One need only investigate their causes deeply and make preparations beforehand. This holds true throughout the realm; how much more so within a single region!
You, honored officials, have condescended to question this humble student. You express concern about the talent of Yanping and Shaowu, the customs of Quanzhou and Zhangzhou, the difficulties obstructing the salt administration, and arrears in tribute and taxes. You give particular attention to the circumstances of ending warfare and to devastation affecting the postal service [?]. These are precisely the matters that I, an ignorant student, wish to discuss. I venture to set out the details in reply.
Formerly, when Hu Yuan was in Suzhou and Huzhou, he established two instructional divisions, and his methods of teaching were put into practice. When Lu Zhi advised Emperor Dezong, clear judgment and forbearance were employed, and litigation and criminal cases were properly adjudicated. When Liu Yan entered service, monetary revenues increased. Li Bo submitted a petition, and the apportionment…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
逃免龔遂守渤海而盜賊斂趙抃治越州
而荒政脩此皆古人已試之明驗也然時
異世殊而理則可同風漓俗變而法未或
改是以為之制者必審推移之術而示勸
沮之方焉蓋延邵二郡諸賢道學之源遠
矣然猶有置書院以延禮師儒有詣學宮
而親為講授嗣是而首風化者亦嘗倣而
行之耶漳泉之地大儒過化之澤深矣然
猶有閉戶耀以止兄弟之害訐諭大義而
令頑民之自思繼此而柄邦成者亦嘗舉
而措之耶嚴私販之條厲侵奪之禁則夙
弊除而榷利興此其法之大凡爾抑不知
今日鹾務之司塩盜鬻之奸有如當時之
為宣慰者否乎信蠲除之令重乾沒之罰
則民隱通而逋負復此其政之梗槩爾抑
不知今日守牧之任汰虛加之額有如昔
人之為宣撫者否乎是則學之所以廢訟
之所以繁法之所以沮而賦之所以稽負
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 八十五
punctuated:
逃免。龔遂守渤海而盜賊斂，趙抃治越州而荒政脩，此皆古人已試之明驗也。然時異世殊，而理則可同；風漓俗變，而法未或改。是以為之制者，必審推移之術，而示勸沮之方焉。

蓋延邵二郡，諸賢道學之源遠矣，然猶有置書院以延禮師儒，有詣學宮而親為講授。嗣是而首風化者，亦嘗倣而行之耶？漳泉之地，大儒過化之澤深矣，然猶有閉戶耀以止兄弟之害訐，諭大義而令頑民之自思。繼此而柄邦成者，亦嘗舉而措之耶？嚴私販之條，厲侵奪之禁，則夙弊除而榷利興，此其法之大凡爾。抑不知今日鹾務之司，塩盜鬻之奸，有如當時之為宣慰者否乎？信蠲除之令，重乾沒之罰，則民隱通而逋負復，此其政之梗槩爾。抑不知今日守牧之任，汰虛加之額，有如昔人之為宣撫者否乎？是則學之所以廢，訟之所以繁，法之所以沮，而賦之所以稽負
translation_en:
…the levies apportioned to cover absconders’ obligations were remitted. When Gong Sui governed Bohai, bandits curtailed their activities; when Zhao Bian administered Yuezhou, famine relief was put in order. These are all clear proofs of measures already tried by men of earlier times. Yet although times and circumstances differ, the principles may remain the same; although social mores decline and customs change, the methods need not necessarily be altered. Those who devise regulations must therefore carefully consider how to adapt them and make clear the means of encouragement and restraint.

In the two prefectures of Yanping and Shaowu, the Learning of the Way transmitted by worthy scholars has a long history. Yet there were still those who established academies to invite and honor learned teachers, and those who visited the prefectural schools to lecture in person. Have their successors, charged with leading moral transformation, ever imitated and practiced these measures? In Zhangzhou and Quanzhou, the transforming influence of great Confucian scholars who passed through left a profound legacy. Yet there were still those who closed their doors [?] to stop brothers from harming and accusing one another, and who explained the great moral obligations so that obstinate people would reflect for themselves. Have those who subsequently took charge of local government ever adopted and implemented these measures?

Make the provisions against illicit trading strict and enforce the prohibitions against encroachment and seizure: longstanding abuses will then be eliminated and monopoly revenues will flourish. These are merely the broad outlines of the method. Yet I wonder whether those now administering salt affairs deal with fraudulent illicit salt sales [?] as did the Pacification Commissioner (xuanwei) of that time. Faithfully implement orders for tax remission and increase the penalties for embezzlement: the people’s concealed hardships will then become known and arrears will be recovered. These are merely the general outlines of the policy. Yet I wonder whether today’s local administrators eliminate falsely added assessments as did the Pacification Commissioner (xuanfu) of former times. Thus, the reasons why learning has fallen into neglect, litigation has multiplied, regulations have been frustrated, and taxes have fallen into arrears…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
者其原當有所考矣至如遏盜之起救歲
之侵又愚生之所願學者也夫汀漳乃甌
閩之奧引帶贛吉而喉襟潮廣興泉為梯
航之會揭以崇山而巨海敵焉值兵則借
調於鄰藩遇荒則仰給於他郡誠有如執
事之憂者蓋盜賊之禍非一日矣然為今
之計者三總三省之衝置遞戍之鎮以解
其嘯聚割數里之地立撫馭之邑以誘其
向方然必斷以歐文忠所謂州郡設兵為
===
備明賞罰之格選捕盜之官而後為確論
也荒歉之變嘗迭見矣然當今所務者三
放貧民之負復陂渠之業以厚其本務通
海舶之商轉廣東之粟以貿其有無然必
參以呂東萊所謂謹預備之政所在蓄積
有可均處使之流通而後能兼濟也凡此
固所謂舉其要以蓄其備者耳然猶未探
其本也夫天下之情不患於不協而患於
不一天下之風不患其不振而患其不同
banxin: 福建鄉錄 八十六
punctuated: 者，其原當有所考矣。至如遏盜之起、救歲之侵，又愚生之所願學者也。夫汀漳乃甌閩之奧，引帶贛吉，而喉襟潮廣；興泉為梯航之會，揭以崇山，而巨海敵焉。值兵則借調於鄰藩，遇荒則仰給於他郡，誠有如執事之憂者。蓋盜賊之禍非一日矣，然為今之計者三：總三省之衝，置遞戍之鎮，以解其嘯聚；割數里之地，立撫馭之邑，以誘其向方；然必斷以歐文忠所謂州郡設兵為備，明賞罰之格，選捕盜之官，而後為確論也。荒歉之變嘗迭見矣，然當今所務者三：放貧民之負，復陂渠之業，以厚其本務；通海舶之商，轉廣東之粟，以貿其有無；然必參以呂東萊所謂謹預備之政，所在蓄積，有可均處，使之流通，而後能兼濟也。凡此，固所謂舉其要以蓄其備者耳，然猶未探其本也。夫天下之情，不患於不協，而患於不一；天下之風，不患其不振，而患其不同。
translation_en:
…the underlying causes of these matters surely deserve investigation. As for checking the rise of banditry and relieving the ravages of a bad harvest, these too are matters about which I, an unworthy student, wish to learn. Tingzhou and Zhangzhou lie in the interior of Ou and Min, linking Ganzhou and Ji’an and commanding the approaches to Chaozhou and Guangdong. Xinghua and Quanzhou are meeting points for travel by land and sea, with lofty mountains rising above them and the vast sea confronting them. When fighting occurs, troops must be borrowed from neighboring provinces; when famine strikes, supplies must be sought from other prefectures. There is indeed cause for the concerns you have expressed.

The scourge of banditry has certainly not arisen in a single day. For the present, however, there are three measures to consider. Take unified control of the strategic approaches of the three provinces and establish a military post with rotating garrisons, to break up the bandits’ gatherings. Carve out a tract of several li and establish a county to pacify and govern them, encouraging them to turn toward proper conduct. Yet a sound proposal must ultimately be grounded in what Ouyang Wenzhong—that is, Ouyang Xiu—advocated: stationing troops in prefectures as a precaution, making the rules for rewards and punishments clear, and selecting officials to apprehend bandits.

Calamitous crop failures have likewise occurred repeatedly. Here too, three tasks demand attention today. Cancel the debts of the poor and restore reservoirs and irrigation channels, thereby strengthening their fundamental occupation of agriculture. Open maritime trade and transport grain from Guangdong, so that places with surpluses and shortages may exchange supplies. Yet these measures must also incorporate what Lü Donglai—that is, Lü Zuqian—advocated: carefully maintaining a policy of advance preparation, accumulating reserves everywhere, and ensuring their circulation wherever supplies can be equitably shared. Only then can relief reach all.

All these measures amount merely to identifying the essentials and laying in preparations; they still do not reach the root of the matter. As for the dispositions of people throughout the realm, the concern is not that they fail to accord, but that they lack unity; as for the prevailing customs of the realm, the concern is not that they lack vigor, but that they are not uniform.

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
先王之世學不雜而才愈多刑不繁而姦
自伏民緩其末而勤於其上化以行而俗
以美夫豈多術哉誠以夸毗偷惰之習不
作而恭儉卑巽之懿興也是故道德者先
王所以一其情而同其俗者也而夫子論
政必以德禮先焉當是時也必有嚴其制
而謹為之防使佻淫不得以相扇貧富不
得以相耀回其心以向於道然後士一其
業民一其務頹風振而和氣臻刑罰省盜
===
賊息而年穀蕃育矣嗚呼十室之邑必有
忠信況閩舊齒
上國而乃無可語者乎先正有言不能行諸天
下猶可驗諸一方惟執事者念之士庶幸
甚謹對
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 八十七
punctuated:
先王之世，學不雜而才愈多，刑不繁而姦自伏，民緩其末而勤於其上，化以行而俗以美。夫豈多術哉？誠以夸毗偷惰之習不作，而恭儉卑巽之懿興也。是故道德者，先王所以一其情而同其俗者也。而夫子論政，必以德禮先焉。當是時也，必有嚴其制而謹為之防，使佻淫不得以相扇，貧富不得以相耀，回其心以向於道，然後士一其業，民一其務，頹風振而和氣臻，刑罰省，盜賊息，而年穀蕃育矣。
嗚呼！十室之邑，必有忠信，況閩舊齒上國，而乃無可語者乎？先正有言：「不能行諸天下，猶可驗諸一方。」惟執事者念之，士庶幸甚。謹對。
translation_en:
In the age of the former kings, learning was unmixed, yet men of talent grew ever more numerous; punishments were not numerous, yet wrongdoers submitted of themselves. The people gave less attention to secondary pursuits and diligently served their superiors. Moral transformation thus took effect, and customs became admirable. Did this require many methods? It was truly because habits of flattery, negligence, and indolence did not arise, while the virtues of reverence, frugality, humility, and deference flourished. Thus moral virtue was the means by which the former kings unified the people's dispositions and brought their customs into accord. When Confucius discussed government, he invariably gave precedence to virtue and ritual propriety. In the present age, there must be those who make regulations strict and carefully establish safeguards, so that frivolity and excess cannot spread through mutual incitement, and rich and poor cannot vie in ostentatious display. They must turn people's hearts toward the Way. Only then will scholars devote themselves single-mindedly to their studies and the common people to their occupations; declining customs will revive and harmonious influences will arrive. Punishments will diminish, banditry will cease, and grain will flourish in the fields.
Alas! Even in a hamlet of ten households there are surely people who are loyal and trustworthy. How much more must this be true of Fujian, which has long ranked among the civilized regions of the realm! Could there really be no one there with whom these matters can be discussed? A worthy predecessor said: “What cannot be put into practice throughout the world may still be tested in a single region.” If only you gentlemen charged with these affairs would consider this, scholars and commoners alike would be most fortunate. Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄後序
正德十有一年秋八月福建
鄉試錄成巡按福建監察御
史胡文靜暨藩臬諸司之承
事于位者肆而觀之胥作而
嘆曰眞哉才閩於今為盛乎
亨惟天之降才固有不同哉
===
肪之玉鏐鐐之金翬雉之絲
丹砂石弩齒毛漆枲之利具
之質而辯其品皆是物也世
之因而資之者取無窮而用
無竭而凡於物者固有擇爾
其於才也亦然粹雅者其才
純凝整者其才正節且固者
banxin: 福建鄉試錄後序 一
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄後序

正德十有一年秋八月，福建鄉試錄成。巡按福建監察御史胡文靜暨藩臬諸司之承事于位者，肆而觀之，胥作而嘆曰：「眞哉，才！閩於今為盛乎！」

亨惟天之降才，固有不同哉！肪之玉，鏐鐐之金，翬雉之絲，丹砂、石弩、齒毛、漆枲之利，具之質而辯其品，皆是物也。世之因而資之者，取無窮而用無竭。而凡於物者，固有擇爾，其於才也亦然。粹雅者，其才純；凝整者，其才正；節且固者，
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

In autumn, in the eighth month of the eleventh year of Zhengde [1516], the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination was completed. Hu Wenjing, Regional Inspector of Fujian and Investigating Censor, together with the officials serving in the Provincial Administration Commission, the Provincial Surveillance Commission, and the other offices, spread it out and examined it. They all rose and exclaimed, “True talent indeed! How abundant it is in Fujian today!”

I, Heng, reflect that the talents Heaven bestows certainly differ. There is jade like mutton fat; precious metal such as fine gold and silver; silk patterned like pheasants; and useful products such as cinnabar, stone crossbows [?], ivory and feathers, lacquer and hemp. Considering their substance and distinguishing their grades [?], these are all material things. People draw upon them for their needs, taking from them without limit and using them without exhaustion. Yet with material things there is necessarily a process of selection; so it is also with talent. Those who are refined and elegant possess pure talent; those who are composed and orderly possess upright talent; those who are principled and steadfast …

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
其才庀以深碩且慧者其才
茂以達決者才肆而蕩者才
靡情淵外飭君子有遺貌焉
由往古而考之昔高陽氏之
才八高辛氏之才八而天下
皆謂之才曠百世而下惟鄒
魯近樸而燕趙多奇又其最
===
後往往有借才之嘆大抵利
功勝矣
國家掄才之科凡三歲一舉其
數特異海內之士有文武忠
孝之譽彌綸天地之道去此
將無由以達況夫全閩衣冠
之舊先作胤述有若恒産閥
banxin: 福建鄉試錄後序 二
punctuated:
其才庀以深；碩且慧者，其才茂以達；決者才肆，而蕩者才靡。情淵外飭，君子有遺貌焉。由往古而考之，昔高陽氏之才八，高辛氏之才八，而天下皆謂之才。曠百世而下，惟鄒魯近樸，而燕趙多奇。又其最後，往往有借才之嘆，大抵利功勝矣。
國家掄才之科，凡三歲一舉，其數特異。海內之士，有文武忠孝之譽、彌綸天地之道，去此將無由以達。況夫全閩衣冠之舊，先作胤述，有若恒産閥
translation_en:
…their talents are ample [?] and deep; those who are substantial and discerning have talents that flourish and reach far; the decisive display their talents freely, while the unrestrained dissipate theirs. With inward feelings profound and outward conduct well ordered, the gentleman has qualities that appearances fail to convey [?]. Looking back into antiquity, there were eight talented men under Gaoyang and eight under Gaoxin, and all under Heaven acknowledged their talent. Across the hundred generations that followed, Zou and Lu were especially close to simplicity, while Yan and Zhao abounded in extraordinary men. Still later, there were often laments about borrowing talent; on the whole, considerations of profit and achievement had come to prevail.
The state holds its examinations for selecting talent once every three years, with particularly distinctive arrangements [?]. Scholars throughout the realm who enjoy reputations for civil and military accomplishments, loyalty and filial devotion, and who possess the Way that comprehends Heaven and Earth, would have no avenue to advancement apart from these examinations. How much more is this so in Fujian, with its longstanding families of scholars and officials, whose forebears initiated endeavors and whose descendants carried them on, as though they possessed an enduring patrimony, eminent lineages [?]…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
傑竒瓖而黼黻當世固自有
士然就諸子今日所能而觀
之叙大業則正君心而釐國
是語朝著則列忠義而黜奸
諛警郡邑則首循謹而屏苛
墨磨礱淹貫之抱雄渾宏富
之氣皆於文乎發之然諸子
豈徒致其才於文而已其將
有先天下而憂者焉矧我
國家養士之法復古庠序之制
郡縣鄉社莫不有學士于其
間藏脩而游息焉者無或他
技六藝之尊蓋百五十年于
茲未之或改也諸士子涵育
banxin: 福建鄉試錄後序 三
punctuated: 傑竒瓖而黼黻當世，固自有士。然就諸子今日所能而觀之，叙大業則正君心而釐國是，語朝著則列忠義而黜奸諛，警郡邑則首循謹而屏苛墨。磨礱淹貫之抱，雄渾宏富之氣，皆於文乎發之。然諸子豈徒致其才於文而已？其將有先天下而憂者焉。矧我國家養士之法，復古庠序之制，郡縣鄉社莫不有學。士于其間藏脩而游息焉者，無或他技，六藝之尊，蓋百五十年于茲，未之或改也。諸士子涵育
translation_en:
… outstanding men of extraordinary worth [?] who lend lustre to the present age: there have certainly been such scholars. Yet, judging by the abilities you gentlemen have displayed today, when discussing the great undertaking of government, you advocate rectifying the ruler’s mind and setting national policy aright; when speaking of the ranks at court, you advocate advancing the loyal and righteous and dismissing the treacherous and flattering; when admonishing prefectural and county administrations, you give priority to conscientious, circumspect officials and exclude the harsh and corrupt. Your aspirations, refined through sustained study and informed by comprehensive learning, and your vigorous, expansive spirit all find expression in your writing. But can you gentlemen intend merely to display your talents in literary composition? Surely among you there will be those who take upon themselves the world’s cares before others do.
Moreover, our dynasty’s methods of nurturing scholars have restored the ancient system of schools: prefectures, counties, townships, and communities all have schools. The scholars who study and cultivate themselves there, at leisure as well as at work, pursue no other arts. The honoured position of the Six Arts has remained unchanged for some hundred and fifty years down to the present. You scholars have been nurtured …

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
聖化旣專且久行將進于春官敭
于
大庭而效其用於四方代工成
務以開太平於無窮者必有
眞才焉出無亦於九十人者
占之亨猥以文辭爲職而濫
論士之請於卒事也因致望
===
焉
河南河南府洛陽縣儒學訓
導夏亨謹序
banxin: 福建鄕試錄後序 四
punctuated:
聖化旣專且久，行將進于春官，敭于大庭，而效其用於四方，代工成務，以開太平於無窮者，必有眞才焉出，無亦於九十人者占之？亨猥以文辭爲職，而濫論士之請，於卒事也，因致望焉。
河南河南府洛陽縣儒學訓導夏亨謹序。
translation_en:
…having received the sage ruler’s transforming influence so exclusively and for so long, they will soon advance to the Ministry of Rites and distinguish themselves at the imperial court, putting their abilities to use throughout the realm. Among those who discharge duties on the ruler’s behalf and accomplish affairs, thereby ushering in peace for all time, men of true talent will surely emerge. Might we not look for them among these ninety men? I, Heng, unworthily make literary composition my occupation and have presumptuously discussed the scholars’ request [?]. Now that the work is completed, I therefore express these hopes for them.
Preface respectfully written by Xia Heng, Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan.

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
正德十一年福建鄉試錄
正德十一年福建鄉試錄
正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄序
聖天子御極之十有一年是爲丙
子天下復當賓興之期福建
藩司舉行如制巡按監察御
史胡文靜寔柄其事而臨焉
初藩司以禮聘考試官請則
既曰諾宜重幣以往繼又曰
===
閩大藩也塲屋湫隘待士之
制未稱乃檄所司斥公帑之
餘新之凡一切條貫罔有不
悉心綜理者于時鎮守福建
太監崔安提督市舶太監尚
春皆雅重儒術協規相成而
總理閩浙鹾政左副都御史
banxin: 福建鄉試錄前序 一
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄序

聖天子御極之十有一年，是爲丙子，天下復當賓興之期。福建藩司舉行如制，巡按監察御史胡文靜寔柄其事而臨焉。初，藩司以禮聘考試官請，則既曰：「諾，宜重幣以往。」繼又曰：「閩大藩也，塲屋湫隘，待士之制未稱。」乃檄所司，斥公帑之餘新之。凡一切條貫，罔有不悉心綜理者。于時，鎮守福建太監崔安、提督市舶太監尚春，皆雅重儒術，協規相成。而總理閩浙鹾政左副都御史
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

The eleventh year since our sagely Son of Heaven ascended the throne was the bingzi year [1516], when the time once again came throughout the realm to select worthy men through the examinations. The Fujian Provincial Administration Commission conducted the examination according to the regulations. Hu Wenjing, the Regional Inspector serving as Investigating Censor, took charge of its affairs and supervised it. Initially, when the Provincial Administration Commission sought his approval to invite Examiners with due ceremony, he said: “Yes. Substantial gifts should accompany the invitation.” He then added: “Min [Fujian] is a major province, yet its examination compound is low-lying and cramped. These arrangements for receiving scholars are inadequate.” He therefore issued orders to the responsible offices to use surplus public funds to renovate it. There was no aspect of the regulations and arrangements that he did not administer with the utmost care.

At that time, Cui An, the Grand Eunuch stationed in Fujian, and Shang Chun, the Grand Eunuch supervising maritime trade, both held Confucian learning in high esteem and worked together in planning and carrying out the undertaking. And the Left Vice Censor-in-Chief administering the salt administration of Fujian and Zhejiang …

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
陳天祥巡撫汀漳諸郡右僉
都御史文森清戎監察御史
王應鵬南京督税戸部員外郎
徐度各以事蒞閩惟是作興
士類爲務士益爭自淬礪以
躍以奮既八月魯等亦應聘
而集御史文靜遂偕入塲屋
===
以魯與訓導夏亨爲考試官
學正陳仲珠胡希銓教諭吳
瑛閻志學吳鎧杜鸞沈磐訓
導徐衍爲同考試官提調則
左布政使伍符右布政使姚
鏌監試則按察使王金僉事
胡鐸賛襄防範于外則左叅
banxin: 福建鄉試錄前序 二
punctuated: 陳天祥、巡撫汀漳諸郡右僉都御史文森、清戎監察御史王應鵬、南京督税戸部員外郎徐度，各以事蒞閩，惟是作興士類爲務。士益爭自淬礪，以躍以奮。既八月，魯等亦應聘而集，御史文靜遂偕入塲屋，以魯與訓導夏亨爲考試官，學正陳仲珠、胡希銓，教諭吳瑛、閻志學、吳鎧、杜鸞、沈磐，訓導徐衍爲同考試官。提調則左布政使伍符、右布政使姚鏌；監試則按察使王金、僉事胡鐸；賛襄防範于外則左叅
translation_en:
… Chen Tianxiang; Wen Sen, Right Assistant Censor-in-chief and Grand Coordinator of Tingzhou, Zhangzhou, and the other prefectures; Wang Yingpeng, Investigating Censor charged with inspecting military affairs; and Xu Du, Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue at Nanjing charged with supervising taxation, each came to Fujian on official business. All made encouraging and fostering the scholars their principal concern. The scholars competed ever more earnestly to hone themselves, eager to rise and distinguish themselves.

When the eighth month arrived, Lu and the others also assembled in response to their invitations. Censor Wen Jing then entered the examination compound with them. Lu and Xia Heng, an Assistant Instructor, were appointed Examiners. Chen Zhongzhu and Hu Xiquan, School Instructors; Wu Ying, Yan Zhixue, Wu Kai, Du Luan, and Shen Pan, Instructors; and Xu Yan, an Assistant Instructor, were appointed Associate Examiners. The Proctors were Wu Fu, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Yao Mo, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner. Wang Jin, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Hu Duo, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, supervised the examination. Assisting with security and precautions outside the compound were the Left Administration Vice …

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
政陳策右參政艾洪左參議
彭夔右參議鄭毅副使陳懷
經唐澤僉事蔡天祐查約胡
璉趙官署都指揮僉事楊勳
李胤而下及內外百執事皆
選諸有司之良無濫預者如
期乃合提學副使劉玉所取
===
列郡士而三試之惟嚴惟慎
惟公且加詳焉遵
制額拔其尤者得九十人幷擇
其文二十一篇為錄以
獻以傳魯當序諸首簡維閩有
場屋舊矣初建於會城之南
旋病其陋已再徙今復病其
banxin: 福建鄉試錄前序 三
punctuated:
政陳策、右參政艾洪、左參議彭夔、右參議鄭毅、副使陳懷經、唐澤、僉事蔡天祐、查約、胡璉、趙官、署都指揮僉事楊勳、李胤，而下及內外百執事，皆選諸有司之良，無濫預者。如期乃合提學副使劉玉所取列郡士而三試之，惟嚴惟慎，惟公且加詳焉。遵制額，拔其尤者，得九十人，幷擇其文二十一篇為錄，以獻以傳。魯當序諸首簡。
維閩有場屋舊矣。初建於會城之南，旋病其陋，已再徙，今復病其
translation_en:
…Left Administration Vice Commissioner Chen Ce, Right Administration Vice Commissioner Ai Hong, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner Peng Kui, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner Zheng Yi, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Chen Huaijing and Tang Ze, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Cai Tianyou, Zha Yue, Hu Lian, and Zhao Guan, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Yang Xun and Li Yin. Down through all the functionaries serving inside and outside the examination compound, everyone was selected from the capable men of the responsible offices; none was admitted indiscriminately. At the appointed time, the candidates from the various prefectures selected by Education Intendant and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Liu Yu were assembled and examined in three sessions. The proceedings were rigorous, cautious, impartial, and especially thorough. In accordance with the quota prescribed by imperial command, ninety of the most outstanding candidates were selected. Twenty-one of their essays were also chosen for a record, to be presented to the throne and circulated. It fell to me, Lu, to write the preface at the beginning of the volume.
Fujian has long had an examination compound. It was first built south of the provincial capital, but its inadequacy soon became a concern. It has already been relocated twice, and now there is again concern about its…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
未廣也乃加闢焉門庭宏邃
棟宇壯傑而丹臒炳炳交輝
新規旣拓舊構復華觀者罔
不動容屬目以爲塲屋之觀
其備於是乎然則天下之事
耻冗近而嚮高明厭卑小而
慕遠大蓋亦莫不有然者矣
===
即以閩士言之秦漢以來固
未齒於上國唐時歐陽詹以
文辭名林蘊以忠義著而閩
士寖以有聞然未徵於事功
而無考於道德亦猶夫故耳
未也歷唐至北宋有楊文公
之詞藻有曾公亮之簡靜有
banxin: 福建鄕試錄前序 四
punctuated:
未廣也，乃加闢焉。門庭宏邃，棟宇壯傑，而丹臒炳炳交輝。新規旣拓，舊構復華，觀者罔不動容屬目，以爲塲屋之觀，其備於是乎！然則天下之事，耻冗近而嚮高明，厭卑小而慕遠大，蓋亦莫不有然者矣。

即以閩士言之，秦漢以來，固未齒於上國。唐時歐陽詹以文辭名，林蘊以忠義著，而閩士寖以有聞。然未徵於事功，而無考於道德，亦猶夫故耳。未也，歷唐至北宋，有楊文公之詞藻，有曾公亮之簡靜，有
translation_en:
…was not spacious enough, so it was further enlarged. Its gates and courtyards are imposing and deep, its halls and roof beams magnificent, and its vermilion decoration [?] shines brilliantly, each part reflecting the others. The new layout has been extended, and the old buildings have regained their splendor. None who see it fail to be moved and gaze intently, thinking: “Surely the magnificence of an examination compound has now reached its fullness!” Thus, in the affairs of the world, people are ashamed of the commonplace and the limited and aspire to the lofty and enlightened; they tire of the lowly and small and yearn for the far-reaching and great. Surely this tendency is universal.

Take the scholars of Fujian as an example. Since Qin and Han times, they had certainly not ranked alongside those of the central regions. Under the Tang, Ouyang Zhan became renowned for his literary compositions, and Lin Yun distinguished himself through loyalty and righteousness; Fujian scholars gradually became known. Yet their accomplishments had not been demonstrated in practical affairs, nor was there evidence by which to assess their attainment in the Way and virtue: things remained much as before. This was not yet enough. Passing from the Tang to the Northern Song, there were Yang Wengong’s literary brilliance and Zeng Gongliang’s unassuming composure, and there was …

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
蔡君謨之惠政有陳述古諸
先生之講授而閩之人物所
謂文學也事功道德也皆彬
彬日趨於美矣而猶未也厥
後李忠定者起遂以相業偉
一世翹然負古大臣之望龜
山身游程門載道而南一時
===
唱和率稱大儒沿至考亭朱
子遂集羣儒之大成用其功
與夫子並居名闕里俗號鄒
魯而武夷雲谷諸峯攢翠聳
碧峩峩然與龜蒙鳬繹相高
游覽於建溪清源之勝者亦
真若浴沂水而挹春風也事
banxin: 福建鄉試錄前序 五
punctuated: 蔡君謨之惠政，有陳述古諸先生之講授，而閩之人物，所謂文學也、事功道德也，皆彬彬日趨於美矣。而猶未也。厥後李忠定者起，遂以相業偉一世，翹然負古大臣之望。龜山身游程門，載道而南，一時唱和，率稱大儒。沿至考亭朱子，遂集羣儒之大成，用其功與夫子並。居名闕里，俗號鄒魯，而武夷、雲谷諸峯攢翠聳碧，峩峩然與龜蒙鳬繹相高。游覽於建溪、清源之勝者，亦真若浴沂水而挹春風也。事
translation_en: …the benevolent administration of Cai Junmo, and the teaching of such masters as Chen Shugu. Thus, among Fujian’s eminent men, literary learning, practical achievements, and moral cultivation all flourished in increasing refinement. Yet this was still not the culmination. Thereafter arose Li Zhongding, whose accomplishments as chief councillor made him outstanding in his age; preeminent, he bore the reputation of a great minister of antiquity. Guishan personally studied in the school of the Cheng masters and carried the Way southward. Those who joined in this intellectual exchange at the time were generally acclaimed as great Confucian scholars. This development continued down to Master Zhu of Kaoting, who brought together the achievements of the many Confucian scholars into a grand synthesis, his contribution thereby ranking alongside that of Confucius. His dwelling was called Queli, and the region’s customs were likened to those of Zou and Lu. The peaks of Wuyi and Yungu, clustered in emerald green and towering in blue-green majesty, rivaled the heights of Gui, Meng, Fu, and Yi. Those touring the scenic places of Jianxi and Qingyuan truly felt as though they were bathing in the Yi River and taking in the spring breeze. Practical achievements…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
功德學之盛皆所謂宏以邃
傑以壯者而雄跨百代矣世
寧有不瞻而仰之者哉閩人
之觀不至是始備哉入我
國朝如張翠屏楊文敏林莊敏
彭惠安諸名公相繼而起是
則所謂華舊構者也流聲實
===
於天下者也其於閩不重有
光哉諸士子登名斯錄皆閩
之俊而亦
國家所養育以待用者其將何
以為謀哉夫自吾之筮仕而
至於為大夫為卿佐為宰輔
位之不同而皆有事業之期
banxin: 福建鄉試錄前序 六
punctuated:
功德學之盛，皆所謂宏以邃、傑以壯者，而雄跨百代矣。世寧有不瞻而仰之者哉？閩人之觀，不至是始備哉？入我國朝，如張翠屏、楊文敏、林莊敏、彭惠安諸名公，相繼而起，是則所謂華舊構者也，流聲實於天下者也。其於閩，不重有光哉？
諸士子登名斯錄，皆閩之俊，而亦國家所養育以待用者，其將何以為謀哉？夫自吾之筮仕，而至於為大夫、為卿佐、為宰輔，位之不同，而皆有事業之期
translation_en:
…The flourishing of achievements, virtue, and learning—all exemplify what is called breadth joined with depth, distinction joined with grandeur—and tower above a hundred generations. Could anyone in the world fail to look upon them with admiration? Is it not only at this point that a view of the people of Min becomes complete? Under our dynasty, such eminent men as Zhang Cuiping, Yang Wenmin, Lin Zhuangmin, and Peng Hui’an have arisen in succession. These are men who, as the saying goes, embellish the old edifice, spreading their reputation and substantial accomplishments throughout the realm. Have they not brought renewed glory to Min?
The scholars whose names appear in this record are all outstanding men of Min, nurtured by the state in readiness for service. What plans, then, will they make? From our first entry into office to becoming grand masters, ministers and their assistants, or chief ministers, our ranks differ, yet at every level there is the expectation of accomplishment…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
焉必求以日新難也自吾之
家之一鄉以至於一國天下
與後世地之不同而皆有名
稱之繫焉必求以自立又難
也諸士子其得不益慎於所
習益勤於所事以為邦邑重
且以副主司望哉昔孔融論
===
東南之美謂會稽竹箭不足
以當之而歸諸季札虞翻二
子融言人材為山川應可也
謂其盡於二子非矣然則八
閩之靈之秀諸士子固當有
繼起而乗之者豈先正之所
能專哉蘇穎濱上韓太尉書
banxin: 福建鄉試錄前序 七
punctuated: 焉，必求以日新，難也。自吾之家之一鄉，以至於一國、天下與後世，地之不同，而皆有名稱之繫焉，必求以自立，又難也。諸士子其得不益慎於所習，益勤於所事，以為邦邑重，且以副主司望哉？昔孔融論東南之美，謂會稽竹箭不足以當之，而歸諸季札、虞翻二子。融言人材為山川應，可也；謂其盡於二子，非矣。然則八閩之靈之秀，諸士子固當有繼起而乗之者，豈先正之所能專哉？蘇穎濱《上韓太尉書》
translation_en:
…and to insist on renewing oneself daily is difficult. From one’s household to one’s home district, and thence to the entire realm, all under Heaven, and later generations, the spheres differ, yet one’s reputation is bound up with them all. To insist on establishing oneself is difficult as well. Can you scholars, then, fail to become still more careful in what you study and still more diligent in what you undertake, so as to bring distinction to your native places and fulfill the expectations of the presiding examiners?

Kong Rong once discussed the finest things of the southeast. He said that the bamboo arrow shafts of Kuaiji did not suffice to deserve that description, and instead bestowed it upon the two men Ji Zha and Yu Fan. Rong was right to say that human talent arises in response to the mountains and rivers; he was wrong to say that it was exhausted in these two men. Thus, among you scholars there surely must be those who will rise in succession to inherit the numinous excellence of the Eight Min regions of Fujian. How could the worthy predecessors possess it exclusively? In Su Yingbin’s “Letter Presented to Defender-in-Chief Han”…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
謂見歐陽子固已為愜猶以
未見太尉為恨此頴濱之善
於求天下之大觀也諸士子
疇昔所慕必嘗動高山之仰
毋亦有舍歐陽而慕稚圭者
乎魯於諸士子既以文字相
知矣然欲進諸士子於道誠
===
不能貢諛言為悅也故特用
其所以忠告者而諄諄焉
浙江寧波府慈谿縣儒學訓
導閔魯謹序
banxin: 福建鄉試錄前序 八
punctuated:
謂見歐陽子，固已為愜，猶以未見太尉為恨。此頴濱之善於求天下之大觀也。諸士子疇昔所慕，必嘗動高山之仰，毋亦有舍歐陽而慕稚圭者乎？魯於諸士子，既以文字相知矣，然欲進諸士子於道，誠不能貢諛言為悅也。故特用其所以忠告者而諄諄焉。
浙江寧波府慈谿縣儒學訓導閔魯謹序。
translation_en:
…said that meeting Master Ouyang had indeed already brought him satisfaction, yet he still regretted not having met the Defender-in-Chief. This shows Yingbin’s skill in seeking out the grand sights of the world. Among those whom you candidates have long admired, surely some have inspired the reverence felt when gazing up at a lofty mountain. Might there also be some among you who turn from Ouyang to admire Zhigui [Han Qi]? I, Lu, have already come to know you candidates through your writing. Yet, wishing to advance you along the Way, I truly cannot offer flattering words merely to please you. Thus I have spoken earnestly and at length, offering you my sincere counsel.
Preface respectfully written by Min Lu, Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang.

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:

福建等處承宣布政使司左布政使伍符〔朝信江西安福縣人丁未進士〕

河南河南府洛陽縣儒學訓導夏亨〔本元陝西咸寧縣人癸酉貢士〕

河南開封府睢州儒學學正陳仲珠〔永輝浙江諸暨縣人庚午貢士〕
河南汝州儒學學正胡希銓〔克脩江西弋陽縣人庚午貢士〕

江西饒州府餘干縣儒學教諭吳鎧〔廷儀湖廣武陵縣人丙午貢士〕
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 一
punctuated:
正德十一年福建鄉試

監臨官
巡按福建監察御史胡文靜〔士寧，浙江山陰縣人，戊辰進士〕。

福建等處承宣布政使司左布政使伍符〔朝信，江西安福縣人，丁未進士〕。福建等處承宣布政使司右布政使姚鏌〔英之，浙江慈谿縣人，癸丑進士〕。

福建等處提刑按察司按察使王金〔曰良，河南臨潁縣人，壬戌進士〕。福建等處提刑按察司僉事胡鐸〔時振，浙江餘姚縣人，乙丑進士〕。

浙江寧波府慈谿縣儒學訓導閔魯〔宗道，江西南昌縣人，庚午貢士〕。河南河南府洛陽縣儒學訓導夏亨〔本元，陝西咸寧縣人，癸酉貢士〕。

河南開封府睢州儒學學正陳仲珠〔永輝，浙江諸暨縣人，庚午貢士〕。河南汝州儒學學正胡希銓〔克脩，江西弋陽縣人，庚午貢士〕。浙江紹興府餘姚縣儒學教諭吳瑛〔廷粲，南京錦衣衛人，甲子貢士〕。直隸鎮江府丹陽縣儒學教諭閻志學〔汝遜，直隸淶水縣人，丁卯貢士〕。江西饒州府餘干縣儒學教諭吳鎧〔廷儀，湖廣武陵縣人，丙午貢士〕。
translation_en:
Fujian Provincial Examination, eleventh year of Zhengde (1516)

Supervising Official
Hu Wenjing, Regional Inspecting Censor for Fujian, courtesy name Shining, was from Shanyin County, Zhejiang, and became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the wuchen year.

Chen Zhongzhu, Instructor at the Confucian School of Sui Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, courtesy name Yonghui, was from Zhuji County, Zhejiang, and became a tribute student in the gengwu year.

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
河南南陽府鄧州新野縣儒學教諭杜鸞〔文輝四川成都府華陽縣人庚午貢士〕
山西太原府平定州樂平縣儒學教諭沈磐〔仲鎭廣西慶遠衛人丁卯貢士〕
浙江嚴州府遂安縣儒學訓導徐衎〔天和廣東揭陽縣人庚午貢士〕
印卷官
福建等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷顏玉〔德純廣西永淳縣人壬子貢士〕
福建等處提刑按察司經歷司知事曾綱〔弘繩廣東潮陽縣人監生〕

福建都轉運鹽使司運使黃衷〔子和廣東南海縣人丙辰進士〕

延平府知府姜文魁〔士元江西進賢縣人丙辰進士〕

banxin: 福建鄉試錄二
punctuated:
