title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
瞻之在前忽焉在後
朱淛
同考試官教諭吳批論語一題作者不泛則滯明贍
詳整如此篇者詎可得耶錄之不專以其文爾
同考試官學正胡批述先難之故萬世如見亦善發
顏子之蘊者乎
考試官訓導夏批辭副乎理邃於文者
===
考試官訓導閔批渾厚醇粹大非他作所及
大賢之嘆聖道擬之而不可為象也蓋道有可
象非道之妙也然則聖人之道大賢亦安能遽
得其象於前後之間也哉昔顏子學既有得述
其先難之故而嘆之至此若曰吾夫子之聖也
其見諸身固無適而非道而其為道也亦何往
而非妙哉故方吾求道之初欲有以彷佛之也
而極目以瞻之徘徊之際亦嘗會無形於有形
宛與我而相值焉欲有以擬議之也而凝眸以
banxin: 福建鄉試錄二十二
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「瞻之在前，忽焉在後。」

朱淛

同考試官教諭吳批：「論語一題，作者不泛則滯。明贍詳整如此篇者，詎可得耶？錄之不專以其文爾。」

同考試官學正胡批：「述先難之故，萬世如見，亦善發顏子之蘊者乎！」

考試官訓導夏批：「辭副乎理，邃於文者。」

考試官訓導閔批：「渾厚醇粹，大非他作所及。」

大賢之嘆聖道，擬之而不可為象也。蓋道有可象，非道之妙也。然則聖人之道，大賢亦安能遽得其象於前後之間也哉？昔顏子學既有得，述其先難之故，而嘆之至此。若曰：吾夫子之聖也，其見諸身，固無適而非道；而其為道也，亦何往而非妙哉？故方吾求道之初，欲有以彷佛之也，而極目以瞻之。徘徊之際，亦嘗會無形於有形，宛與我而相值焉。欲有以擬議之也，而凝眸以
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“I look for it ahead; suddenly it is behind.”

Zhu Zhe 朱淛

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “On this topic from the Analects, writers tend either to be vague or to become bogged down. Where could one find another essay as lucid, ample, thorough, and orderly as this? It is not solely for its literary qualities that I have selected it.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, School Instructor: “He recounts the reasons for the initial difficulties so vividly that readers through ten thousand generations might witness them. Does he not also excel at bringing out the depths of Master Yan’s thought!”

Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: “The language accords with the principle: here is a writer deeply versed in literary composition.”

Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: “Substantial and profound, refined and pure—far beyond the reach of other compositions.”

The great worthy’s sigh over the sage’s Way arose because, though he sought to conceive it, he could not give it an image. For whatever in the Way can be represented is not its subtle essence. How, then, could even the great worthy readily grasp an image of the sage’s Way somewhere between what lies ahead and what lies behind? Long ago, when Master Yan had already gained something through learning, he recounted the reasons for his initial difficulties, and his sigh reached this point. It was as if he said: “Such is the sageliness of our Master that, as manifested in his person, it is everywhere the Way; and as for that Way, where is it not subtle and wondrous? Thus, when I first sought the Way, I wished to gain some likeness of it and strained my eyes to look for it. Amid my lingering search, I did at times apprehend the formless within the formed, as though it had come face to face with me. I wished to conceive and consider it, and fixed my gaze in order to…”

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
視之俯仰之餘亦嘗契無象於有象恍與我而
相參焉就之若見其可親也嚮之若見其可往
也而夫子之道有著於吾前矣據之若見其可
守也憑之若見其可依也而夫子之道有形於
吾目矣夫瞻之在前吾以道在是矣然力未及
於精詳也而已遽失其似時方屬於頃刻也而
已遂忘其初向之彷彿而在前者忽焉復在吾
之後相值也卒與我而相違悵悵然徒自立於
混茫之地顧何所親而亦何所往耶向之擬議
===
而在前者忽焉又出吾之後相參也竟與我而
相失皇皇然徒自處於蒙昧之所將孰爲守而
亦孰爲依耶是則在前而又在後若得而又若
遺恍惚不可爲象如此是可以易心求之哉雖
然聖人可學而至也畏其難而自沮可乎由博
文約禮循序而進以至欲罷不能既竭吾才則
卓爾之域可馴致矣此顏子已試之明驗也先
儒謂顏子發聖人之蘊敎萬世無窮其此章之
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 二十三
punctuated: 視之，俯仰之餘，亦嘗契無象於有象，恍與我而相參焉。就之，若見其可親也；嚮之，若見其可往也，而夫子之道有著於吾前矣。據之，若見其可守也；憑之，若見其可依也，而夫子之道有形於吾目矣。夫瞻之在前，吾以道在是矣。然力未及於精詳也，而已遽失其似；時方屬於頃刻也，而已遂忘其初。向之彷彿而在前者，忽焉復在吾之後，相值也，卒與我而相違。悵悵然徒自立於混茫之地，顧何所親，而亦何所往耶？向之擬議而在前者，忽焉又出吾之後，相參也，竟與我而相失。皇皇然徒自處於蒙昧之所，將孰爲守，而亦孰爲依耶？是則在前而又在後，若得而又若遺，恍惚不可爲象如此，是可以易心求之哉？雖然，聖人可學而至也，畏其難而自沮，可乎？由博文約禮，循序而進，以至欲罷不能，既竭吾才，則卓爾之域可馴致矣。此顏子已試之明驗也。先儒謂顏子發聖人之蘊，敎萬世無窮，其此章之
translation_en:
…gaze upon it. As I looked down and up, I too once apprehended the formless through what had form, as though it were joining with me. Approaching it, I seemed to see something I could draw close to; turning toward it, I seemed to see somewhere I could proceed. Thus the Master's Way became manifest before me. Taking hold of it, I seemed to see something I could preserve; leaning upon it, I seemed to see something I could rely on. Thus the Master's Way took shape before my eyes. Gazing upon it ahead, I supposed that the Way was there. Yet before my efforts could attain precision and thoroughness, I had suddenly lost its semblance; scarcely a moment had passed, and already I had lost my initial apprehension. What had seemed indistinctly present before me suddenly appeared behind me again. What had met with me ultimately drew away from me. Disconsolate, I stood alone in a realm of confusion: what could I draw close to, and where could I proceed? What I had sought to conceive and discuss as being before me suddenly emerged behind me again. What had seemed to join with me ultimately slipped away from me. Bewildered, I remained alone in a place of obscurity: what could I preserve, and what could I rely on? Thus it is ahead and then behind, seemingly grasped and then seemingly lost, so elusive that no image can represent it. Could one seek it with a careless mind?

Nevertheless, sagehood can be attained through learning. Is it acceptable to be daunted by its difficulty and discourage oneself? By broadening one's learning through letters and restraining oneself through ritual, advancing in due sequence until one wishes to stop but cannot, and fully exerting one's abilities, one may gradually reach that lofty realm. This is clear evidence already established through Yan Zi's own experience. Earlier Confucian scholars said that Yan Zi disclosed the sage's innermost meaning and taught the myriad generations without end. Perhaps this chapter's…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
夫微之顯誠之不可揜如此夫
楊萼
同考試官教諭沈批中庸精粹之理無出此者
是作獨能以精粹之語發之可以為式矣
同考試官教諭杜批發明陰陽合散之理不餘一
辭錄之以範膚淺之學
考試官訓導夏批理到辭到
考試官訓導閔批說理之文惟有此篇
中庸結言鬼神之隱而見者一本於實理之為
===
也蓋隱而能見鬼神之德盛矣謂不本於實理
而能若是也哉中庸十六章發明道之費隱而
有及于此蓋謂鬼神之德固極其盛而其所以
盛也要必有其本者在焉是故其為體也以形
求之泯焉若無而不可得于其形斯天下之至
幽者也以聲擬之杳焉若寂而不可得于其聲
斯天下之至隱者也其微如此然効其能於兩
間而天地之功賴之以成一往一來而物之終
始有不能遺其情狀蓋炳有可見者焉昭其靈
banxin: 福建鄉試錄二十四
punctuated:
夫微之顯，誠之不可揜，如此夫！

楊萼

同考試官教諭沈批：中庸精粹之理，無出此者。是作獨能以精粹之語發之，可以為式矣。

同考試官教諭杜批：發明陰陽合散之理，不餘一辭。錄之以範膚淺之學。

考試官訓導夏批：理到，辭到。

考試官訓導閔批：說理之文，惟有此篇。

《中庸》結言鬼神之隱而見者，一本於實理之為也。蓋隱而能見，鬼神之德盛矣，謂不本於實理而能若是也哉？《中庸》十六章發明道之費隱，而有及于此。蓋謂鬼神之德固極其盛，而其所以盛也，要必有其本者在焉。是故其為體也，以形求之，泯焉若無，而不可得于其形，斯天下之至幽者也；以聲擬之，杳焉若寂，而不可得于其聲，斯天下之至隱者也。其微如此，然効其能於兩間，而天地之功賴之以成；一往一來，而物之終始有不能遺，其情狀蓋炳有可見者焉。昭其靈
translation_en:
“Such is the manifestation of the subtle, and such is the impossibility of concealing what is real!”

Yang E 楊萼

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: “No principle surpasses this in expressing the refined essence of the Doctrine of the Mean. This composition alone can bring it forth in language of corresponding refinement and purity. It may serve as a model.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Du, Instructor: “It elucidates the principle of the coming together and dispersal of yin and yang without a single superfluous word. It is recorded here to provide a standard for those whose learning is superficial.”

Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: “The reasoning is fully realized, and so is its expression.”

Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: “Among compositions expounding principle, this essay stands alone.”

The Doctrine of the Mean concludes by saying that the manifestation of ghosts and spirits, though hidden, is rooted entirely in the workings of real principle. Though hidden, they can manifest themselves: abundant indeed is the potency of ghosts and spirits! Could they be like this without being rooted in real principle? Chapter sixteen of the Doctrine of the Mean elucidates the all-pervading yet hidden character of the Way and thus touches upon this matter. Its meaning is that the potency of ghosts and spirits is indeed supremely abundant, but that this abundance must necessarily have a foundation.

Thus, as to their essential nature: seek them through form, and they vanish as though nonexistent, impossible to apprehend in any form—this is the most obscure thing in the world. Try to conceive of them through sound, and they are remote, as though silent, impossible to apprehend in any sound—this is the most hidden thing in the world. Such is their subtlety. Yet they exercise their powers between heaven and earth, and the achievements of heaven and earth depend upon them for their completion. In each departure and each arrival, the ending and beginning of things cannot dispense with them; their actual workings are thus brilliantly manifest to view. They display their numinous power…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
於六合而造化之迹因之以著一屈一伸而物
之始終自不能外其功效蓋灼有可觀者焉夫
鬼神之微而能顯者果何以哉亦惟誠焉而已
耳蓋鬼神一陰陽也陰陽一實理也於穆之表
孰綱維是倏而合倏而散莫非純一不二者以
爲之本範圍之內孰根柢是合而凝散而盡莫
非真實無妄者以爲之基故其體既實而用自
行往來相推含之而愈光無爲而無不爲也發
越之盛塞乎兩間而不能以自秘否則與物不
===
相值矣烏能如是其顯哉德既實而效自著屈
伸相感翕之而愈闢無在而無不在也昭明之
迹彌乎六合而不能以自藏否則於物無所攝
矣烏能若此其顯哉是則體之微者隱也用之
顯者費也中庸即鬼神之德之盛以明道之全
體其意深矣抑嘗因是而考之誠者造化之樞
紐雖天地之大所弗能違者而況於鬼神乎知
鬼神本於誠則知有無動靜通一無二而道有
可求者後世不知乎此徇無者淪於空執有者
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 二十五
punctuated:
於六合，而造化之迹因之以著。一屈一伸，而物之始終自不能外其功效，蓋灼有可觀者焉。夫鬼神之微而能顯者，果何以哉？亦惟誠焉而已耳。蓋鬼神，一陰陽也；陰陽，一實理也。於穆之表，孰綱維是？倏而合，倏而散，莫非純一不二者以爲之本。範圍之內，孰根柢是？合而凝，散而盡，莫非真實無妄者以爲之基。故其體既實，而用自行，往來相推，含之而愈光，無爲而無不爲也。發越之盛，塞乎兩間，而不能以自秘；否則與物不相值矣，烏能如是其顯哉？德既實，而效自著，屈伸相感，翕之而愈闢，無在而無不在也。昭明之迹，彌乎六合，而不能以自藏；否則於物無所攝矣，烏能若此其顯哉？是則體之微者，隱也；用之顯者，費也。《中庸》即鬼神之德之盛以明道之全體，其意深矣！

抑嘗因是而考之：誠者，造化之樞紐，雖天地之大所弗能違者，而況於鬼神乎？知鬼神本於誠，則知有無動靜通一無二，而道有可求者。後世不知乎此，徇無者淪於空，執有者
translation_en:
…throughout the six directions, and through this the traces of creation and transformation become manifest. With each contraction and expansion, the beginnings and endings of things necessarily fall within their efficacy: here, indeed, is something plainly observable. How, then, can ghosts and spirits, subtle as they are, become manifest? It is solely through sincerity—that is, their unfailing reality. Ghosts and spirits are simply yin and yang; yin and yang are simply real principle. Beyond the profound and reverent mystery, what holds all this together? Now coming together, now dispersing, all takes as its foundation that which is wholly one and undivided. Within the compass of the cosmos, what gives all this its root? Coming together and condensing, dispersing and being exhausted, all takes as its basis that which is real and without falsity. Thus, because their substance is real, their activity proceeds of itself. Coming and going propel one another; the more their radiance is contained, the more brightly it shines. They act without deliberate action, yet leave nothing undone. Their abundant manifestation fills the space between Heaven and Earth and cannot keep itself concealed. Otherwise, they would not encounter things: how could they be so manifest? Because their potency is real, its effects become evident of themselves. Contraction and expansion respond to one another; the more they draw inward, the more widely they unfold. They have no fixed location, yet are nowhere absent. Their luminous traces extend throughout the six directions and cannot hide themselves. Otherwise, they would have no hold upon things: how could they be so manifest? Thus, the subtlety of their substance is what is called “hidden,” and the manifestation of their activity is what is called “all-pervading.” The Doctrine of the Mean uses the abundant potency of ghosts and spirits to illuminate the Way in its entirety. Its meaning is profound indeed!

Moreover, reflecting on this, I have considered the following: sincerity is the pivot of creation and transformation. Even Heaven and Earth, vast as they are, cannot depart from it; how much less can ghosts and spirits? Once we know that ghosts and spirits are rooted in sincerity, we know that being and nonbeing, movement and stillness, form a single, undivided continuum, and that the Way can be sought therein. Later generations failed to understand this. Those who pursued nonbeing sank into emptiness; those who clung to being…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
泥於迹而其所謂鬼神亦異於是矣此邪說所
以惑世而誣民也子思引孔子之言固已明乎
道體而其以闢邪扶敎之意亦有不可誣者歟
日月有明容光必照焉
方召南
同考試官訓導徐批此題場中類爲所窘是篇詞
氣灝發若不經思而理自足審非無本者也
同考試官敎諭吳批說理之言深沉雅飭所以爲難
耳錄之
===
考試官訓導夏批能委曲道孟子音意明暢可式
考試官訓導閔批理致之詞雄勁之筆足範後學
大賢論二曜之著而無微不及者以見聖道之
有本也蓋日月二曜天象之至著者也而光無
遺照焉非其明之有本而能然乎孟子論孔子
之道而此則言其有本也如此意謂不觀聖道
之有本固未知其所以爲大不觀日月之有明
又寧知其所以有本哉故陽本明也日則秉陽
之精而明於晝陰雖晦也月則受日之光而明
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 二十六
punctuated:
泥於迹，而其所謂鬼神亦異於是矣。此邪說所以惑世而誣民也。子思引孔子之言，固已明乎道體，而其以闢邪扶敎之意，亦有不可誣者歟！

日月有明，容光必照焉。

方召南

同考試官訓導徐批：此題場中類爲所窘，是篇詞氣灝發，若不經思而理自足，審非無本者也。

同考試官敎諭吳批：說理之言，深沉雅飭，所以爲難耳。錄之。

考試官訓導夏批：能委曲道孟子音意，明暢可式。

考試官訓導閔批：理致之詞，雄勁之筆，足範後學。

大賢論二曜之著而無微不及者，以見聖道之有本也。蓋日月二曜，天象之至著者也，而光無遺照焉，非其明之有本而能然乎？孟子論孔子之道，而此則言其有本也如此。意謂不觀聖道之有本，固未知其所以爲大；不觀日月之有明，又寧知其所以有本哉？故陽本明也，日則秉陽之精而明於晝；陰雖晦也，月則受日之光而明
translation_en:
…become mired in outward traces, and what they call ghosts and spirits likewise differs from what is meant here. This is how heterodox teachings mislead the world and deceive the people. By quoting Confucius, Zisi has certainly clarified the substance of the Way; surely his intention to refute heterodoxy and uphold the teaching is also undeniable!

“The sun and moon possess brightness; any opening that admits light is sure to be illuminated.”

Fang Zhaonan

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor: This topic seems to have stumped most candidates in the examination hall. In this essay, the language and spirit flow abundantly, as though composed without deliberation, yet its reasoning is complete in itself. It certainly does not lack a foundation.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: In language that expounds principles, depth, refinement, and disciplined expression are difficult to achieve. Include this essay in the record.

Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: It conveys the tenor and meaning of Mencius [?] with subtle thoroughness. Clear and fluent, it may serve as a model.

Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: Language that captures the purport of principles, and a vigorous, forceful pen: these suffice to set a model for later students.

The great worthy discusses how the two luminaries shine conspicuously yet reach even the smallest spaces, thereby showing that the Way of the sage has a foundation. The sun and moon, the two luminaries, are the most conspicuous celestial phenomena, yet their light leaves nothing unilluminated. Could this be so unless their brightness had a foundation? Mencius discusses the Way of Confucius, and here he speaks of its having a foundation in just this manner. His meaning is that, unless one considers the foundation of the sage’s Way, one cannot understand what makes it great; and unless one considers the brightness of the sun and moon, how can one understand what gives it a foundation? Thus yang is inherently bright, and the sun embodies the essence of yang and shines by day. Although yin is dark, the moon receives the sun’s light and shines…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
於夜揭中天而行而群陰爲之屏伏有以發鎬
鎬之輝懸層霄而麗而列宿爲之隱藏有以流
皎皎之素貞明之道在宇宙而常新有目者之
所共覩也其明也孰加焉久照之體終萬古而
有耀有見者之所共仰也其明也孰尚焉惟日
月有明如此是以九州四海何廣大也舉其所
下臨之地八方萬國何遼邈也皆其所旁燭之
鄉是惟無隙則已一有隙焉而光即抵之未有
不遇之而成色者是惟無間則已一有間焉而
===
光即投之未有不借之而增彩者乘虛生白其
餘光之所被有以破暗室之幽矣夫豈照於此
而遺於彼乎自牖通明其餘輝之所及有以啓
豐蔀之蔽矣又豈照於大而遺於小乎是則明
之有本如此此日月之所以爲日月也孔子之
道之大而夫豈無其本哉雖然孟子之於孔子
始以登山觀海爲言繼以日月觀瀾爲言其論
亦極於高遠而無繼矣然豈徒爲是嚮仰者之
言哉蓋嘗致力於是而獨會於心故不覺其嘆
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 二十七
punctuated: 於夜。揭中天而行，而群陰爲之屏伏，有以發鎬鎬之輝；懸層霄而麗，而列宿爲之隱藏，有以流皎皎之素。貞明之道，在宇宙而常新，有目者之所共覩也，其明也孰加焉？久照之體，終萬古而有耀，有見者之所共仰也，其明也孰尚焉？惟日月有明如此，是以九州四海何廣大也，舉其所下臨之地；八方萬國何遼邈也，皆其所旁燭之鄉。是惟無隙則已，一有隙焉，而光即抵之，未有不遇之而成色者；是惟無間則已，一有間焉，而光即投之，未有不借之而增彩者。乘虛生白，其餘光之所被，有以破暗室之幽矣，夫豈照於此而遺於彼乎？自牖通明，其餘輝之所及，有以啓豐蔀之蔽矣，又豈照於大而遺於小乎？是則明之有本如此，此日月之所以爲日月也。孔子之道之大，而夫豈無其本哉？雖然，孟子之於孔子，始以登山觀海爲言，繼以日月觀瀾爲言，其論亦極於高遠而無繼矣。然豈徒爲是嚮仰者之言哉？蓋嘗致力於是，而獨會於心，故不覺其嘆
translation_en:
…at night. Rising into mid-heaven and moving across it, the sun makes all dark forces withdraw and lie subdued, displaying its brilliant radiance [?]. Suspended and shining in the lofty heavens, the moon makes the stars disappear, spreading its clear white light. Their constant brightness remains ever fresh throughout the universe, witnessed by all who have eyes: what could surpass their light? Their enduring power to illuminate shines through all eternity, admired by all who can see: what could excel their brightness? Such is the light of the sun and moon. Thus, however vast the Nine Provinces and Four Seas, they are all lands beneath their illumination; however distant the eight directions and myriad states, they are all regions reached by their rays. Only where there is no opening does their light not enter; wherever there is an opening, their light reaches it, and nothing fails to acquire color upon encountering it. Only where there is no gap does their light not penetrate; wherever there is a gap, their light falls into it, and nothing fails to gain luster by borrowing from it. Entering empty spaces and producing brightness, their residual light dispels the gloom of dark chambers wherever it falls. How could they illuminate this place and neglect that one? Admitting brightness through windows, their residual radiance penetrates even dense coverings wherever it reaches. How could they illuminate the great and neglect the small? Such is the foundation of their brightness; this is what makes the sun and moon what they are. Could the greatness of Kongzi’s Way possibly lack its own foundation?

Yet Mengzi, in speaking of Kongzi, began with climbing mountains and viewing the sea, then went on to speak of the sun and moon and of observing waves. His discussion attained the utmost heights and distances, beyond which nothing could follow. But were these merely the words of someone looking up in admiration? He had himself devoted effort to this Way and attained a distinctive understanding within his own heart; thus, without realizing it, his admiration…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
之至此耳觀于下文又曰君子之志於道不成
章不達此造道而有得者之言軻之達於孔子
幾矣是雖爲學者設得非亦以自喻也歟
易
健而說决而和
廖世昭
同考試官教諭沈批夫子賛易義甚明正場
中作者能語其精微者寡爾此作於决之善處發明詳盡且
詞氣瑩然盖邃於易者也
===
同考試官教諭杜批夬之得中場中作者往往
能言而未了其義且冗贅可厭此作辭吃理盡真佳士也
考試官訓導夏批典重精詳宜錄以爲程式
考試官訓導閔批易義似此絕少
彖傳賛夬之德以見夫决之善也甚矣决陰之
難也而夬之卦德有以備其善焉宜彖傳指以
示人也歟吾夫子賛易之意蓋謂夬以决陰爲
義决以得中爲善今此卦之德下體乾也其德
爲健上體兌也其德爲說健而且說吾知其秉
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 二十八
punctuated:
之至此耳。觀于下文，又曰：「君子之志於道，不成章不達。」此造道而有得者之言，軻之達於孔子幾矣。是雖爲學者設，得非亦以自喻也歟？

易
健而說，决而和。
廖世昭

同考試官教諭沈批：夫子賛易，義甚明正。場中作者能語其精微者寡爾。此作於决之善處發明詳盡，且詞氣瑩然，盖邃於易者也。

同考試官教諭杜批：夬之得中，場中作者往往能言，而未了其義，且冗贅可厭。此作辭吃理盡，真佳士也。

考試官訓導夏批：典重精詳，宜錄以爲程式。

考試官訓導閔批：易義似此絕少。

彖傳賛夬之德，以見夫决之善也。甚矣，决陰之難也！而夬之卦德有以備其善焉，宜彖傳指以示人也歟！吾夫子賛易之意，蓋謂夬以决陰爲義，决以得中爲善。今此卦之德，下體乾也，其德爲健；上體兌也，其德爲說。健而且說，吾知其秉
translation_en:
…that his admiration reached such a pitch. Looking further in the text, we also read: “The gentleman who sets his mind upon the Way does not advance until he has achieved a complete pattern.” These are the words of one who has approached the Way and attained something of it. Ke [Meng Ke, or Mencius] came close to comprehending Confucius. Although this statement was offered for learners, might he not also have been describing himself?

Book of Changes
“Strong yet joyous; resolute yet harmonious.”
Liao Shizhao

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: The Master's commentary on the Changes is exceedingly clear and correct in meaning. Few candidates in this examination can articulate its subtle profundities. This essay explains fully and in detail wherein the excellence of resolution lies; its language and tone are also lucid. Its author is surely deeply versed in the Changes.

Comment by Associate Examiner Du, Instructor: Candidates in this examination can often speak of how the hexagram Guai (Breakthrough) attains the mean, yet they have not fully understood its meaning; moreover, their tedious verbosity is tiresome. This essay's wording is halting [?], but its exposition of principle is exhaustive. Its author is truly an outstanding scholar.

Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: Dignified and weighty, precise and thorough. It should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: Expositions of the meaning of the Changes like this are exceedingly rare.

The Commentary on the Judgments elucidates the qualities of Guai to reveal the excellence of resolution. How difficult it is to eliminate yin! Yet the qualities of the hexagram Guai provide all that is needed to do so well. Is it not fitting that the Commentary on the Judgments points them out to instruct people? Our Master, in commenting on the Changes, presumably meant that Guai signifies eliminating yin, and that resolution is good when it attains the mean. Now, as for the qualities of this hexagram: its lower trigram is Qian, whose quality is strength; its upper trigram is Dui, whose quality is joy. Strong and also joyous, I know that it possesses…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
純陽之性惕厲常存於一心而有以自強妙天
德之全志氣常伸於萬物而無所係累靜焉專
一其惡惡之心蓋有確乎而不可拔者健孰加
焉然又襟度寛平坦然樂易而可親不怒而威
則威不在於猛矣吾何爲而壯吾之頥氣象優
裕怡然温厚而可接不惡而嚴則嚴不在於暴
矣吾何爲而厲吾之色若然則其說之德又有
以濟夫健之所不及矣夬德果何偏乎夫健則自
能决矣說則自能和矣决而且和吾知其黨雖
===
將盡也猶慮其復蔓而去之必决心雖無比也
猶恐其若濡而决之必勇動焉直遂其去惡之
勢蓋有斷然而不可易者决孰尚焉然又藏其
用於自治之時從容不迫而求之必中其情是
可羣也而亦可以渙其羣何乖戾之有密其機
於有厲之際順適自如而制之必得其要非無
異也而不以立其異何繆妄之有若然則其和
之善又有以成夫决之所用矣德又何偏乎卦
有其德聖人舉而賛之厥旨深矣大抵君子小
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 二十九
punctuated: 純陽之性，惕厲常存於一心，而有以自強；妙天德之全，志氣常伸於萬物，而無所係累。靜焉專一，其惡惡之心，蓋有確乎而不可拔者，健孰加焉？然又襟度寛平，坦然樂易而可親；不怒而威，則威不在於猛矣，吾何爲而壯吾之頥？氣象優裕，怡然温厚而可接；不惡而嚴，則嚴不在於暴矣，吾何爲而厲吾之色？若然，則其說之德，又有以濟夫健之所不及矣。夬德果何偏乎？夫健則自能决矣，說則自能和矣。决而且和，吾知其黨雖將盡也，猶慮其復蔓，而去之必决；心雖無比也，猶恐其若濡，而决之必勇。動焉直遂，其去惡之勢，蓋有斷然而不可易者，决孰尚焉？然又藏其用於自治之時，從容不迫，而求之必中其情；是可羣也，而亦可以渙其羣，何乖戾之有？密其機於有厲之際，順適自如，而制之必得其要；非無異也，而不以立其異，何繆妄之有？若然，則其和之善，又有以成夫决之所用矣。德又何偏乎？卦有其德，聖人舉而賛之，厥旨深矣。大抵君子小
translation_en:
…the nature of pure yang: vigilance and apprehension remain constantly within the heart, enabling self-strengthening. Marvelously embodying the fullness of Heaven’s virtue, its resolve and vital spirit continually extend among the myriad things, without attachment or encumbrance. In stillness it is concentrated and single-minded; its hatred of evil is firm and cannot be uprooted. What could surpass such strength? Yet its disposition is also generous and even-tempered, open, cheerful, easygoing, and approachable. It inspires awe without anger, so its authority does not depend upon ferocity. Why, then, should I thrust out my jaw in a show of force? Its bearing is composed and unhurried, pleasantly warm and gentle, inviting others to approach. It is dignified without fierceness, so its dignity does not depend upon violence. Why, then, should I make my expression severe? Thus its virtue of joy can supply what strength alone cannot accomplish. How, indeed, could the virtue of Guai, the hexagram of Resoluteness, be one-sided?

Strength naturally enables resolution; joy naturally enables harmony. Resolute yet harmonious, it recognizes that, though the opposing faction is nearly exhausted, one must still fear its spreading anew and therefore be decisive in removing it. Though the heart has no attachment to that faction, one must still fear irresolution and therefore act courageously in making the break. In action it proceeds directly toward its goal; its momentum in removing evil is decisive and cannot be deflected. What could surpass such resolution? Yet it conceals its exercise of power while putting itself in order, remaining composed and unhurried, and its inquiry invariably reaches the true circumstances. These people can form a faction, yet their faction can also be dispersed: what perversity is there in this? It keeps its workings hidden at moments of danger, responding smoothly and freely, and invariably grasps the essential point in bringing matters under control. It is not without differences, yet it does not insist upon establishing its distinctness: what error or recklessness is there in this? Thus the excellence of its harmony can bring the exercise of its resolution to fulfillment. How, then, could its virtue be one-sided?

The hexagram possesses these virtues, and the sage singles them out for praise. His intent is profound indeed. Generally speaking, noble men and petty…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
人勢不兩立然以正去邪宜無不勝之理但君
子之待夫小人也常恕而小人之伺夫君子者
甚密一或不謹鮮不及矣此聖人於陰陽消長
之間每致其意焉而不苟也噫有是責而當是
事者其亦知所慎也哉
是故變化云為吉事有祥象事知器占事
知來天地設位聖人成能人謀鬼謀百
姓與能
丘養浩
===
同考試官教諭沈 批 此題上言畫前之易正是天地
之能處聖人作易乃所以成其能耳場中作者類多漫說若不相
關獨此篇發揮明白是宜錄出
同考試官教諭杜 批 聖人成能處必如此說方與
上文相應蓋嘗用心於易者
考試官訓導夏 批 理精詞到邃於易學者也
考試官訓導閔 批 得潔淨精微之旨
造化之易妙夫用聖人之易顯其用蓋易之未
作而其理已見於造化矣聖人著之易以示人
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 三十
punctuated:
人勢不兩立，然以正去邪，宜無不勝之理。但君子之待夫小人也常恕，而小人之伺夫君子者甚密，一或不謹，鮮不及矣。此聖人於陰陽消長之間，每致其意焉而不苟也。噫！有是責而當是事者，其亦知所慎也哉！
「是故變化云為，吉事有祥，象事知器，占事知來。天地設位，聖人成能。人謀鬼謀，百姓與能。」
丘養浩
同考試官教諭沈批：「此題上言畫前之易，正是天地之能處。聖人作易，乃所以成其能耳。場中作者類多漫說，若不相關，獨此篇發揮明白，是宜錄出。」
同考試官教諭杜批：「聖人成能處，必如此說，方與上文相應。蓋嘗用心於易者。」
考試官訓導夏批：「理精詞到，邃於易學者也。」
考試官訓導閔批：「得潔淨精微之旨。」
造化之易妙夫用，聖人之易顯其用。蓋易之未作，而其理已見於造化矣。聖人著之易以示人，
translation_en:
…and petty men cannot both prevail. Yet when the upright expel the wicked, there should be no reason why they cannot triumph. But the noble man is always forgiving in his treatment of petty men, whereas petty men keep an exceedingly close watch on the noble man. If he is once incautious, he will seldom escape their reach. This is why the sages always attend carefully to the waxing and waning of yin and yang, never treating it lightly. Ah! Those who bear this responsibility and face such affairs should surely know where caution is needed!
“Thus there are transformations and changes, words and deeds; auspicious affairs have favorable signs. By representing affairs in images, one understands implements; by divining about affairs, one knows what is to come. Heaven and Earth establish their positions, and the sages bring their capacities to fulfillment. Counsel is sought from men and from spirits, and the common people participate in these capacities.”
Qiu Yanghao
Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: “The opening of this topic speaks of the Changes before the hexagrams were drawn: this is precisely where the capacities of Heaven and Earth reside. The sages’ composition of the Book of Changes was simply the means of bringing those capacities to fulfillment. Most candidates in the examination discuss this loosely, as though the two were unrelated. This essay alone expounds it clearly and therefore deserves to be recorded.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Du, Instructor: “The passage about the sages bringing these capacities to fulfillment must be explained in this way if it is to correspond to the preceding text. The writer has evidently devoted thought to the Book of Changes.”
Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: “The reasoning is refined and the expression apt. This is someone deeply versed in the study of the Book of Changes.”
Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: “He has grasped the purport of purity and stillness, subtlety and precision.”
The Changes within the creative transformations of nature are wondrous in their operation; the sages’ Book of Changes makes that operation manifest. For before the Book of Changes was composed, its principles were already evident in nature’s creative transformations. The sages set them down in the Book of Changes to show them to others…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
其用不有以顯於天下哉大傳論乾坤而推言
及此蓋謂乾坤之用固皆本於健順然亦於造
化之理有足徵焉者以其理之顯者言之剛柔
相推一變一化而消長之機以寓動靜相感或
云或爲而得失之象以明是非其顯而易見者
乎以其理之微者言之福之將至事雖未成而
其兆爲之先見善之將来迹雖未著而其幾爲
之先萌是非其微而難明者乎變化云爲有象
可擬也以之而象夫事考迹以觀其變執古以
===
御乎今則其理之一定而不可易者已默藏於
吾心矣吉事有祥有理可推也以之而占夫事
探賾以索其隱由微以察其著則理之將來而
不可測者蓋已昭晣於吾目矣夫造化自然之
易如此苟非聖人作易何以顯其用乎是故輕
清成象者天也穹然而位于上重濁成形者地
也隤然而位于下天地之間但能示人以顯微
之理而已而亦不能以告人也聖人作易立其
象而制乎變則有以研乎天下之幾象變所示
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 三十一
punctuated: 其用不有以顯於天下哉？大傳論乾坤而推言及此，蓋謂乾坤之用固皆本於健順，然亦於造化之理有足徵焉者。以其理之顯者言之，剛柔相推，一變一化，而消長之機以寓；動靜相感，或云或爲，而得失之象以明。是非其顯而易見者乎？以其理之微者言之，福之將至，事雖未成，而其兆爲之先見；善之將来，迹雖未著，而其幾爲之先萌。是非其微而難明者乎？變化云爲，有象可擬也。以之而象夫事，考迹以觀其變，執古以御乎今，則其理之一定而不可易者，已默藏於吾心矣。吉事有祥，有理可推也。以之而占夫事，探賾以索其隱，由微以察其著，則理之將來而不可測者，蓋已昭晣於吾目矣。夫造化自然之易如此，苟非聖人作易，何以顯其用乎？是故輕清成象者，天也，穹然而位于上；重濁成形者，地也，隤然而位于下。天地之間，但能示人以顯微之理而已，而亦不能以告人也。聖人作易，立其象而制乎變，則有以研乎天下之幾。象變所示
translation_en:
…would not its operation thereby be made manifest to all under Heaven? The Great Commentary, in discussing Qian and Kun, extends its argument to this point. It means that the workings of Qian and Kun are indeed rooted in strength and compliance, yet also find ample confirmation in the principles of nature’s creative transformations. To speak of these principles in their manifest aspect: the firm and yielding impel one another, alternating in change and transformation, and within this lies the impulse of waxing and waning; movement and stillness respond to one another, issuing in speech or action, and thereby make the patterns of gain and loss apparent. Are these not what is manifest and readily seen? To speak of these principles in their subtle aspect: when good fortune is about to arrive, although the event has not yet come to fruition, its portent appears beforehand; when something good is about to come, although its traces are not yet apparent, its incipient tendency has already begun to emerge. Are these not what is subtle and difficult to discern?

Changes and transformations, speech and action, have images by which they can be represented. Using these to represent affairs, examining traces to observe their changes, and holding to the ancient to govern the present, the principles that are fixed and unalterable are already silently stored within my mind. Auspicious events have favorable portents, and there are principles from which inferences can be drawn. Using these to divine affairs, probing their intricacies to seek out what is hidden, and proceeding from the subtle to discern what becomes manifest, the future course of principles, otherwise beyond prediction, has already become clear before my eyes.

Such are the spontaneous changes of nature’s creative transformations. Had the sages not composed the Book of Changes, how could their operation have been made manifest? Thus, that which is light and clear and takes on an image is Heaven, arching above; that which is heavy and turbid and takes on form is Earth, resting low below. Heaven and Earth can only display to people the principles of the manifest and the subtle; they cannot explain them to people. The sages composed the Book of Changes, establishing its images and regulating its changes, thereby providing a means to investigate the incipient tendencies of all under Heaven. What the images and changes display…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
皆天地之能也繫其辭而定夫占則有以極天
下之深辭占所示亦天地之能也不皆有賴於
聖人而成哉由是明則有人也而謀之以決其
疑幽則有鬼也而謀之以致其用吾見百姓之
愚其疑者固因之以决而能知夫趨避之方其
怠者亦因之以勉而有得於鼓舞之妙豈不有
以與其能哉是則天地之易賴聖人以顯而聖
人之易本天地以作此天地無全功而聖人所
以能成位乎兩間也歟抑又論之易理固散見
===
于天地而具于書然近取諸身本無不備但百
姓日用而不知耳乾坤雖極天下之健順亦局
於所禀而不能以會其全此上文所以論其能
事而作易之功必以歸之聖人也然則易非啓
天地之秘而發聖人之蘊者邪學者欲希賢希
聖而希天必本於易而反身之功亦自有不可
缺者夫
書
banxin: 福建鄉試録 二十二
punctuated:
皆天地之能也。繫其辭而定夫占，則有以極天下之深，辭占所示亦天地之能也。不皆有賴於聖人而成哉？由是，明則有人也，而謀之以決其疑；幽則有鬼也，而謀之以致其用。吾見百姓之愚，其疑者固因之以决，而能知夫趨避之方；其怠者亦因之以勉，而有得於鼓舞之妙。豈不有以與其能哉？是則天地之易賴聖人以顯，而聖人之易本天地以作。此天地無全功，而聖人所以能成位乎兩間也歟？抑又論之，易理固散見于天地而具于書，然近取諸身，本無不備，但百姓日用而不知耳。乾坤雖極天下之健順，亦局於所禀而不能以會其全。此上文所以論其能事，而作易之功必以歸之聖人也。然則易非啓天地之秘而發聖人之蘊者邪？學者欲希賢希聖而希天，必本於易，而反身之功亦自有不可缺者夫！
書
translation_en:
…are all the capacities of Heaven and Earth. By appending statements and determining the prognostications, the sages could plumb the deepest things in the world; what these statements and prognostications reveal are likewise the capacities of Heaven and Earth. Do not all these depend upon the sages for their accomplishment? Thus, in the visible realm there are human beings, whom one consults to resolve doubts; in the unseen realm there are spirits, whom one consults to bring their efficacy into use. I see that among the uncomprehending common people, those who are doubtful thereby resolve their doubts and learn what to pursue and what to avoid; those who are indolent are likewise thereby encouraged and come to appreciate the subtle efficacy of inspiration. Does this not enable them to participate in these capacities? Thus, the changes of Heaven and Earth depend upon the sages to become manifest, while the sages’ Book of Changes was composed on the basis of Heaven and Earth. Is this not why Heaven and Earth cannot accomplish their work in full by themselves, and why the sages can establish their place between the two?
To discuss this further: the principles of change are indeed manifest throughout Heaven and Earth and fully embodied in the book. Yet if one looks close at hand within oneself, nothing is originally lacking; it is simply that the common people use them daily without knowing it. Although Qian and Kun exemplify to the utmost the vigor and compliance found in the world, each is also confined to what it has been endowed with and cannot encompass the whole. This is why the preceding passage discusses their capacities, yet necessarily attributes the achievement of composing the Book of Changes to the sages. Does the Book of Changes not, then, disclose the secrets of Heaven and Earth and reveal what lies within the sages? Students who aspire to emulate the worthies, the sages, and Heaven must take the Book of Changes as their foundation; the work of examining themselves is also indispensable!
Book of Documents

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
林應驄
同考試官訓導徐批幾之一字皐陶欲舜儆
戒之意正在於此塲中作者多畧而不講間有說者又冗
贅可厭此篇理明詞暢深得人臣勸戒之體故錄之以式後學
同考試官教諭吳批幾字意義最難模寫是
篇鋪叙明白而詞氣渾厚其有得於皐陶進戒之旨者是宜錄出
考試官訓導夏批皐陶告舜之意發明殆盡佳作也
考試官訓導閔批講能發題意聘浮臆說者可
以謂矣
===
當至淺之時有至衆之務大臣告君之深意也
蓋一日二日時之至淺者也而幾務之來且至
萬焉人君其可一日而不謹哉昔皐陶陳知人
之謨于舜至此謂夫君人者必勤儉率諸侯而
兢業以自處者何哉誠以自朝至中自中至昃
時之所經僅一日之期耳晷刻之推移何有於
浹旬之久耶是固至近矣明而既晦晦而復明
日之所歷斯二日而已耳辰候之代謝何有乎
banxin: 福建鄉試錄三十三
punctuated:
林應驄

同考試官訓導徐批：「幾之一字，皐陶欲舜儆戒之意正在於此。塲中作者多畧而不講，間有說者，又冗贅可厭。此篇理明詞暢，深得人臣勸戒之體，故錄之以式後學。」

同考試官教諭吳批：「幾字意義最難模寫，是篇鋪叙明白，而詞氣渾厚，其有得於皐陶進戒之旨者，是宜錄出。」

考試官訓導夏批：「皐陶告舜之意，發明殆盡，佳作也。」

考試官訓導閔批：「講能發題意，聘浮臆說者，可以謂矣。」

當至淺之時，有至衆之務，大臣告君之深意也。蓋一日二日，時之至淺者也，而幾務之來且至萬焉，人君其可一日而不謹哉？昔皐陶陳知人之謨于舜，至此謂夫君人者必勤儉率諸侯，而兢業以自處者，何哉？誠以自朝至中，自中至昃，時之所經僅一日之期耳，晷刻之推移，何有於浹旬之久耶？是固至近矣。明而既晦，晦而復明，日之所歷斯二日而已耳，辰候之代謝，何有乎
translation_en:
Lin Yingcong 林應驄

Associate Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The single word ji 幾—incipient developments—is precisely where Gao Yao’s intention to urge vigilance upon Shun lies. Most candidates in the examination hall pass over it without discussion; the few who do explain it are tiresomely prolix. This essay is clear in reasoning and fluent in expression, and thoroughly captures the manner appropriate to a minister exhorting and admonishing his ruler. It is therefore recorded as a model for future students.”

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “The meaning of the word ji is exceptionally difficult to convey. This essay develops it clearly, with substantial and dignified expression. It grasps the purpose of Gao Yao’s admonition and accordingly deserves to be recorded.”

Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor, comments: “It elucidates almost completely the meaning of Gao Yao’s address to Shun. An excellent composition.”

Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Its exposition brings out the meaning of the topic; as for indulging in superficial conjecture [?], one may say this of it [?].”

Within the briefest span of time there are affairs of the greatest multitude: this is the profound meaning of the great minister’s counsel to his ruler. One day or two days is indeed a very brief span; yet the incipient affairs that arise may number as many as ten thousand. Can a ruler go even one day without vigilance? In former times, Gao Yao presented to Shun his counsels on understanding men. At this point, why did he say that one who rules others must lead the regional lords through diligence and frugality, and conduct himself with reverent vigilance? It is truly because, from morning to midday and from midday until the sun declines, the time elapsed is merely a single day. How could the passage of these hours and moments amount to the length of a full ten-day period? This is certainly a very short interval. Light gives way to darkness, and darkness to light again: the days elapsed are only two. How could the succession of times and periods …

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
慮者然人主置身兆庶之上事幾之來蓋動以
萬計而有常勤之務時止二日似無可患者然
人君聯屬天下之大事幾之至蓋將以萬計而
有必親之政乾綱總於一人而天下之政制之
在始所以煩淵衷勞宸斷者常循環而無窮政
柄歸於九五而天下之事爲之在豫所以宏廟
謨勚聖慮者常相續而不絶大而紀綱法度之
施四海之休戚繫焉苟毫髮幾微之不察則藏
於細者必形於大而或以貽患於天下必兢業
===
焉爲大於其細可也夫可以一日之近而偷安
乎小而條教號令之布生民之休戚存焉苟頃
刻謹畏之不存則隱於易者每至於難或以基
禍於邦家必兢業焉圖難於其易可也又可以
二日之淺而玩愒乎吁人主以一身居天下之
尊而不敢一日忽天下之務則君身克謹而羣
臣咸有所取法矣又何治功之不可成哉宜皐
陶以是而警之也嗟夫君至於舜至矣盡矣不
可以復加矣何有於逸欲而不兢業於心哉顧
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 三十
punctuated: 慮者。然人主置身兆庶之上，事幾之來，蓋動以萬計，而有常勤之務。時止二日，似無可患者，然人君聯屬天下之大，事幾之至，蓋將以萬計，而有必親之政。乾綱總於一人，而天下之政制之在始，所以煩淵衷、勞宸斷者，常循環而無窮；政柄歸於九五，而天下之事爲之在豫，所以宏廟謨、勚聖慮者，常相續而不絶。大而紀綱法度之施，四海之休戚繫焉。苟毫髮幾微之不察，則藏於細者必形於大，而或以貽患於天下。必兢業焉，爲大於其細可也。夫可以一日之近而偷安乎？小而條教號令之布，生民之休戚存焉。苟頃刻謹畏之不存，則隱於易者每至於難，或以基禍於邦家。必兢業焉，圖難於其易可也。又可以二日之淺而玩愒乎？吁！人主以一身居天下之尊，而不敢一日忽天下之務，則君身克謹，而羣臣咸有所取法矣。又何治功之不可成哉？宜皐陶以是而警之也。嗟夫！君至於舜，至矣，盡矣，不可以復加矣。何有於逸欲而不兢業於心哉？顧
translation_en: …a matter for concern [?]. Yet the ruler stands above the multitudes, and the incipient affairs that come before him readily number in the tens of thousands: there are duties requiring constant diligence. The time amounts to only two days, seemingly giving no cause for concern; yet the sovereign holds together the vast realm, and the incipient affairs arriving before him will number in the tens of thousands: there are matters of government that he must attend to personally. Supreme authority is concentrated in one man, and the realm’s governance must be ordered from the outset; thus the matters that trouble his profound heart and tax his imperial judgment recur endlessly. The power of government rests with the sovereign, and the realm’s affairs must be handled in anticipation; thus the matters that call for far-reaching court deliberations and weary his sagely thought follow one another without cease. In great matters, such as implementing the principles of government and its laws and institutions, the well-being and suffering of all within the four seas hang in the balance. If even the slightest incipient development escapes scrutiny, what lies concealed in small things will inevitably become manifest in great ones, perhaps bringing calamity upon the realm. He must be vigilant and diligent, dealing with great matters while they are still small. How could he indulge in ease merely because a single day is so short? In lesser matters, such as promulgating instructions and commands, the well-being and suffering of the people are at stake. If caution and apprehension lapse even for a moment, what lies hidden in the easy will often develop into the difficult, perhaps laying the foundations of disaster for the state. He must be vigilant and diligent, planning for difficulties while they are still easy. How, then, could he idle away his time merely because two days are so brief? Ah! If the ruler, occupying alone the most exalted position in the realm, dares not neglect its affairs for even a day, he will conduct himself circumspectly, and all his ministers will have an example to follow. What achievements in government could then be beyond attainment? It was fitting that Gao Yao should admonish him with these words. Alas! In Shun, rulership reached its utmost perfection; nothing further could be added. How could he have harbored desires for idle pleasure and failed to remain vigilant and diligent at heart? Yet…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
皐陶陳謨必至於此者蓋有說也何者古之大
臣不以世之已治而忘儆戒之心不以君之旣
聖而忘責難之意茲有虞之世所以爲不可及
也嗚呼以舜爲君而有臣如此天下安得而不
治乎
監于先王成憲其永無愆惟說式克欽承
旁招俊乂列于庶位王曰嗚呼說四海
之內咸仰朕德時乃風股肱惟人良臣
惟聖昔先正保衡作我先王乃曰予弗
===
克俾厥后惟堯舜其心愧耻若撻于市
一夫不獲則曰時予之辜佑我烈祖格
于皇天爾尚明保予罔俾阿衡專美有
商惟后非賢不乂惟賢非后不食其爾
克紹乃辟于先王永綏民說拜稽首曰
敢對揚天子之休命
陳騰鸞
同考試官訓導徐批高宗傅說交相責望與
所以自期待之意作者類能言之寧繁無可厭此作文理
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 三十五
punctuated:
皐陶陳謨必至於此者，蓋有說也。何者？古之大臣不以世之已治而忘儆戒之心，不以君之旣聖而忘責難之意。茲有虞之世所以爲不可及也。嗚呼！以舜爲君，而有臣如此，天下安得而不治乎？

監于先王成憲，其永無愆。惟說式克欽承，旁招俊乂，列于庶位。王曰：「嗚呼！說，四海之內咸仰朕德，時乃風。股肱惟人，良臣惟聖。昔先正保衡作我先王，乃曰：『予弗克俾厥后惟堯舜，其心愧耻若撻于市。』一夫不獲，則曰：『時予之辜。』佑我烈祖，格于皇天。爾尚明保予，罔俾阿衡專美有商。惟后非賢不乂，惟賢非后不食。其爾克紹乃辟于先王，永綏民。」說拜稽首曰：「敢對揚天子之休命。」

陳騰鸞

同考試官訓導徐批：高宗、傅說交相責望，與所以自期待之意，作者類能言之。寧繁，無可厭。此作文理
translation_en:
…There is a reason why Gao Yao, in presenting his counsels, necessarily went this far. What was it? The great ministers of antiquity did not forget the need for vigilance and admonition merely because the age was already well governed; nor did they forget their intention to demand difficult accomplishments of their ruler merely because he was already a sage. This is why the age of Yu Shun cannot be equaled. Ah! With Shun as ruler and ministers such as these, how could All under Heaven fail to be well governed?

“Look to the established statutes of the former kings, and you will forever be without fault.” Yue reverently carried out this charge, broadly recruiting men of outstanding talent and virtue and placing them in the various offices. The king said: “Ah, Yue! All within the Four Seas look up to my virtue: this is the effect of your influence. As arms and legs are to a person, so are good ministers to a sage. Formerly, the earlier chief minister, the Guardian and Equalizer, assisted our former king. He said: ‘If I cannot make my sovereign like Yao and Shun, I feel as ashamed as if I were being flogged in the marketplace.’ If even one man failed to obtain his due, he said: ‘This is my fault.’ He aided our illustrious ancestor, whose virtue reached August Heaven. May you wisely protect me, and not allow the A-heng alone to enjoy renown in our Shang dynasty. A sovereign cannot govern without worthy men; worthy men cannot obtain their sustenance without a sovereign. May you enable your ruler to carry on the former kings’ legacy and bring lasting peace to the people.” Yue bowed and knocked his head to the ground, saying: “I venture to acknowledge and extol the Son of Heaven’s gracious command.”

Chen Tengluan.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor: Most writers can express the expectations Gaozong and Fu Yue placed upon one another, together with what each expected of himself. Even at some length, there need be nothing tiresome. The reasoning in this composition…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
明淨且有照應取之以冠本房
同考試官教諭吳批長題貴簡明而厭冗雜
此作鋪叙嚴整得當時君臣相期自任之意尤宜高薦
考試官訓導夏批明潔可觀蓋純於璧經者
考試官訓導閔批此作簡嚴必老學之士宜寘高選
觀有商之君臣重致相望之意而皆有以自任
焉蓋商之君臣莫聖於成湯伊尹也然高宗傅
說之交相告勉得不以此責望而復致自任也
哉昔傅說勉高宗進學及此謂夫吾君德雖造
===
於罔覺法必監于先王彼脩己治人先王成法
固歷萬世而無弊矣君必視以為準遵而行之
斯克永世而無過焉然君德苟至于無愆則說
用能敬承其意于以明揚俊民而列于庶位敷
求哲人而布于衆職以人事君德愈懋矣高宗
遂嘆之以為天下之大咸仰我德而無間焉者
實汝之風有以動之而致然也然欲慰天下之
望在汝盡輔聖之功蓋人不自成也必手足備
而後成君不自聖也必良臣輔而後聖昔伊尹
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 三十六
punctuated:
明淨且有照應，取之以冠本房。

同考試官教諭吳批：長題貴簡明而厭冗雜，此作鋪叙嚴整，得當時君臣相期自任之意，尤宜高薦。

考試官訓導夏批：明潔可觀，蓋純於璧經者。

考試官訓導閔批：此作簡嚴，必老學之士，宜寘高選。

觀有商之君臣重致相望之意，而皆有以自任焉。蓋商之君臣莫聖於成湯、伊尹也，然高宗、傅說之交相告勉，得不以此責望而復致自任也哉？昔傅說勉高宗進學，及此謂夫吾君德雖造於罔覺，法必監于先王。彼脩己治人，先王成法，固歷萬世而無弊矣。君必視以為準，遵而行之，斯克永世而無過焉。然君德苟至于無愆，則說用能敬承其意，于以明揚俊民而列于庶位，敷求哲人而布于衆職，以人事君，德愈懋矣。高宗遂嘆之，以為天下之大，咸仰我德而無間焉者，實汝之風有以動之而致然也。然欲慰天下之望，在汝盡輔聖之功。蓋人不自成也，必手足備而後成；君不自聖也，必良臣輔而後聖。昔伊尹
translation_en:
…clear and lucid, with parts that echo one another. I select it to rank first among the papers in this examining room.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: A long topic calls for concision and clarity and admits no prolixity or clutter. This composition develops its argument with rigor and order, capturing the expectations that ruler and minister then held for one another and the responsibilities each assumed. It particularly deserves a high recommendation.

Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: Clear and cleanly written, and well worth reading. Its author is evidently thoroughly versed in the classic [?; the transcription reads 璧經].

Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: This composition is concise and rigorous. Its author must be a seasoned scholar and should be placed high among those selected.

Observe how the ruler and minister of Shang earnestly reiterated their expectations of one another, while each assumed responsibilities himself. Among the rulers and ministers of Shang, none surpassed Cheng Tang and Yi Yin in sageliness. Yet when Gaozong and Fu Yue admonished and encouraged one another, could they fail to hold each other to this standard and also renew their own commitments? Formerly, when Fu Yue urged Gaozong to advance in learning, he came to this point: although our ruler’s virtue has reached the stage of effortless understanding, in taking models he must still look to the former kings. The established methods of the former kings for cultivating oneself and governing others can indeed endure ten thousand generations without ill effect. The ruler must regard them as his standard and follow them in practice; only then can he remain free from error for all time. If the ruler’s virtue indeed becomes faultless, then I, Yue, can reverently carry out his intentions: publicly promoting outstanding men and placing them in the various ranks, searching widely for wise men and distributing them among the many offices. With such men serving the ruler, his virtue will flourish still more.

Gaozong thereupon exclaimed in admiration: Throughout the vast realm, all look up to my virtue without reservation. It is truly your influence that has moved them and brought this about. Yet to fulfill the hopes of all under Heaven depends upon your fully accomplishing the work of assisting your ruler toward sageliness. A person is not complete by himself: only with hands and feet present is he complete. A ruler does not become a sage by himself: only with the assistance of worthy ministers does he become a sage. Formerly, Yi Yin…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
保衡作我先王以為堯舜其君予之心也君不
堯舜則有愧于心若撻之于市焉堯舜其民予
之志也一民不獲則自咎于身若納之溝中焉
故能篤棐左右以佑我先王懋著厥功以格于
上帝爾當明以保我亦致我而為烈祖可也可
使尹而獨美於商乎且君非賢臣寧虛其位而
已不與其治也臣非賢君寧晦吾迹而已不與
共食也爾其克紹乃辟于先王不殊於尹之事
君焉綏安兆民於永久不異於尹之治民焉說
===
於是拜稽首而言曰克紹乃辟乃致君之休命
也永綏兆民乃澤民之美命也吾必對之於巳
而揚之於衆務使君為堯舜而後吾之心始愜
耳務俾民為唐虞而後吾之責始塞耳噫君臣
交相責望既欲以成湯伊尹為準的而又皆直
任之無慊所謂上下交而德業成豈非有商之
極盛乎考之高宗之於傅說始得之其事異繼
命之其任重終望之其意深而說也卒能輔導
高宗進學脩德而無愧於成湯使高宗為商之
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 三十七
punctuated:
保衡作我先王，以為：堯舜其君，予之心也；君不堯舜，則有愧于心，若撻之于市焉。堯舜其民，予之志也；一民不獲，則自咎于身，若納之溝中焉。故能篤棐左右，以佑我先王，懋著厥功，以格于上帝。爾當明以保我，亦致我而為烈祖可也，可使尹而獨美於商乎？且君非賢臣，寧虛其位而已，不與其治也；臣非賢君，寧晦吾迹而已，不與共食也。爾其克紹乃辟于先王，不殊於尹之事君焉；綏安兆民於永久，不異於尹之治民焉。
說於是拜稽首而言曰：「克紹乃辟，乃致君之休命也；永綏兆民，乃澤民之美命也。吾必對之於巳，而揚之於衆，務使君為堯舜，而後吾之心始愜耳；務俾民為唐虞，而後吾之責始塞耳。」
噫！君臣交相責望，既欲以成湯、伊尹為準的，而又皆直任之無慊。所謂上下交而德業成，豈非有商之極盛乎？考之高宗之於傅說，始得之，其事異；繼命之，其任重；終望之，其意深。而說也卒能輔導高宗進學脩德，而無愧於成湯，使高宗為商之
translation_en:
…as Protector (Baoheng), guided our former king. He considered: “To make my ruler a Yao or Shun is my heart’s desire. If my ruler does not become a Yao or Shun, I feel shame in my heart, as though I were being flogged in the marketplace. To make his people like the people of Yao and Shun is my ambition. If even one person fails to obtain his proper place, I blame myself, as though I had thrust him into a ditch.” Thus he could give steadfast assistance at the king’s side, supporting our former king and gloriously establishing his achievements so that they reached the Lord on High. You should wisely protect me and likewise bring me to equal my illustrious ancestor. Can we allow Yin alone to enjoy such distinction in Shang? Moreover, unless a ruler has a worthy minister, he would sooner leave the post vacant than share the work of government with another; unless a minister has a worthy ruler, he would sooner remain in obscurity than partake of that ruler’s sustenance. May you enable your sovereign to carry on the former king’s legacy, just as Yin served his ruler; and may you bring lasting peace to the myriad people, just as Yin governed them.
Yue then bowed and knocked his head to the ground, saying: “To enable your sovereign to carry on that legacy is an auspicious command to bring the ruler to perfection; to bring lasting peace to the myriad people is an excellent command to bestow benefits upon them. I must answer it in my own person [?] and proclaim it to all. I shall strive to make my ruler a Yao or Shun; only then will my heart be satisfied. I shall strive to make the people like those of Tang and Yu; only then will my responsibility be fulfilled.”
Ah! Ruler and minister held one another to exacting expectations. They wished to take Cheng Tang and Yi Yin as their standard, and both directly accepted this responsibility without misgiving. This is what is meant by those above and below communicating so that virtue and achievement are brought to completion. Was this not Shang at its very height? Examining Gaozong’s dealings with Fu Yue, we find that when he first obtained him, the circumstances were extraordinary; when he subsequently charged him with office, the responsibility was weighty; and in his final expression of expectations, his intentions were profound. Yue ultimately succeeded in assisting and guiding Gaozong to advance his learning and cultivate his virtue, so that he need feel no shame before Cheng Tang, making Gaozong one of Shang’s…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
令主說亦爲商之賢佐明君賢相兩無愧焉赫
赫厥聲濯濯厥靈之盛有由然矣後世得其書
讀之猶可想見於數千載之上
詩
衆維魚矣旐維旟矣
朱潚
同考試官教諭吳批此題塲中士子多記舊
文千篇一律無可去取晚得此卷會傳意成文而詞足以發
之當是作手
===
同考試官學正胡批理明詞暢立論尤出人意
表是可錄也已
考試官訓導夏批寫出牧人之夢宛然在目可
以占子之善說詩矣
考試官訓導閔批語新而意盡可取
盛時牧人之夢隨感而皆有異也夫夢人而爲
魚夢旐而爲旟是固皆出於意象之外者也牧
人之夢有是焉夫豈徒然也哉無羊之詩牧事
有成而作也至此若曰當牧事有成之日正牧
banxin: 福建鄉試錄三十八
punctuated:
令主，說亦爲商之賢佐，明君賢相，兩無愧焉。赫赫厥聲，濯濯厥靈之盛，有由然矣。後世得其書讀之，猶可想見於數千載之上。

詩
衆維魚矣，旐維旟矣。
朱潚

同考試官教諭吳批：此題塲中士子多記舊文，千篇一律，無可去取。晚得此卷，會傳意成文，而詞足以發之，當是作手。

同考試官學正胡批：理明詞暢，立論尤出人意表，是可錄也已。

考試官訓導夏批：寫出牧人之夢，宛然在目，可以占子之善說詩矣。

考試官訓導閔批：語新而意盡，可取。

盛時牧人之夢，隨感而皆有異也。夫夢人而爲魚，夢旐而爲旟，是固皆出於意象之外者也。牧人之夢有是焉，夫豈徒然也哉？《無羊》之詩，牧事有成而作也。至此若曰：當牧事有成之日，正牧
translation_en:
…a worthy ruler of Shang, while Yue likewise became a worthy assistant to Shang. As an enlightened ruler and a worthy minister, neither fell short. There was thus a reason for the splendid flourishing described as “Glorious was his renown; resplendent was his spiritual might.” When later generations obtain this text and read it, they can still envision what happened thousands of years before.

Classic of Poetry
“The people became fish; the tortoise-and-snake banners became bird-and-falcon banners.”
Zhu Su 朱潚

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: On this topic, most candidates in the examination hall reproduced old compositions from memory. A thousand essays followed the same pattern, leaving no basis for choosing or rejecting them. Late in the process I obtained this paper. It grasps the meaning of the commentary and shapes it into an essay, with language adequate to bring that meaning out. Its author must be an accomplished writer.

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, School Director: The reasoning is clear and the language fluent. The argument, in particular, goes beyond what one would expect. This certainly merits selection.

Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: The herdsmen’s dream is depicted so vividly that it seems to stand before our eyes. From this one may discern your skill in explaining the Poetry.

Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: The language is fresh and the meaning fully expressed. Worth selecting.

In a flourishing age, the herdsmen’s dreams, responding to what moves them, all contain something extraordinary. To dream of people becoming fish and tortoise-and-snake banners becoming bird-and-falcon banners—these are indeed things beyond ordinary imagining. Such things occur in the herdsmen’s dreams: could they possibly be without significance? The poem “No Sheep” was composed when the work of tending livestock had succeeded. At this point it seems to say: the day when the tending of livestock had succeeded was precisely when the herdsmen…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
人有暇之時而爲夢也果何如哉故靈萬物而
獨秀於兩間人也而魚則鱗族之微耳人與魚
豈其同類者哉牧人夢與天地相爲流通夢人
維人固常也而非異矣然而示諸恍惚之間則
人非人也而爲魚焉飾以冠履者乃馨鬣其形
華以襟裾者皆鱗介其属儀容之楚楚也其逐
波濤而上下者乎咲言之啞啞也其游江湖而
煦濡者乎而族類之蕃育固有潑潑以適者矣
人與物有定形而夢之所及何嘗有定形哉且
===
四斿而特建於郊野者旐也而旟則州里所建
焉旐與旟豈其同用者哉牧人夢與陰陽相爲
會合夢旐維旐亦常也而非異矣然而見諸彷
彿之際則旐非旐也而爲旟焉畫爲龜蛇者乃
鳥隼其章象著玄武者寔朱雀其制甲而爲息
伏也其乘風雲而摶擊者乎跗而為蜿蜒也其
凌霄漢而翱翔者乎而州里之彩繪固有翩翩
以舉者矣旐與旟有定制也而夢之所及何嘗
banxin: 福建鄕試錄 三十九
punctuated: 人有暇之時，而爲夢也，果何如哉？故靈萬物而獨秀於兩間，人也；而魚則鱗族之微耳。人與魚，豈其同類者哉？牧人夢與天地相爲流通，夢人維人，固常也，而非異矣。然而示諸恍惚之間，則人非人也，而爲魚焉。飾以冠履者，乃馨鬣其形；華以襟裾者，皆鱗介其属。儀容之楚楚也，其逐波濤而上下者乎？咲言之啞啞也，其游江湖而煦濡者乎？而族類之蕃育，固有潑潑以適者矣。人與物有定形，而夢之所及，何嘗有定形哉？且四斿而特建於郊野者，旐也；而旟則州里所建焉。旐與旟，豈其同用者哉？牧人夢與陰陽相爲會合，夢旐維旐，亦常也，而非異矣。然而見諸彷彿之際，則旐非旐也，而爲旟焉。畫爲龜蛇者，乃鳥隼其章；象著玄武者，寔朱雀其制。甲而爲息伏也，其乘風雲而摶擊者乎？跗而為蜿蜒也，其凌霄漢而翱翔者乎？而州里之彩繪，固有翩翩以舉者矣。旐與旟有定制也，而夢之所及，何嘗
translation_en: …when the herdsmen had leisure and dreamed—what, then, were their dreams like? It is humans who possess the spiritual intelligence of the myriad creatures and stand uniquely distinguished between Heaven and Earth; fish are merely humble members of the scaly tribes. How could humans and fish belong to the same kind? In their dreams, the herdsmen enter into mutual communication with Heaven and Earth. To dream of humans as simply humans would certainly be ordinary, with nothing strange about it. Yet in the indistinct visions that appear, humans are no longer humans but become fish. Those adorned with caps and shoes take on forms with fins [?]; those resplendent in robes become creatures covered in scales. Those so elegant in bearing—are they now rising and falling with the waves? Those whose laughter and speech rang out—are they now swimming in rivers and lakes, warming and moistening one another? As their kind multiplies, there are indeed fish darting about at ease. Humans and other creatures have fixed forms, but how could the realm of dreams ever have fixed forms? Moreover, the banner with four streamers, erected specifically in the countryside, is the zhao banner; the yu banner is erected in the districts and villages. How could the zhao and yu banners serve the same purpose? In their dreams, the herdsmen enter into union with yin and yang. To dream of a zhao banner as simply a zhao banner would likewise be ordinary, with nothing strange about it. Yet in the hazy visions that appear, the zhao is no longer a zhao but becomes a yu. What was painted with tortoises and snakes now bears birds and falcons as its emblems; what displayed the image of the Dark Warrior now takes the form of the Vermilion Bird. The shelled creature resting in concealment—does it now ride the winds and clouds and strike at its prey? The creature that twists and winds upon its feet [?]—does it now soar through the lofty heavens? The painted banners of the districts and villages do indeed rise fluttering aloft. The zhao and yu banners have fixed designs, but in the realm of dreams, how could there ever…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
天下之大太卜占之而推爲富庶之祥宜矣抑
考厲王暴虐周室板蕩民靡有黎具禍以燼而
生靈之淪斁將盡矣降此蟊賊稼穡卒痒而中
國之具贅卒荒矣而宣王承其餘烈遇災知懼
側身脩行天下喜於王化復行百姓見憂故民
困甦而流離集天意回而國事殷富庶之祥兆
於牧人之夢良亦不偶是知人事脩於下則和
氣應於上雖樵童牧竪亦能獻吉夢以增中興
之勝槩讀是詩者宜併合雲漢之章而觀之
===
作之屛之其菑其翳脩之平之其灌其栵
啓之辟之其檉其椐攘之剔之其檿其
柘
謝寬
同考試官教諭吳 批 題本平淡作者類忽章
句所審典雅春容僅見此篇宜錄之以式後學
同考試官學正胡 批 場中作此題者多冗雜
塵腐令人厭觀整潔如此篇者絕少故用錄之
考試官州判夏 批 詠王一時開闢氣象羣寫
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 四十
punctuated:
天下之大，太卜占之，而推爲富庶之祥，宜矣。抑考厲王暴虐，周室板蕩，民靡有黎，具禍以燼，而生靈之淪斁將盡矣。降此蟊賊，稼穡卒痒，而中國之具贅卒荒矣。而宣王承其餘烈，遇災知懼，側身脩行，天下喜於王化復行，百姓見憂。故民困甦而流離集，天意回而國事殷。富庶之祥，兆於牧人之夢，良亦不偶。是知人事脩於下，則和氣應於上，雖樵童牧竪，亦能獻吉夢，以增中興之勝槩。讀是詩者，宜併合《雲漢》之章而觀之。

作之屛之，其菑其翳；脩之平之，其灌其栵；啓之辟之，其檉其椐；攘之剔之，其檿其柘。

謝寬

同考試官教諭吳批：題本平淡，作者類忽。章句所審，典雅春容，僅見此篇，宜錄之以式後學。

同考試官學正胡批：場中作此題者，多冗雜塵腐，令人厭觀。整潔如此篇者絕少，故用錄之。

考試官州判夏批：詠王一時開闢氣象，羣寫
translation_en:
…the vastness of all under Heaven. It was fitting that the Grand Diviner should interpret this dream and infer an auspicious sign of prosperity and a flourishing population. Consider, however, King Li’s tyranny: the royal house of Zhou was in turmoil; none of the people remained, all suffering calamity until they were reduced to ashes, and the living were nearly engulfed in ruin. These crop-devouring pests descended, and all the crops suffered; throughout the central lands, everything was burdensome and ultimately laid waste [?]. King Xuan inherited the aftermath of these troubles. Encountering disasters, he knew fear, humbled himself, and cultivated his conduct. All under Heaven rejoiced that royal moral transformation was once again at work and that the common people were receiving solicitous care. Thus the people recovered from their distress, and the displaced gathered again; Heaven’s disposition turned favorable, and the affairs of state flourished. That an omen of prosperity and a flourishing population appeared in a herdsman’s dream was surely no coincidence. From this we know that when human affairs are put in order below, harmonious qi responds above. Even woodcutting boys and young herdsmen can offer auspicious dreams that enhance the splendid achievements of a dynastic restoration. Readers of this ode should consider it together with the ode The Milky Way (Yunhan).

They cut them down and cleared them away—the dead standing trees and the dense growth; they trimmed them and leveled them—the shrubs and clustered shoots; they opened up and cleared the land—the tamarisks and the ju trees; they removed them and stripped them away—the mountain mulberries and the silkworm thorns.

Xie Kuan.

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: The topic is inherently plain, and writers generally neglect it. In its carefully considered phrasing, this essay alone displays classical elegance and a springlike ease [?]. It should be recorded as a model for later students.

Associate Examiner Hu, School Director, comments: Among those who addressed this topic in the examination, many produced prolix, disordered, stale writing that was tiresome to read. Essays as orderly and clean as this one were extremely rare, so we have selected it for inclusion.

Examiner Xia, Assistant Prefect, comments: In celebrating the king’s work of opening up the land in his day, it depicts the scene in its entirety…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
殆盡傑作也可敬可敬
考試官訓導閔批筆健語莊是繩尺文字可取
隨物性而致開闢之功此賢君立國然也蓋人
事脩而後天意可承也周人開國而漸見於林
木之治如此王業其嗣而興乎昔詩人叙太王
太伯王季之德至此謂夫我太王當遷岐定居
之始正隨山刊木之時其所以開闢者何如哉
故夫枯木宜去其茂而密者未易以盡除也則
因其勢而治焉拔之使起屏之使去并其根株
===
條幹而盡棄者皆夫生意已絕為菑與翳也是
寧有穢襍而復存者哉脩之使通平之使理求
其疎密直正之皆宜者乃其叢列而生為灌與
栵也是復有參錯而不治者哉夫於菑翳灌栵
而皆致力焉則山林之險僻者自是有可通之
道彼徂矣岐其駸駸乎人物之會乎不特此也
凡木可無其美而材者不可以不畜也則順其
宜而治之故恐其為蓊鬱也啓闢之以除其類
不使之駢附而起者則檉也而檉之外又有椐
banxin: 福建鄉試錄四十一
punctuated:
殆盡，傑作也，可敬可敬！
考試官訓導閔批：筆健語莊，是繩尺文字，可取。
隨物性而致開闢之功，此賢君立國然也。蓋人事脩而後天意可承也。周人開國，而漸見於林木之治如此，王業其嗣而興乎！昔詩人叙太王、太伯、王季之德，至此謂夫我太王當遷岐定居之始，正隨山刊木之時，其所以開闢者何如哉？故夫枯木宜去，其茂而密者未易以盡除也，則因其勢而治焉。拔之使起，屏之使去，并其根株條幹而盡棄者，皆夫生意已絕，為菑與翳也。是寧有穢襍而復存者哉？脩之使通，平之使理，求其疎密直正之皆宜者，乃其叢列而生，為灌與栵也。是復有參錯而不治者哉？夫於菑翳灌栵而皆致力焉，則山林之險僻者，自是有可通之道。彼徂矣岐，其駸駸乎人物之會乎！不特此也，凡木可無，其美而材者不可以不畜也，則順其宜而治之。故恐其為蓊鬱也，啓闢之以除其類，不使之駢附而起者，則檉也，而檉之外又有椐
translation_en:
…almost exhaustively. A masterpiece! Admirable, admirable!
Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The brushwork is vigorous and the language dignified. This is writing that meets the standards and merits acceptance.”
To accomplish the work of clearing and opening the land by following the nature of things: such is how a worthy ruler establishes his state [?]. For only after human affairs have been put in order can Heaven’s will be received and upheld. As the people of Zhou founded their state, its development gradually became apparent in their management of the woods in this fashion. Would not the royal enterprise flourish through succeeding generations? Long ago, when the poet recounted the virtues of Tai Wang, Tai Bo, and Wang Ji, at this point he spoke of our Tai Wang at the beginning of his migration to Qi and settlement there. This was precisely the time for following the contours of the hills and cutting down trees. How, then, did he undertake this clearing and opening?
Dead trees ought to be removed, but where growth was luxuriant and dense, it was no easy matter to clear them all away. He therefore managed them according to their circumstances. Those pulled up and uprooted, cleared away and removed, discarded altogether with roots, stumps, branches, and trunks, were the standing dead trees and fallen timber whose vitality was already exhausted. Could any obstructive tangle still remain? Those pruned to allow passage and leveled to bring order, with care taken that their spacing and upright growth were all appropriate, were the shrubs and shoots growing in clusters and rows. Could any tangled growth still be left untended? When effort had thus been devoted to dead trees, fallen timber, shrubs, and shoots alike, the rugged, remote woods and hills henceforth had paths by which they could be traversed. “They went to Qi”: how swiftly it was becoming a gathering place for people and things!
Nor was this all. Ordinary trees might be dispensed with, but fine trees useful for timber had to be preserved. These he tended according to what suited them. Thus, fearing that they would become too thick and luxuriant, he opened and cleared the growth, removing others of their kind so that they would not grow crowded together. Such were the tamarisks; and besides the tamarisks there were also the ju trees…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
焉蓋非吾山林之植者皆剪伐以去之矣憂其
過繁冗也攘剔之以助其成必欲其挺拔而茂
者則檿也而檿之外又有柘焉蓋利吾民生之
用者又培植以養之矣夫於檉椐檿柘而皆從
事焉則林木之深阻者自是成有夷之行天作
高山其勃勃乎都邑之風乎是知太王於營建
之始而已弘開國之規其上承天命下啟王業
而中以慰歸市者之望真有不苟然者矣雖然
周自后稷以来凡三造而營于岐君子勤德小
===
人勤力其精神風氣已大異於去邠踰梁之日
及乎太伯王季之賢文王之聖而王業始定其
於險阻蓋備嘗之故詩人每深致其意焉嗣君
其皆知之否乎使其皆知之而皆念之則岐雖
世為周有可矣
春秋
公會齊人宋人救鄭莊公二十八年
魏廷美
同考試官教諭闞 批 此題塲中作者多取書人書
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 四十二
punctuated:
焉。蓋非吾山林之植者，皆剪伐以去之矣。憂其過繁冗也，攘剔之以助其成，必欲其挺拔而茂者，則檿也，而檿之外又有柘焉。蓋利吾民生之用者，又培植以養之矣。夫於檉椐檿柘而皆從事焉，則林木之深阻者，自是成有夷之行。天作高山，其勃勃乎都邑之風乎！是知太王於營建之始，而已弘開國之規，其上承天命，下啟王業，而中以慰歸市者之望，真有不苟然者矣。雖然，周自后稷以来，凡三造而營于岐，君子勤德，小人勤力，其精神風氣已大異於去邠踰梁之日。及乎太伯、王季之賢，文王之聖，而王業始定，其於險阻蓋備嘗之。故詩人每深致其意焉。嗣君其皆知之否乎？使其皆知之而皆念之，則岐雖世為周有，可矣。

春秋

公會齊人、宋人救鄭。莊公二十八年。

魏廷美

同考試官教諭闞批：此題塲中作者，多取書人書
translation_en:
…there were also ju trees. Whatever did not belong among the plants of our mountains and forests was cut down and removed. Concerned that the growth might become excessively dense, they cleared and thinned it to help it flourish, seeking above all to make the mountain mulberries grow tall and luxuriant; besides these there were also zhe mulberries. Whatever served the needs of our people's livelihood was cultivated and nurtured. By attending to the tamarisks, ju trees, mountain mulberries, and zhe mulberries alike, they made level roads through the deep, obstructed woodland. “Heaven made the lofty mountain”: how vigorously the character of a capital was taking shape! Thus we know that, from the very beginning of construction, King Tai had already laid out an expansive plan for founding the state. Above, he received Heaven's mandate; below, he opened the way for the royal enterprise; and in doing so he fulfilled the hopes of those who came to settle and trade. Truly, none of this was done carelessly.

Yet from Hou Ji onward, Zhou underwent three foundations before establishing itself at Qi. The gentlemen labored at virtue, and the common people labored with their strength. Their spirit and prevailing ethos were already greatly different from those of the days when they left Bin and crossed Mount Liang. Only with the worthiness of Tai Bo and Wang Ji, and the sageliness of King Wen, was the royal enterprise secured. They had indeed experienced every hardship and obstacle. Thus the poet repeatedly expressed these matters with profound feeling. Do succeeding rulers know them all? If they know them all and keep them all in mind, then Qi may indeed remain Zhou's possession for generations.

Spring and Autumn Annals

“The duke joined men of Qi and men of Song in coming to the aid of Zheng.” Twenty-eighth year of Duke Zhuang.

Wei Tingmei
