Officials who died in service generally received commendations and posthumous honors: was this not “establishing an exemplary influence”?

He decreed the opening of examinations and employed classical learning alone, thereby unifying moral principles and bringing customs into accord. In his instructions on founding the state, he invariably gave priority to the governing framework, ordering the eight affairs of government to prevent excess. The administration of the inner palace did not interfere in external government: was this not what is meant by “setting an example for one’s wife”? Princely branches of the imperial clan extended throughout the realm: was this not what is meant by “extensively enfeoffing those of the same surname”? Abolishing the Central Secretariat and establishing the Six Ministries followed the principle of dividing responsibilities and directing subordinate officials. Guarding against the northwest while giving less attention to the other foreign peoples followed the way of conciliating those far away and maintaining harmony with those nearby. He abolished such punishments as tattooing, mutilation of the legs [?], and cutting off the nose, warning against them all and leaving them unused: was this not the benevolence of reverent concern for those subject to punishment? As for the various [forms of music] that were frivolous [?], dissolute, licentious, and obscene …

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
樂皆禁而不作非克諧其聲乎凡此皆前
王所未行與行而未至者豈直漢高帝之所
不與雖唐虞三代無以過之矣然則我
國家靈長之祚何莫而不有賴於我
聖祖乎所以光繼述之圖者亦何法而不在我
聖祖乎書曰惟天聰明惟聖時憲我
聖祖之謂矣詩曰不愆不忘率由舊章此
聖子神孫所當留意以熙治化於無窮者也愚
敢竊之以為
===
今日誦
第二問
林應驄
同考試官訓導徐批策本錯舉前史疑義為
問此作答問如響而是非之真不爽學而有得者乎
同考試官教諭吳批論往事不拘成說要其
中本自有見此學造於微者也末以時勢為言尤為高識
考試官訓導夏批此策道古人事若指諸掌
遠慮出於言外蓋有未盡其詞者必有志用世之士
banxin: 福建鄉試錄七十一
punctuated:
樂皆禁而不作，非克諧其聲乎？凡此皆前王所未行與行而未至者，豈直漢高帝之所不與？雖唐虞三代，無以過之矣。然則我國家靈長之祚，何莫而不有賴於我聖祖乎？所以光繼述之圖者，亦何法而不在我聖祖乎？《書》曰：「惟天聰明，惟聖時憲。」我聖祖之謂矣。《詩》曰：「不愆不忘，率由舊章。」此聖子神孫所當留意，以熙治化於無窮者也。愚敢竊之，以為今日誦。

第二問
林應驄

同考試官訓導徐批：「策本錯舉前史疑義為問，此作答問如響，而是非之真不爽，學而有得者乎？」

同考試官教諭吳批：「論往事，不拘成說，要其中本自有見，此學造於微者也。末以時勢為言，尤為高識。」

考試官訓導夏批：「此策道古人事，若指諸掌，遠慮出於言外，蓋有未盡其詞者，必有志用世之士。」
translation_en:
…music was all prohibited and left unperformed: was this not his ability to harmonize its sounds? All these were things that former kings had either never undertaken or undertaken without fully achieving them. How could it be merely Emperor Gao of Han who fell short? Even the reigns of Tang Yao and Yu Shun and the Three Dynasties could not surpass them. Thus, in what respect does the enduring fortune of our dynasty not depend upon our Sagely Ancestor? And what model for gloriously carrying forward his undertaking is not to be found in our Sagely Ancestor? The Book of Documents says: “Heaven alone is keen of hearing and clear of sight; the sage alone takes it as his model.” This describes our Sagely Ancestor. The Book of Odes says: “Neither erring nor forgetting, follow the old statutes.” This is what his sagely sons and divine grandsons should keep in mind, so that enlightened government and moral transformation may flourish without end. I, in my ignorance, venture to appropriate these words as a recitation for today.

Second Question
Lin Yingcong

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor: “The policy question brings together doubtful points from earlier histories for examination. This essay answers them as promptly as an echo, without departing from the truth of right and wrong. Surely its author has gained understanding through study?”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “In discussing past events, he is not bound by established interpretations. What matters is that he has insights of his own: his learning has reached into subtleties. His concluding discussion of the circumstances of the present age shows especially lofty discernment.”

Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: “This policy essay recounts the affairs of the ancients as clearly as if pointing to something in the palm of one’s hand. Its far-reaching concerns extend beyond what is explicitly said; indeed, some things have been left unexpressed. Its author must be a scholar intent on putting his abilities to use in public service.”

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官訓導閔批博洽之學的實之見通融之
才具於此策見之其篇末數語尤見識慮之遠
對審於為治者優乎識者也審於論治者
明乎理者也蓋天下有可為之事必有可
守之理猶根荄之相屬而脉絡之相維也
學而達乎古今之故通乎時務之宜而必
推之以不易之理焉以治則善以論則定
而措諸天下也不難矣執事發策歷舉前
代政治之跡顧愚何足與言耶雖然亦嘗
===
聞諸師矣昔漢祖櫟陽寄治之日關中當
焫蕩之餘東歸之思宜未忘也蕭何大營
宮室以重四海之家誠有如劉元城所云
者然不趨生民之急而襲傾宮之風孰謂
垂統之君而可以示侈乎文帝入奉宗廟
之後天下方和洽之初嬴秦之舊尚自若
也賈誼請改制度以成一代之法誠有如
楊龜山所稱者然挾英銳之氣而嬰撫在
廷之臣孰謂專權之毀非有以自召乎入
banxin: 福建鄉試錄七十二
punctuated:
考試官訓導閔批：博洽之學、的實之見、通融之才，具於此策見之。其篇末數語，尤見識慮之遠。

對：審於為治者，優乎識者也；審於論治者，明乎理者也。蓋天下有可為之事，必有可守之理，猶根荄之相屬而脉絡之相維也。學而達乎古今之故，通乎時務之宜，而必推之以不易之理焉，以治則善，以論則定，而措諸天下也不難矣。執事發策，歷舉前代政治之跡，顧愚何足與言耶？雖然，亦嘗聞諸師矣。昔漢祖櫟陽寄治之日，關中當焫蕩之餘，東歸之思宜未忘也。蕭何大營宮室，以重四海之家，誠有如劉元城所云者。然不趨生民之急，而襲傾宮之風，孰謂垂統之君而可以示侈乎？文帝入奉宗廟之後，天下方和洽之初，嬴秦之舊尚自若也。賈誼請改制度，以成一代之法，誠有如楊龜山所稱者。然挾英銳之氣，而嬰撫在廷之臣，孰謂專權之毀非有以自召乎？入
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: This policy essay displays extensive learning, sound judgment, and versatile ability. Its final few sentences particularly reveal the far-reaching character of the writer’s insight and deliberation.

In reply: Those who exercise sound judgment in governing excel in discernment; those who exercise sound judgment in discussing government understand principles clearly. For every undertaking in the world that can be carried out, there must be a principle that can be upheld, just as roots are connected to one another and the body’s channels are linked together. Through learning, one comes to understand the circumstances of past and present and what is appropriate to current affairs; yet one must always examine these in light of unchanging principles. Applied to government, this produces good administration; applied to discussion, it produces firm conclusions. Putting it into practice throughout the realm will then present no difficulty. In setting this policy question, you have enumerated instances of government in earlier dynasties. How could someone as ignorant as I be worthy of discussing them with you? Nevertheless, I have heard something of these matters from my teachers.

When Gaozu of Han temporarily established his seat of government at Yueyang, Guanzhong had just suffered devastation by fire, and it is understandable that thoughts of returning east had not yet been forgotten. Xiao He undertook extensive palace construction to lend dignity to the household that ruled all within the Four Seas. There was indeed something in this of what Liu Yuancheng described. Yet, by failing to attend urgently to the people’s pressing needs and instead adopting the extravagant ways exemplified by the Qing Palace, how could a ruler founding a dynastic succession be justified in setting an example of extravagance?

After Emperor Wen entered upon the service of the ancestral temples, the realm was only beginning to enjoy harmony, while the old institutions of the Ying house of Qin remained unchanged. Jia Yi requested changes to the institutions so as to establish laws proper to the new dynasty. There was indeed something in this of what Yang Guishan praised. Yet, carried away by his brilliant and impetuous spirit, he antagonized the ministers at court [?]. Who could say that he had done nothing to bring upon himself the accusation of monopolizing power? [The page ends with 入, apparently a transcription error; the following passage continues …]

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
才之盛風俗之美取士以行故也楊綰奏
罷力田童子諸科其見蓋出於此呂祖謙
所以惜其天奪之速而未究於用設官以
禁設法以斂取財於商舊也張平叔乃議
坐市列肆之術其慮誠不及遠韓昌黎所
以駁其求利未得而斂怨已多玄史文儒
之學興宋元嘉於是好文矣蓋史者儒之
一端文者儒之餘事而老莊虛無非所為
教溫公肆為之辯者豈非為道之至耶鄰
===
里黨長之戶定魏李冲於是準古矣蓋隱
冒寢其餘奸課調省於常數而孤老貧病
得以自存鄭羲乃以為非者豈其識治之
淺耶德宗之末猜忌旣深聚斂愈急國家
大事動繫於相也經濟如陸贄顧不先於
竇參以李泌之智而為天下舉者乃如是
其疎乎慶曆之始上無失德下無失政朝
廷大體正不在激也好異如石介宜不列
於諫議非仲淹之賢而為世道計者能如
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 十七
punctuated:
才之盛，風俗之美，取士以行故也。楊綰奏罷力田、童子諸科，其見蓋出於此。呂祖謙所以惜其天奪之速而未究於用。
設官以禁，設法以斂，取財於商，舊也。張平叔乃議坐市列肆之術，其慮誠不及遠。韓昌黎所以駁其求利未得而斂怨已多。
玄史文儒之學興，宋元嘉於是好文矣。蓋史者儒之一端，文者儒之餘事，而老莊虛無，非所為教。溫公肆為之辯者，豈非為道之至耶？
鄰里黨長之戶定，魏李冲於是準古矣。蓋隱冒寢其餘奸，課調省於常數，而孤老貧病得以自存。鄭羲乃以為非者，豈其識治之淺耶？
德宗之末，猜忌旣深，聚斂愈急，國家大事動繫於相也。經濟如陸贄，顧不先於竇參，以李泌之智，而為天下舉者，乃如是其疎乎？
慶曆之始，上無失德，下無失政，朝廷大體正不在激也。好異如石介，宜不列於諫議。非仲淹之賢，而為世道計者，能如
translation_en:
…the abundance of talent and the excellence of customs resulted from selecting men for office on the basis of conduct. Yang Wan’s memorial proposing the abolition of the examinations for diligent farmers, prodigies, and other categories presumably arose from this understanding. This is why Lü Zuqian lamented that Heaven took him away so soon, before his ideas could be fully put into practice.
Establishing officials to enforce prohibitions and regulations to collect revenue—drawing wealth from merchants—was an old practice. Yet Zhang Pingshu proposed a scheme for conducting trade in markets and setting up shops; his deliberations truly lacked foresight. This is why Han Changli rebuked him for having already accumulated much resentment before securing the profits he sought.
Schools of metaphysics, history, literature, and Confucian learning arose: thus, during the Yuanjia era of the Song, literary culture was esteemed. Yet history is one branch of Confucian learning, and literary composition a subsidiary pursuit, while the emptiness and nonbeing taught by Laozi and Zhuangzi are not proper subjects of instruction. Was not Duke Wen’s extensive argument on this matter an expression of his utmost devotion to the Way?
The numbers of households under neighborhood, village, and community heads were fixed: thus Li Chong of the Wei took antiquity as his model. Concealment and fraudulent registration, along with other abuses, subsided; tax assessments were reduced below their customary amounts; and the orphaned, elderly, poor, and sick could maintain themselves. Yet Zheng Xi regarded this as wrong. Was this because his understanding of government was shallow?
Toward the end of Dezong’s reign, suspicion had grown deep and the extraction of revenue became ever more pressing; great affairs of state continually depended upon the chief councilor. Yet Lu Zhi, with all his capacity for ordering the realm, was not given precedence over Dou Can. Could Li Mi, for all his wisdom, have been so careless in recommending men for the sake of the realm?
At the beginning of the Qingli era, the ruler above had committed no lapse in virtue, and officials below had committed no failure in administration. The court’s proper general course certainly did not lie in provocative action. Someone as fond of unconventional views as Shi Jie ought not to have been placed among the remonstrance officials. Could anyone without Zhongyan’s worthiness have deliberated on the course of the age with such…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
是其深乎涼州三輔之蔽也涼州可棄先
帝開拓之蹟彼土武烈之士其可棄耶此
鄧隲之昧於永圖而虞詡所以爭之力者
宜矣強弱漢魏之形也魏固可伐一國尫
羸之衆數州窮蹙之民其可伐耶此姜維
之急於近功而譙周所以諷之切者是矣
令忌數更也李沆自叙報國首賛黙言之
功呂蒙正因論黃老而進撓魚之喻二者
何害乎鎮靜然或待天下於無人或後聖
===
賢於外教均之守文之過歟事必有法也
寇準斥檢例簿謂其壞政而損道杜衍命
書條式將以稽弊而肅奸二者或疑於異
同蓋在宰相以知人為務在掌銓以資序
為先均之制事之權歟然此特政之跡理
之經而已其時與勢不與焉夫否泰相懸
理亂相襲聖君賢相不相際時也遁於微
而制天下之機動於邇而窮天下之遠勢
也脩四者之說然後國事之得失而臣工
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 七十四
punctuated:
是其深乎？涼州，三輔之蔽也。涼州可棄，先帝開拓之蹟、彼土武烈之士，其可棄耶？此鄧隲之昧於永圖，而虞詡所以爭之力者，宜矣。強弱，漢魏之形也。魏固可伐，一國尫羸之衆、數州窮蹙之民，其可伐耶？此姜維之急於近功，而譙周所以諷之切者，是矣。
令忌數更也。李沆自叙報國，首賛黙言之功；呂蒙正因論黃老，而進撓魚之喻。二者何害乎鎮靜？然或待天下於無人，或後聖賢於外教，均之守文之過歟？事必有法也。寇準斥檢例簿，謂其壞政而損道；杜衍命書條式，將以稽弊而肅奸。二者或疑於異同。蓋在宰相，以知人為務；在掌銓，以資序為先。均之制事之權歟？
然此特政之跡、理之經而已，其時與勢不與焉。夫否泰相懸，理亂相襲，聖君賢相不相際，時也；遁於微而制天下之機，動於邇而窮天下之遠，勢也。脩四者之說，然後國事之得失而臣工
translation_en:
…have been so far-reaching? Liangzhou was the protective screen of the Three Capital Districts. Even if Liangzhou could be abandoned, could the achievements of the former emperors in extending the realm, and the valiant fighting men of that land, be abandoned? Deng Zhi failed here to understand long-term planning, and Yu Xu was therefore right to oppose him so vigorously. Strength and weakness defined the relative circumstances of Han and Wei. Wei was certainly a legitimate target for attack; but could the enfeebled host of a single state, the hard-pressed people of a few provinces, undertake that attack? Jiang Wei was too eager here for immediate success, and Qiao Zhou was therefore right to remonstrate with him so pointedly.
Frequent changes in ordinances are to be avoided. When Li Hang described his own service to the state, he first praised the merit of remaining silent; Lü Mengzheng, in discussing the teachings of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi, presented the analogy of disturbing fish while cooking them. How could either approach detract from tranquil government? Yet one perhaps treated the realm as though it had no capable men, while the other placed the sages and worthies below teachings outside the Confucian tradition. Were both instances of carrying adherence to established forms too far? Affairs must have governing rules. Kou Zhun rejected the register for consulting precedents, saying that it undermined government and impaired the Way; Du Yan ordered regulations to be written down, intending thereby to investigate abuses and discipline wrongdoers. These two approaches might seem inconsistent. Yet a chief councillor’s task is to discern men’s abilities, whereas an official responsible for personnel selection must give priority to qualifications and seniority. Were both exercises of discretion in handling affairs?
Yet these are merely the outward workings of government and the constant principles of order; the circumstances of the time and the configuration of forces are not included. Adversity and prosperity stand far apart, order and disorder succeed one another, and sagely rulers and worthy chief councillors fail to meet: this is a matter of the times. Remaining concealed in the subtle while controlling the pivotal workings of the realm, acting close at hand while reaching its farthest bounds: this is a matter of the configuration of forces. Elaborate the explanations of these four matters, and then the successes and failures of state affairs and the officials’ …

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
之淑慝人心之昭伏而物論之向背無隱
乎爾噫可虞之故何代無之計必有大於
此者矣惟執事者進而教之
第三問
倪組〔對〕
同考試官教諭閻批先正謂六藝之中樂之教尤
為親切古樂之亡久矣然其可考者亦每散見於經傳之間顧人不察
耳以是發問非不切用正欲以覘好古之學也今此策條對無遺得之
不覺躍然以喜宜錄之以勸來者
===
考試官訓導夏批對既詳悉而又能深究作樂之本
原是必有用之學也可嘉可嘉
考試官訓導閔批發明鍾律之妙明白簡易要有
得於心者亦將和其聲以鳴
國家之盛者歟錄之以俟
樂之道為至妙固不可以易而知樂之功
為至大尤不容以易而作夫樂不可以徒知
也察之於聲容之表而得之於心悟之餘
非妙夫音律者固無以與乎是矣然欲奉
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 七十五
punctuated:
之淑慝、人心之昭伏而物論之向背，無隱乎爾。噫！可虞之故，何代無之？計必有大於此者矣。惟執事者進而教之。
第三問
倪組〔對〕
同考試官教諭閻批：先正謂六藝之中，樂之教尤為親切。古樂之亡久矣，然其可考者，亦每散見於經傳之間，顧人不察耳。以是發問，非不切用，正欲以覘好古之學也。今此策條對無遺，得之，不覺躍然以喜。宜錄之，以勸來者。
考試官訓導夏批：對既詳悉，而又能深究作樂之本原，是必有用之學也。可嘉！可嘉！
考試官訓導閔批：發明鍾律之妙，明白簡易，要有得於心者。亦將和其聲，以鳴國家之盛者歟？錄之以俟。
樂之道為至妙，固不可以易而知；樂之功為至大，尤不容以易而作。夫樂不可以徒知也，察之於聲容之表，而得之於心悟之餘，非妙夫音律者，固無以與乎是矣。然欲奉
translation_en:
…the goodness or wickedness of officials, what is manifest or hidden in people’s hearts, and the support or opposition expressed in public opinion: none of these will remain concealed. Alas! What age has lacked causes for apprehension? Surely there must be plans greater than these. I ask you, who preside over this examination, to offer further instruction.
Third Question
Ni Zu 〔Response〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Yan, Instructor: A worthy predecessor said that, among the Six Arts, the teaching of music touches people especially closely. Ancient music has long been lost, yet evidence concerning it still appears here and there in the classics and their commentaries; people simply fail to notice it. To pose a question on this subject is by no means irrelevant to practical use: its precise purpose is to discern learning devoted to antiquity. This policy essay now answers every point without omission. On receiving it, I could not help leaping with delight. It should be recorded to encourage those who come after.
Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: The response is comprehensive and detailed, and moreover probes deeply into the fundamental basis for creating music. This is assuredly learning that will prove useful. Admirable! Admirable!
Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: It elucidates the subtleties of bells and pitch standards clearly, simply, and accessibly. In essence, the writer has grasped them in his heart. Will he also harmonize their sounds to proclaim the flourishing of the state? Let this be recorded in anticipation.
The Way of music is supremely subtle and certainly cannot be understood lightly; the efficacy of music is supremely great, and its creation must even less be undertaken lightly. Music cannot be merely understood intellectually. One must discern it beyond the outward manifestations of sound and movement, and grasp it through insight in the heart. Unless one has a subtle mastery of tones and pitch standards, one certainly cannot participate in this. Yet if one wishes to take it up…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
而作之以收天下大順之功則必有制作
之本者而後能之也又豈徒區區辨音律
者之擬哉執事發策下詢而有及于樂請
述所聞以告可乎嘗考之樂記有知聲知
音知樂之等而品以禽獸衆庶君子之别
其旨固微矣近世方氏以吾夫子與季札
爲君子之知樂蓋亦有見矣然夫子在齊
之所聞既已莫之可考而季札聘魯之所
觀實有足徴者札於諸風雅頌以及乎象
===
舞皆致夫深賛之詞可也而獨於小雅嘆
其爲周之衰文中子疑豳風烏乎樂必知
與二南相誤故也而獨於小雅反謂爲周
之盛者誠以小雅者周道盛衰之會也季
札之所言蓋當時親見夫周道之衰而不
覩乎文武成康之盛也文中子之所言蓋
謂文武之餘烈未忘而天下猶宗周也眉
山蘇氏有曰必合二子之說而小雅之道
備其言得之矣自是而後知樂者益鮮然
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 七十六
punctuated: 而作之，以收天下大順之功，則必有制作之本者而後能之也，又豈徒區區辨音律者之擬哉？執事發策下詢，而有及于樂，請述所聞以告，可乎？嘗考之《樂記》，有知聲、知音、知樂之等，而品以禽獸、衆庶、君子之别，其旨固微矣。近世方氏以吾夫子與季札爲君子之知樂，蓋亦有見矣。然夫子在齊之所聞，既已莫之可考，而季札聘魯之所觀，實有足徴者。札於諸風、雅、頌，以及乎象舞，皆致夫深賛之詞，可也；而獨於《小雅》，嘆其爲周之衰。文中子疑《豳風》，烏乎樂必知與《二南》相誤故也；而獨於《小雅》，反謂爲周之盛者，誠以《小雅》者周道盛衰之會也。季札之所言，蓋當時親見夫周道之衰，而不覩乎文武成康之盛也。文中子之所言，蓋謂文武之餘烈未忘，而天下猶宗周也。眉山蘇氏有曰：「必合二子之說，而《小雅》之道備。」其言得之矣。自是而後，知樂者益鮮，然
translation_en:
…and bring it into practice, thereby achieving universal concord throughout the realm, one must first possess the foundation for instituting music. How could someone merely skilled in distinguishing tones and pitch standards hope to equal this? You, honored examiners, have issued policy questions inviting our responses, and these touch upon music. May I set forth what I have learned?

I have examined the Record of Music, which distinguishes the levels of understanding sounds, understanding musical tones, and understanding music, assigning these respectively to beasts, ordinary people, and gentlemen. Its meaning is indeed subtle. In more recent times, Master Fang identified our Master Confucius and Ji Zha as examples of gentlemen who understood music; this, too, was an insightful judgment. Yet what the Master heard in Qi can no longer be ascertained, whereas what Ji Zha witnessed when visiting Lu as an envoy does provide evidence. It was fitting that Ji Zha offered profound praise for the various Airs, Court Hymns, and Eulogies, and even the Xiang dance; yet only of the Lesser Court Hymns did he lament that they represented Zhou’s decline. Wenzhongzi questioned the Airs of Bin, because they had been confused with the Two Nan sections [?; the intervening words concerning understanding music are garbled]. Yet of the Lesser Court Hymns alone, he instead said that they represented Zhou’s flourishing. This was truly because the Lesser Court Hymns stand at the juncture of the flourishing and decline of the Zhou order.

Ji Zha spoke as he did because he personally witnessed the decline of the Zhou order in his own time, but had not seen its flourishing under Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang. Wenzhongzi’s statement meant that the enduring achievements of Kings Wen and Wu had not been forgotten and that the realm still acknowledged Zhou as its sovereign. Master Su of Meishan said: “Only by combining the explanations of these two men can the meaning of the Lesser Court Hymns be fully understood.” His words grasped the matter. Thereafter, those who understood music became ever fewer; nevertheless…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
在晉則有荀勗焉得牛鐸於趙人而聲律
以諧故當時有暗解之稱其時又有阮咸
焉得玉尺於田夫而校量無異故當時有
神解之譽魏之陳仲孺依準以調八音而
輕重不失其倫隋之萬寶常扣器以成宮
商而高下曲盡其妙張文收之得玉磬於
潤州也知其爲黃鍾之闕楊收之見古鍾
於岑陽也識其爲姑洗之角他若信都芳
則仰觀雲色而知乎律管之飛灰王維則
===
俯按樂圖而知爲霓裳之三疊之數子者
皆精於音律而超出乎鏗鏘節奏之表固
非衆庶之知音可及矣然或昧於所本而
未造乎探本窮源之地比之季札之知德
者有間焉凡此猶皆就樂以論者至如司
馬遷之爲律書也其始雖不言律而言兵
不言兵之用而言兵之偃然又繼以文帝
偃兵息民以致召和之說蓋以天地之氣
正而律可造即所謂風氣正而十二律定
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 七十七
punctuated: 在晉則有荀勗焉，得牛鐸於趙人，而聲律以諧，故當時有暗解之稱。其時又有阮咸焉，得玉尺於田夫，而校量無異，故當時有神解之譽。魏之陳仲孺依準以調八音，而輕重不失其倫；隋之萬寶常扣器以成宮商，而高下曲盡其妙。張文收之得玉磬於潤州也，知其爲黃鍾之闕；楊收之見古鍾於岑陽也，識其爲姑洗之角。他若信都芳，則仰觀雲色而知乎律管之飛灰；王維則俯按樂圖而知爲霓裳之三疊。之數子者，皆精於音律，而超出乎鏗鏘節奏之表，固非衆庶之知音可及矣。然或昧於所本，而未造乎探本窮源之地，比之季札之知德者有間焉。凡此猶皆就樂以論者。至如司馬遷之爲《律書》也，其始雖不言律而言兵，不言兵之用而言兵之偃，然又繼以文帝偃兵息民以致召和之說。蓋以天地之氣正而律可造，即所謂風氣正而十二律定
translation_en: … In the Jin dynasty there was Xun Xu, who obtained an ox bell from a man of Zhao and thereby brought the pitches into harmony; hence he was praised at the time for his intuitive understanding. At the same time there was also Ruan Xian, who obtained a jade ruler from a farmer and found no discrepancy when comparing measurements; hence he was praised at the time for his inspired understanding. Chen Zhongru of Wei used a pitch-standard instrument to tune the eight classes of musical instruments, keeping their relative weight and force in proper order. Wan Baochang of Sui struck vessels to produce the gong and shang notes, fully realizing the subtleties of high and low pitches. When Zhang Wenshou obtained a jade chime stone in Runzhou, he recognized that it supplied the missing Huangzhong pitch. When Yang Shou saw an ancient bell in Cenyang, he recognized it as the jue note of the Guxian mode. Others included Xindu Fang, who looked up at the colors of the clouds and knew when ashes would fly from the pitch pipes, and Wang Wei, who looked down at a picture of musicians performing and recognized the third section of the Rainbow Skirt melody. These several men [?] were all expert in musical pitches, and their understanding transcended the mere ringing of instruments and patterns of rhythm. It was certainly beyond the musical discernment of ordinary people. Yet some were unclear about the underlying basis and had not reached the point of investigating its roots and tracing it to its source. They fell short of Ji Zha’s ability to discern virtue through music. All these examples still concern discussion of music in terms of music itself. As for Sima Qian’s composition of the Treatise on Pitch Standards, although he began by speaking of warfare rather than pitch standards, and of laying down arms rather than employing them, he followed this with an account of how Emperor Wen laid down arms and gave the people respite, thereby bringing about harmony. His point was that pitch standards could be established when the qi of Heaven and Earth was properly ordered. This is precisely what is meant by saying that when the winds and qi are properly ordered, the twelve pitch standards are fixed …

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
者陳氏謂其知制律之本不亦宜乎諸葛
亮治蜀雖曰干戈方勤於一隅設施未及
於天下然能左右昭烈出興漢討賊之師
爲仗義執言之舉天地之大義已明天下
之人心亦服所謂名正言順而事成者王
通謂其可興禮樂豈不信乎夫何文帝謙
讓未遑而昭烈中道崩殂後世之觀者蓋
不能無憾於斯矣然幸道未墜地有宋大
儒若晦庵朱子西山蔡氏應時以出而師
===
友之間倡明道學又以其暇力著爲通解
鍾律律呂新書二編自今觀之蔡氏之爲
新書也起於黃鍾終於度量權衡二十三
篇之間大抵皆古人已試之成法而參以
已意簡約周盡而無遺憾焉朱子因之爲
鍾律也起於陰陽辰位相生次序終於黃
鍾生十一律數法一十三篇之中大率多
蔡氏所著之成規而更互演繹尤爲明邃
而有可觀焉然則二書之在天下誠爲六
banxin: 福建鄉試録 七十八
punctuated:
者，陳氏謂其知制律之本，不亦宜乎？諸葛亮治蜀，雖曰干戈方勤於一隅，設施未及於天下，然能左右昭烈，出興漢討賊之師，爲仗義執言之舉。天地之大義已明，天下之人心亦服，所謂名正言順而事成者。王通謂其可興禮樂，豈不信乎？夫何文帝謙讓未遑，而昭烈中道崩殂，後世之觀者蓋不能無憾於斯矣。然幸道未墜地，有宋大儒若晦庵朱子、西山蔡氏，應時以出，而師友之間倡明道學，又以其暇力著爲《通解鍾律》、《律呂新書》二編。
自今觀之，蔡氏之爲《新書》也，起於黃鍾，終於度量權衡，二十三篇之間，大抵皆古人已試之成法，而參以已意，簡約周盡而無遺憾焉。朱子因之爲《鍾律》也，起於陰陽辰位相生次序，終於黃鍾生十一律數法，一十三篇之中，大率多蔡氏所著之成規，而更互演繹，尤爲明邃而有可觀焉。然則二書之在天下，誠爲六
translation_en:
…Master Chen’s statement that he understood the foundation of establishing the pitch standards—is it not fitting? When Zhuge Liang governed Shu, although warfare still occupied his efforts in one corner of the realm and his measures had not extended throughout All-under-Heaven, he nevertheless assisted Emperor Zhaolie in sending forth armies to restore the Han and punish the rebels, acting in defense of righteousness and speaking for a just cause. The great moral principles of Heaven and Earth were thereby made clear, and the hearts of the people throughout the realm submitted. This exemplified the saying that when names are correct, words accord with principle and affairs succeed. Was Wang Tong’s assertion that he could revive rites and music not indeed true? Yet why was Emperor Wen too modest and deferential to undertake this, while Emperor Zhaolie died midway through his endeavors? Later observers cannot but feel regret at this. Fortunately, however, the Way had not fallen into oblivion. Great Confucian scholars of the Song, such as Master Zhu, known as Hui’an, and Master Cai, known as Xishan, arose in response to their times. As teachers and friends, they promoted and elucidated the Learning of the Way, and with their remaining time and energy compiled two works: Bells and Pitch Standards from the Comprehensive Explanations, and the New Treatise on Pitch Standards.
Viewed from the present, Master Cai’s New Treatise begins with the Yellow Bell pitch and ends with measures of length and capacity and standards of weight. Its twenty-three chapters largely consist of established methods already tested by the ancients, supplemented by his own ideas. Concise yet comprehensive, they leave nothing wanting. Master Zhu drew upon this in composing Bells and Pitch Standards. It begins with the sequence in which pitches generate one another according to yin and yang and the twelve earthly-branch positions, and ends with numerical methods by which the Yellow Bell generates the other eleven pitches. Its thirteen chapters largely follow the established rules set out by Master Cai, further developing and elucidating their interrelations. They are especially clear and profound, and well worth studying. Thus, these two books, available to the world, truly serve as aids to the Six …

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
經之輔翼而可以補樂音之殘缺者矣我
太祖高皇帝創業于先
列聖相承繼統于後累葉重光甄陶天下百五
十餘年正積德久而禮樂可興之時也二
儒之書尚俟
聖天子采而用之因今而求之古循俗而入于
雅將見
和平之治可成而三代之樂亦可復見于
今日矣執事不以為妄進而教之雖曰未能
===
願學焉
第四問
鄭漳
同考試官學正陳批五策援經據史若千金之
市隨取而無不足者此篇於老成之智養才之望品藻明審而其模
寫忠際之大歷歷如在錄之以見尚友之志云
考試官訓導夏批老成處疑决變要自素養
而彈壓之望不可誣也此策筆力遒勁而諸賢英偉之烈發揚
殆盡高薦何忝
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 七十九
punctuated:
經之輔翼，而可以補樂音之殘缺者矣。我太祖高皇帝創業于先，列聖相承，繼統于後，累葉重光，甄陶天下百五十餘年，正積德久而禮樂可興之時也。二儒之書尚俟聖天子采而用之，因今而求之古，循俗而入于雅，將見和平之治可成，而三代之樂亦可復見于今日矣。執事不以為妄，進而教之。雖曰未能，願學焉。

第四問
鄭漳

同考試官學正陳批：五策援經據史，若千金之市，隨取而無不足者。此篇於老成之智、養才之望，品藻明審，而其模寫忠際之大，歷歷如在。錄之以見尚友之志云。

考試官訓導夏批：老成處疑决變，要自素養，而彈壓之望不可誣也。此策筆力遒勁，而諸賢英偉之烈發揚殆盡，高薦何忝？
translation_en:
…Classics, serving as aids to them and making good the deficiencies in musical sound. Our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the dynasty, and the successive sage emperors thereafter inherited its rule. For generation after generation their brilliance has shone anew, molding and nurturing all under Heaven for more than a hundred and fifty years. This is precisely the time when virtue, long accumulated, allows rites and music to flourish. The works of these two scholars still await adoption and use by the sage Son of Heaven. By proceeding from the present to seek out antiquity, and following customary practice toward refined standards, we shall see peaceful and harmonious government achieved, and the music of the Three Dynasties may appear again today. If you, honored sir, do not consider these words presumptuous, please receive me and instruct me. Though I cannot yet accomplish this, I wish to learn.

Fourth Question
Zheng Zhang

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, School Director: All five policy essays invoke the Classics and draw upon history. They are like a market stocked with a thousand gold pieces’ worth of goods: whatever one takes, there is no shortage. This essay offers clear and judicious assessments of the wisdom of seasoned men and the expectations attached to nurturing talent. Its portrayal of the greatness of “loyalty’s bounds” [?] is so vivid that it seems present before our eyes. I have selected it to show his aspiration to take the worthies of antiquity as his friends.

Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: The ability of seasoned men to address uncertainties and resolve crises must come from sustained cultivation; their prestige in maintaining order cannot be feigned. This policy essay is written with vigorous force and brings out almost to the full the heroic and magnificent achievements of the worthies. What cause for shame could there be in recommending it highly?

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官訓導閔批前二試已知子之奇而此策
文思沛乎與先賢光大之氣若競爽然者得士如此無負科目
也已
對人君任天下之重必有以圖天下之務
人臣成天下之務必有以負天下之望蓋
天下之大事與所謂大疑者其爲幾至要
爲責至難而爲功亦至大也人才閱世之
淺深繋國之輕重而治亂因以占之故周
章疎謬者非練達之士而安危之幾毅然
===
有立者必其更事多而思慮熟者耳蓋嘗
考夫易之大過言大過之時非有大過人
之才不能濟也詩曰雖無老成人尚有典
刑言老成之重於典刑也故太公奮跡磻
溪而成燮伐之功畢公弼亮四世而重保
釐之位是皆所謂老成之才而濟大過之
時者也有國者其獨得不加意於若人哉
愚請得而條陳之夫抱關夷門侯生似可
鄙矣然信陵執轡而建救趙之謀少不如
banxin: 福建鄉試錄八十
punctuated:
考試官訓導閔批：前二試已知子之奇，而此策文思沛乎，與先賢光大之氣若競爽然者。得士如此，無負科目也已。
對：人君任天下之重，必有以圖天下之務；人臣成天下之務，必有以負天下之望。蓋天下之大事與所謂大疑者，其爲幾至要，爲責至難，而爲功亦至大也。人才閱世之淺深，繋國之輕重，而治亂因以占之。故周章疎謬者非練達之士，而安危之幾毅然有立者，必其更事多而思慮熟者耳。蓋嘗考夫《易》之《大過》，言大過之時，非有大過人之才不能濟也。《詩》曰：「雖無老成人，尚有典刑。」言老成之重於典刑也。故太公奮跡磻溪，而成燮伐之功；畢公弼亮四世，而重保釐之位。是皆所謂老成之才，而濟大過之時者也。有國者，其獨得不加意於若人哉？愚請得而條陳之。夫抱關夷門，侯生似可鄙矣；然信陵執轡，而建救趙之謀。少不如
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: In the first two sessions I already recognized your exceptional ability. In this policy essay, your literary thought pours forth abundantly, seeming to vie in brilliance with the expansive spirit of the worthies of old. To obtain a scholar such as this is indeed to fulfill the purpose of the examinations.
Answer: A ruler who bears the weight of All under Heaven must have the means to plan its affairs; a minister who accomplishes those affairs must have the means to shoulder its expectations. For the great affairs of All under Heaven and what are called its great uncertainties involve junctures of the utmost importance, responsibilities of the utmost difficulty, and achievements of the utmost magnitude. The depth or shallowness of a talented man's experience of the world bears upon the strength or weakness of the state, and from this one can gauge whether order or disorder will prevail. Thus those who are flustered, careless, and mistaken are not men of seasoned judgment. Those who stand resolute at the turning point between security and danger must be men who have experienced many affairs and considered them thoroughly.
I have examined the hexagram Great Exceeding in the Book of Changes. It says that in a time of great exceeding, none can bring matters to a successful conclusion without talents that greatly exceed those of others. The Book of Odes says: “Though there are no mature and experienced men, there are still established models.” This speaks of the importance of such men in relation to established models. Thus the Grand Duke, Taigong, rose from Panxi and achieved the merit of assisting the punitive campaign; the Duke of Bi, Bi Gong, assisted and enlightened four generations of rulers and lent weight to the office charged with protection and governance. These were all men of what is called mature and experienced talent, who brought matters to a successful conclusion in times of great exceeding. Can those who possess a state fail to give special attention to such men?
I venture to request leave to set this out point by point. Holding the gate at Yimen, Master Hou might have seemed contemptible. Yet the Lord of Xinling took the reins for him, and he devised the plan to rescue Zhao. The young could not equal … [?]

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
入燭之武信無能矣然秦伯請盟而紓鄭
侯之難王翦動衆六十萬一舉而破荆楚
豈框怯之所能趙充國留屯十二事全策
而制先零固好謀而有濟神龍之初唐之
宗廟巳爲周矣張柬之提兵禁衛中宗之
位巳正而上陽之號遂尊天寶之末唐之
王室巳如贅矣郭子儀建節朔方兩京之
績既收而涇陽之盟彌固淮蔡之役成計
幾於見沮裴度身親戎務而僭亂以之削
===
平真宗之立羣小幾於造變呂端首折異
謀而大位以之鎮定新法既行致鄭公之
解郡元祐之薦煩彥博而再來然或屢疏
大事而注天子之思或獨著風裁而起遠
人之敬其所以屬當時之望者重矣正色
立朝乃王曾之大節重厚如勃實韓琦之
大忠然或感動兩宮而左右畏憚或歷任
三朝而繫國安危其所以任社稷之重者
力矣自今觀之士生其時以才則周以智
banxin: 公昌試錄八十一
punctuated:
入燭之武信無能矣，然秦伯請盟，而紓鄭侯之難。王翦動衆六十萬，一舉而破荆楚，豈框怯之所能？趙充國留屯十二事，全策而制先零，固好謀而有濟。神龍之初，唐之宗廟巳爲周矣，張柬之提兵禁衛，中宗之位巳正，而上陽之號遂尊。天寶之末，唐之王室巳如贅矣，郭子儀建節朔方，兩京之績既收，而涇陽之盟彌固。淮蔡之役，成計幾於見沮，裴度身親戎務，而僭亂以之削平。真宗之立，羣小幾於造變，呂端首折異謀，而大位以之鎮定。新法既行，致鄭公之解郡；元祐之薦，煩彥博而再來。然或屢疏大事而注天子之思，或獨著風裁而起遠人之敬，其所以屬當時之望者重矣。正色立朝，乃王曾之大節；重厚如勃，實韓琦之大忠。然或感動兩宮而左右畏憚，或歷任三朝而繫國安危，其所以任社稷之重者力矣。
自今觀之，士生其時，以才則周，以智
translation_en:
… Zhu Zhiwu indeed seemed incapable [?]; yet the Earl of Qin requested a covenant, thereby relieving the Marquis of Zheng’s distress. Wang Jian mobilized six hundred thousand men and defeated Jing-Chu in a single campaign. Could a timid man [?] have accomplished this? Zhao Chongguo submitted twelve proposals for keeping troops in agricultural garrisons and subdued the Xianling through a comprehensive strategy: he was indeed skilled in planning and effective in execution.
At the beginning of the Shenlong era, the ancestral temples of Tang had already become those of Zhou. Zhang Jianzhi led troops of the palace guard; Zhongzong was duly restored to the throne, while the title of the sovereign at Shangyang was accorded honor. At the end of the Tianbao era, the Tang royal house had become like a mere appendage. Guo Ziyi took up military command at Shuofang; having achieved the recovery of the two capitals, he further secured the covenant at Jingyang. During the campaign against Huai and Cai, the settled plan nearly met with obstruction. Pei Du personally attended to military affairs, and the usurping rebels were consequently suppressed. At Zhenzong’s accession, a group of petty men nearly fomented an upheaval. Lü Duan took the lead in thwarting their conspiracy, and the imperial throne was thereby secured.
Once the New Policies were implemented, the Duke of Zheng relinquished his prefectural charge. A recommendation during the Yuanyou era required Yanbo to return once more. Whether repeatedly submitting memorials on great affairs and engaging the emperor’s attention, or displaying a distinctive moral bearing and winning the respect of distant peoples, these men bore a weighty responsibility as the focus of their contemporaries’ hopes. Standing at court with an uncompromising countenance was Wang Zeng’s great integrity; being dignified and substantial like Zhou Bo was Han Qi’s great loyalty. Whether moving the sovereigns of the two palaces so that their attendants stood in awe, or serving through three reigns with the state’s security depending upon them, they had the strength to bear the weight of the altars of soil and grain.
Viewed from the present, these men, born into their respective times, were comprehensive in their abilities; in their wisdom …

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
則審以成天下之事則大矣而後世猶不
能無異論者何也愚嘗慨夫勇如王翦以
怯見棄而卒自衒其能智如侯生以術見
用而乃幸售其謀諸武既誅大義不容以
不正質如柬之顧貽反噬之慘勲庸既顯
晚節不可以不脩賢如裴度乃為自安之
計之數子者智有餘而養則未純才可資
而望或不足是故君子所以有遺憾也若
夫令公之忠貫金石而讒邪之間消信行
===
蠻貊而反側之變弭而先儒許之為大臣
者豈無所據乎魏公之再决大策奠天下
之危疑矢心狥國畧一身之成敗而先儒
擬之為間氣者抑有所見乎鄭公之两使
點虜五辭起復忠義之氣爭光日月而史
稱其有仁人之利者此也潞公之四代元
臣累秉鈞軸公忠之烈聞于四夷史贊其
有大臣之槩者是也之四子者養既深而
德則厚才既全而望復隆取人三代而下
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 八十二
punctuated:
則審，以成天下之事則大矣。而後世猶不能無異論者，何也？愚嘗慨夫勇如王翦，以怯見棄，而卒自衒其能；智如侯生，以術見用，而乃幸售其謀。諸武既誅，大義不容以不正，質如柬之，顧貽反噬之慘；勲庸既顯，晚節不可以不脩，賢如裴度，乃為自安之計。之數子者，智有餘而養則未純，才可資而望或不足，是故君子所以有遺憾也。
若夫令公之忠貫金石，而讒邪之間消；信行蠻貊，而反側之變弭，而先儒許之為大臣者，豈無所據乎？魏公之再决大策，奠天下之危疑，矢心狥國，畧一身之成敗，而先儒擬之為間氣者，抑有所見乎？鄭公之两使點虜，五辭起復，忠義之氣爭光日月，而史稱其有仁人之利者，此也。潞公之四代元臣，累秉鈞軸，公忠之烈聞于四夷，史贊其有大臣之槩者，是也。之四子者，養既深而德則厚，才既全而望復隆。取人三代而下
translation_en:
…in judgment they were discerning, and their accomplishments in the affairs of the realm were great. Why, then, have later generations nevertheless voiced differing judgments about them? I have often lamented that someone as courageous as Wang Jian was rejected as cowardly and ultimately had to advertise his own ability; that someone as wise as Master Hou gained employment through his stratagems, yet depended on good fortune to have his plan accepted. Once the members of the Wu clan had been executed, the great principles of righteousness had to be set right; yet even someone of Zhang Jianzhi’s substance brought upon himself the calamity of a retaliatory attack. Once distinguished achievements had been established, integrity in later life still had to be cultivated; yet even someone as worthy as Pei Du devised plans for his own security. These men possessed ample intelligence, but their self-cultivation was not yet pure. Their talents could be put to use, but their standing sometimes fell short. This is why the gentleman finds grounds for regret.
As for Lord Guo Ziyi, his loyalty penetrated metal and stone, dissolving the estrangement sown by slanderers and the wicked; his trustworthiness prevailed among the Man and Mo peoples, quelling disturbances among the disaffected. Could earlier Confucian scholars have lacked grounds for acclaiming him as a great minister? The Duke of Wei, Han Qi, twice settled momentous affairs of state, bringing stability amid the realm’s peril and uncertainty. He pledged his heart to serve his country to the utmost, disregarding his own success or failure. Surely earlier Confucian scholars had something in view when they likened him to a man endowed with the exceptional vital force that appears only at rare intervals? The Duke of Zheng, Fu Bi, twice served as envoy to the northern enemy [?] and five times declined recall to office during mourning. His spirit of loyalty and righteousness rivaled the sun and moon in radiance: this is why the histories credited him with the beneficence of a humane man [?]. The Duke of Lu, Wen Yanbo, was a senior statesman under four sovereigns and repeatedly held the reins of government. His outstanding public devotion and loyalty were known among the peoples of all four quarters: this is what the histories meant in praising him for the bearing of a great minister. These four men possessed profound self-cultivation and substantial virtue, comprehensive talents and exalted reputations. In selecting men from the ages after the Three Dynasties…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
此其優者耳至於區區智謀之末如燭之
武者何足以爲士哉抑嘗論老成之有益
於天下也譬如蓍龜之爲信楩柟之爲材
求而用之天下之事無不濟也違而棄之
天下之事無不悖也故人君遇之必隆其
禮任之必竭其忠蓋有倚其夙昔之望而
不責其造次之功者矣嗚呼太公尚父之
號畢公父師之尊誠非致文貌於一朝一
夕之間而已此固圖任老成之意也愚生
===
芹曝之誠願爲
今日獻焉謹對
第五問
廖世昭
同考試官教諭沈批策本時務場中答者多
草草蹈襲以應故事不然漫為大言無徴於用良為可厭今
觀此篇用事引證區處精切蓋亦識古今事勢者末復以
教化立說尤出入數倍得士如此可以薦矣
同考試官教諭杜批意語明秀格製典古故
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 八十三
punctuated:
此其優者耳。至於區區智謀之末，如燭之武者，何足以爲士哉？抑嘗論老成之有益於天下也，譬如蓍龜之爲信、楩柟之爲材，求而用之，天下之事無不濟也；違而棄之，天下之事無不悖也。故人君遇之，必隆其禮；任之，必竭其忠。蓋有倚其夙昔之望，而不責其造次之功者矣。嗚呼！太公尚父之號、畢公父師之尊，誠非致文貌於一朝一夕之間而已，此固圖任老成之意也。愚生芹曝之誠，願爲今日獻焉。謹對。
第五問
廖世昭
同考試官教諭沈批：策本時務，場中答者多草草蹈襲，以應故事；不然，漫為大言，無徴於用，良為可厭。今觀此篇，用事引證，區處精切，蓋亦識古今事勢者。末復以教化立說，尤出入數倍。得士如此，可以薦矣。
同考試官教諭杜批：意語明秀，格製典古，故
translation_en:
…these were among the finest. As for petty feats of clever stratagem, such as those of Zhu Zhiwu, how could they suffice to make one a worthy scholar? I have also considered how seasoned and mature men benefit the realm. They are like yarrow stalks and tortoise shells in their trustworthiness, or pian and nan trees in their usefulness as timber. Seek them out and employ them, and no undertaking in the realm will fail; disregard and discard them, and no undertaking will escape going awry. Thus, when a ruler receives them, he must accord them the highest courtesies; when he entrusts them with office, he must elicit their utmost loyalty. Indeed, he should rely on their long-established standing without demanding achievements at a moment’s notice. Ah! The Grand Duke’s designation as “Revered Father” and the Duke of Bi’s honored status as “Father and Preceptor” were surely more than outward courtesies extended for a single morning or evening. They expressed precisely the intention to seek out and employ seasoned and mature men. With the sincerity of a humble student offering celery or the warmth of the sun, I wish to present this counsel to the present government. Respectfully submitted in reply.
Fifth Question
Liao Shizhao
Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: Policy questions are fundamentally concerned with current affairs. Most candidates in the examination hall hastily repeat familiar formulas to satisfy established procedure; otherwise, they indulge in grand pronouncements with no demonstrated practical application. This is truly tiresome. Looking now at this essay, its use of historical examples and supporting evidence, and its proposals for handling affairs, are precise and pertinent. Its author evidently understands the circumstances of affairs both past and present. At the end, he further grounds his argument in moral education, surpassing the others several times over [?]. Having found a scholar like this, we may recommend him.
Comment by Associate Examiner Du, Instructor: The ideas and language are clear and elegant; the form and composition are classically dignified. Thus …

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
時大務摘發呈露而無餘秘非胷中素有尺度疇能有是
歟古人以匹夫而懐抱天下之憂子殆有見乎徒羡讀羨
考試官訓導夏批考究詳明識見高遠眞豪俊
傑之士也他日幹济治道必有以自致於
君民者是用錄之以俟
考試官訓導閔批用事的而立論確當是素抱
經濟大畧者
對治世者必審夫善俗之幾而舉夫制變
之要焉天下之生乆矣未有無弊之事亦
===
未有無患之時抑豈終無拯之之術與禦
之之法哉亦惟曰深求其故而預為之備
爾是蓋推之天下而皆然者矧一方乎執
事下詢末學乃有憂於延邵之人才泉漳
之風俗鹽法之困滯貢賦之逋負而於寢
兵郵荒之故尤加之意焉此正愚生之所
欲言也敢舉其詳以對昔胡瑗之在蘇湖
立二齋而法敎行陸贄之告德宗用明恕
而訟獄正劉晏出而緡筭增李渤請而攤
banxin: 福建鄉試八十四
punctuated:
時大務，摘發呈露而無餘秘，非胷中素有尺度，疇能有是歟？古人以匹夫而懐抱天下之憂，子殆有見乎！徒羡讀羨。

考試官訓導夏批：考究詳明，識見高遠，眞豪俊傑之士也。他日幹济治道，必有以自致於君民者，是用錄之以俟。

考試官訓導閔批：用事的而立論確，當是素抱經濟大畧者。

對：治世者必審夫善俗之幾，而舉夫制變之要焉。天下之生乆矣，未有無弊之事，亦未有無患之時。抑豈終無拯之之術與禦之之法哉？亦惟曰深求其故，而預為之備爾。是蓋推之天下而皆然者，矧一方乎！執事下詢末學，乃有憂於延邵之人才、泉漳之風俗、鹽法之困滯、貢賦之逋負，而於寢兵郵荒之故尤加之意焉。此正愚生之所欲言也，敢舉其詳以對。昔胡瑗之在蘇湖，立二齋而法敎行；陸贄之告德宗，用明恕而訟獄正；劉晏出而緡筭增；李渤請而攤
translation_en:
…the great affairs of the time are brought out and laid bare, leaving nothing concealed. Unless one had long possessed sound standards of judgment within, who could achieve this? Men of antiquity, though private individuals, cherished concern for all under Heaven. You seem to have understood this! One can only admire it upon reading [?].

Comment by Examiner Xia, Assistant Instructor: His investigations are thorough and clear, and his understanding is lofty and far-reaching. He is truly a man of outstanding talent. In the future, through his capable contribution to good government, he will surely render service to the ruler and the people. For this reason, we record his essay and await what he will accomplish.

Comment by Examiner Min, Assistant Instructor: His use of historical precedents is precise, and his arguments are sound. He must be someone who has long harbored broad plans for ordering the realm and aiding its people.

Answer: Those who govern the world must examine carefully the means of improving popular customs and grasp the essentials of responding to change. Human life under Heaven has endured long: no undertaking has ever been free of abuses, nor has any age been free of troubles. Yet can it be that there are ultimately no means of remedying them or methods of warding them off? One need only probe deeply into their causes and prepare against them in advance. This holds true when extended throughout the realm; how much more so within a single region!

You, honored officials, have condescended to question us humble students, expressing concern about talented men in Yanping and Shaowu, popular customs in Quanzhou and Zhangzhou, the difficulties and stagnation of the salt administration, and arrears in tribute and taxes. You give particular attention to the causes of military inactivity, postal affairs, and famine [?]. These are precisely the matters that I, an ignorant student, wish to discuss. I venture to set out the particulars in reply.

Formerly, when Hu Yuan was in Suzhou and Huzhou, he established two instructional divisions, and his educational methods took effect. When Lu Zhi advised Emperor Dezong, clarity and forbearance were employed, and litigation and criminal adjudication were set right. When Liu Yan entered office, monetary revenues increased. Li Bo petitioned, and the apportionment …

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
逃免龔遂守渤海而盜賊斂趙抃治越州
而荒政脩此皆古人已試之明驗也然時
異世殊而理則可同風漓俗變而法未成
改是以爲之制者必審推移之術而示勸
沮之方焉蓋延邵二郡諸賢道學之源遠
矣然猶有置書院以延禮師儒有詣學宮
而親爲講授嗣是而首風化者亦嘗倣而
行之耶漳泉之地大儒過化之澤深矣然
猶有閉戶糶以止兄弟之告訐諭大義而
===
令頑民之自思繼此而柄邦成者亦嘗舉
而措之耶嚴私販之條厲侵奪之禁則夙
弊除而榷利興此其法之大凡爾抑不知
今日鹾務之司處盜竊之奸有如當時之
爲宣慰者否乎信蠲除之令重乾沒之罰
則民隱通而逋負復此其政之梗槩爾抑
不知今日守牧之任汰虛加之額有如昔
人之爲宣撫者否乎是則學之所以廢訟
之所以繁法之所以沮而賦之所以稽員
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 九十五
punctuated: 逃免，龔遂守渤海而盜賊斂，趙抃治越州而荒政脩，此皆古人已試之明驗也。然時異世殊，而理則可同；風漓俗變，而法未成改。是以爲之制者，必審推移之術，而示勸沮之方焉。蓋延邵二郡，諸賢道學之源遠矣，然猶有置書院以延禮師儒，有詣學宮而親爲講授。嗣是而首風化者，亦嘗倣而行之耶？漳泉之地，大儒過化之澤深矣，然猶有閉戶糶以止兄弟之告訐，諭大義而令頑民之自思。繼此而柄邦成者，亦嘗舉而措之耶？嚴私販之條，厲侵奪之禁，則夙弊除而榷利興，此其法之大凡爾。抑不知今日鹾務之司，處盜竊之奸，有如當時之爲宣慰者否乎？信蠲除之令，重乾沒之罰，則民隱通而逋負復，此其政之梗槩爾。抑不知今日守牧之任，汰虛加之額，有如昔人之爲宣撫者否乎？是則學之所以廢、訟之所以繁、法之所以沮而賦之所以稽員
translation_en:
…the taxes apportioned to cover absconders were remitted. When Gong Sui governed Bohai, banditry subsided; when Zhao Bian governed Yuezhou, famine relief was put in good order. These are all clear proofs of measures tried by men of former times. Yet although times and circumstances differ, the principles may be shared; although public morals decline and customs change, the methods need not be altered [?]. Thus those who frame regulations must carefully consider how to adapt them and make clear the means of encouragement and restraint.

In the two prefectures of Yanping and Shaowu, the Learning of the Way transmitted by worthy men has a long pedigree. Nevertheless, some established academies to invite and honor learned teachers, while others visited the prefectural schools and lectured in person. Have those who subsequently took the lead in moral transformation ever followed these examples in practice? In Zhangzhou and Quanzhou, the great Confucian masters left a profound legacy of transforming people wherever they went. Nevertheless, some closed their doors to grain sales [?] to stop brothers from bringing accusations against one another, and explained the great moral obligations to make recalcitrant people reflect for themselves. Have those who subsequently wielded authority over local administration ever put these measures into practice?

Make the regulations against illicit trading strict and enforce the prohibitions against encroachment and seizure: longstanding abuses will then be eliminated and monopoly revenues will flourish. These are merely the broad outlines of the method. Yet I wonder whether those now responsible for salt administration deal with fraudulent theft as did the Pacification Commissioner (xuanwei) of that time. Faithfully implement orders for tax remission and impose heavy penalties for embezzlement: the people’s hidden sufferings will then be made known and arrears recovered. These are merely the broad outlines of the policy. Yet I wonder whether those now serving as local governors eliminate fictitious additions to tax quotas as did the Pacification Commissioner (xuanfu) of former times. Thus, the reasons why learning falls into neglect, litigation proliferates, regulations are frustrated, and taxes are delayed [?]…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
者其原當有所考矣至如遏盜之起救歲
之侵又愚生之所願學者也夫汀漳乃甌
閩之奧引帶贛吉而喉襟潮廣興泉為梯
航之會揭以崇山而巨海敵焉值兵則借
調於鄰藩遇荒則仰給於他郡誠有如執
事之憂者蓋盜賊之禍非一日矣然為今
之計者三總三省之衝置𠳲戍之鎮以解
其嘯聚割數里之地立撫馭之邑以誘其
向方然必斷以歐文忠所謂州郡設兵為
===
備明賞罰之格嚴捕盜之官而後為確論
也荒歉之變嘗迭見矣然當今所務者三
放貧民之負復陂渠之業以厚其本務通
海舶之商轉廣東之粟以貿其有無然必
參以吕東萊所謂謹預備之政所在蓄積
有可均處使之流通而後能兼濟也凡此
固所謂舉其要以蓄其備者耳然猶未探
其本也夫天下之情不患於不協而患於
不一天下之風不患其不振而患其不同
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 八十六
punctuated:
者，其原當有所考矣。至如遏盜之起，救歲之侵，又愚生之所願學者也。夫汀漳乃甌閩之奧，引帶贛吉，而喉襟潮廣；興泉為梯航之會，揭以崇山，而巨海敵焉。值兵則借調於鄰藩，遇荒則仰給於他郡，誠有如執事之憂者。蓋盜賊之禍非一日矣，然為今之計者三：總三省之衝，置𠳲戍之鎮，以解其嘯聚；割數里之地，立撫馭之邑，以誘其向方。然必斷以歐文忠所謂「州郡設兵為備」，明賞罰之格，嚴捕盜之官，而後為確論也。
荒歉之變嘗迭見矣，然當今所務者三：放貧民之負，復陂渠之業，以厚其本務；通海舶之商，轉廣東之粟，以貿其有無。然必參以吕東萊所謂「謹預備之政」，所在蓄積，有可均處，使之流通，而後能兼濟也。凡此固所謂舉其要以蓄其備者耳，然猶未探其本也。夫天下之情，不患於不協，而患於不一；天下之風，不患其不振，而患其不同。
translation_en:
…their underlying causes surely deserve investigation. As for preventing bandit uprisings and relieving the ravages of bad harvests, these too are matters about which this unworthy student wishes to learn. Ting and Zhang lie in the interior of Ou and Min, linking Gan and Ji and commanding the approaches to Chao and Guang. Xing and Quan are meeting points of overland and maritime routes, raised against lofty mountains and facing the vast sea. When warfare occurs, troops must be borrowed from neighboring provincial administrations; when famine strikes, supplies must be sought from other prefectures. There are indeed grounds for the concerns you have expressed. The scourge of banditry is certainly no recent development. There are, however, three measures to consider at present: bring the strategic junction of the three provinces under unified control and establish a garrison command [?] to break up the bandits’ gatherings; carve out a tract of several li and establish a county to pacify and govern them, encouraging them to turn toward proper conduct. Yet a sound proposal must ultimately rest on what Ouyang Wenzhong called “stationing troops in prefectures as a precaution”: make the rules for rewards and punishments clear and hold the officials responsible for apprehending bandits to strict account.
Disasters of famine and poor harvests have repeatedly occurred. There are, however, three urgent tasks at present: cancel the debts of the poor and restore reservoirs and irrigation channels, thereby strengthening their fundamental occupation of agriculture; facilitate seaborne trade and transport grain from Guangdong, thereby exchanging surpluses to meet shortages. Yet these measures must also incorporate what Lü Donglai called “careful administration of advance preparations”: build up reserves everywhere and, wherever supplies can be shared, enable them to circulate. Only then can relief reach all. All these measures merely amount to identifying the essentials and building up provisions against emergencies; they still do not reach the root of the matter. As for the dispositions of people throughout the realm, the concern is not that they fail to accord, but that they lack unity; as for the customs of the realm, the concern is not that they lack vigor, but that they are not uniform.

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
先王之世學不雜而才愈多刑不繁而姦
自伏民緩其末而勤於其上化以行而俗
以美夫豈多術哉誠以夸毗偷惰之習不
作而恭儉卑巽之懿興也是故道德者先
王所以一其情而同其俗者也而夫子論
政必以德禮先焉當是時也必有嚴其制
而謹為之防使佻淫不得以相扇貧富不
得以相耀回其心以向於道然後士一其
業民一其務頹風振而和氣臻刑罰省盜
===
賊息而年穀蕃育矣嗚呼十室之邑必有
忠信況閩舊齒
上國而乃無可語者乎先正有言不能行諸天
下猶可驗諸一方惟執事者念之士庶幸
甚謹對
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 八十七
punctuated:
先王之世，學不雜而才愈多，刑不繁而姦自伏，民緩其末而勤於其上，化以行而俗以美，夫豈多術哉？誠以夸毗偷惰之習不作，而恭儉卑巽之懿興也。是故道德者，先王所以一其情而同其俗者也。而夫子論政，必以德禮先焉。當是時也，必有嚴其制而謹為之防，使佻淫不得以相扇，貧富不得以相耀，回其心以向於道，然後士一其業，民一其務，頹風振而和氣臻，刑罰省，盜賊息，而年穀蕃育矣。
嗚呼！十室之邑，必有忠信，況閩舊齒上國，而乃無可語者乎？先正有言：「不能行諸天下，猶可驗諸一方。」惟執事者念之，士庶幸甚。謹對。
translation_en:
In the age of the former kings, learning was unmixed, yet men of talent were all the more numerous; punishments were not multiplied, yet wrongdoers submitted of themselves. The people gave little attention to secondary pursuits and diligently served their superiors [?]; moral transformation took effect, and customs became admirable. Did this require many techniques? It was truly because habits of flattery, indolence, and sloth did not arise, while the virtues of reverence, frugality, humility, and deference flourished. Thus moral virtue was the means by which the former kings united the people's sentiments and brought their customs into accord. Whenever the Master discussed government, he invariably put virtue and ritual propriety first. At the present time, there must be those who enforce regulations strictly and carefully establish safeguards, so that frivolity and licentiousness cannot spread through mutual incitement, and rich and poor cannot vie in ostentation. They must turn people's hearts toward the Way. Only then will scholars devote themselves single-mindedly to their studies and the people to their occupations. Declining customs will be revived, harmonious influences will arrive, punishments will diminish, banditry will cease, and the annual grain crops will flourish.
Ah! Even in a settlement of ten households, there must be someone loyal and trustworthy. How much more so in Fujian, long ranked among the civilized regions of the realm: could there really be no one with whom these matters might be discussed? A worthy predecessor said: “What cannot be put into practice throughout the realm may still be tested in a single region.” May you who hold responsibility give this thought; scholars and commoners would be most fortunate. Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄後序
正德十有一年秋八月福建
鄉試錄成巡按福建監察御
史胡文靜暨藩臬諸司之承
事于位者肆而觀之胥作而
嘆曰美哉才閩於今為盛乎
亨惟天之降才固有不同哉
===
肪之玉鏐鐐之金翬雉之綵
丹砂石砮齒毛漆枲之利具
之質而辨其品皆是物也世
之因而資之者取無窮而用
無竭而凡於物者固有擇爾
其於才也亦然粹雅者其才
純凝整者其才正節且固者
banxin: 福建鄉試錄後序
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄後序

正德十有一年秋八月，福建鄉試錄成。巡按福建監察御史胡文靜暨藩臬諸司之承事于位者，肆而觀之，胥作而嘆曰：「美哉！才，閩於今為盛乎！」

亨惟天之降才，固有不同哉！肪之玉、鏐鐐之金、翬雉之綵、丹砂、石砮、齒、毛、漆、枲之利，具之質而辨其品，皆是物也。世之因而資之者，取無窮而用無竭，而凡於物者固有擇爾。其於才也亦然：粹雅者其才純，凝整者其才正，節且固者
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

In the autumn, in the eighth month of the eleventh year of Zhengde [1516], the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination was completed. Hu Wenjing, Regional Inspector of Fujian and Investigating Censor, together with the officials serving in the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions and the other offices, spread it out for inspection. They all rose and exclaimed in admiration: “How splendid! Talent in Fujian must now be flourishing indeed!”

I, Heng, reflect that Heaven surely bestows talent in differing forms! Jade like fat, fine gold and silver [?], the brilliant plumage of pheasants, and such useful products as cinnabar, stone arrowheads, ivory, feathers, lacquer, and hemp—all are material things, each possessing its substance and distinguishable by its grade. Those in the world who draw upon them for their needs find their supply inexhaustible and their uses unending; yet with material things there is necessarily a process of selection. So too with talent: those who are refined and elegant possess pure talent; those who are composed and orderly possess upright talent; those who are principled and steadfast …

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
其才悊以深碩且慧者其才
茂以達泱者才肆而蕩者才
靡情淵外飾君子有遺貌焉
由往古而考之昔高陽氏之
才八高辛氏之才八而天下
皆謂之才曠百世而下惟鄒
魯近樸而燕趙多奇又其最
===
後往往有借才之嘆大抵利
功勝矣
國家掄才之科凡三歲一舉其
數特異海内之士有文武忠
孝之譽彌綸天地之道去此
將無由以達况夫全閩衣冠
之舊先作胤述有若恒産閥
banxin: 福建鄉試錄後序二
punctuated:
其才悊以深；碩且慧者，其才茂以達；泱者才肆，而蕩者才靡。情淵外飾，君子有遺貌焉。由往古而考之，昔高陽氏之才八，高辛氏之才八，而天下皆謂之才。曠百世而下，惟鄒魯近樸，而燕趙多奇。又其最後，往往有借才之嘆，大抵利功勝矣。
國家掄才之科，凡三歲一舉，其數特異。海内之士，有文武忠孝之譽、彌綸天地之道，去此將無由以達。况夫全閩衣冠之舊，先作胤述，有若恒産，閥
translation_en:
…their talent is discerning and profound; those who are substantial and intelligent possess flourishing and far-reaching talent. Those of expansive spirit have unrestrained talent, while the unrestrained have dissipated talent. With inward feelings deep and outward appearance adorned [?], the gentleman sometimes disregards appearances. Examining antiquity, we find that there were eight talented men under Gaoyang and eight under Gaoxin, and all under Heaven called them men of talent. Across a hundred generations thereafter, Zou and Lu remained close to simplicity, while Yan and Zhao produced many extraordinary men. In still later times, there were often laments about having to borrow talent; broadly speaking, advantage and achievement had come to prevail.
The state's examination for selecting talent is held once every three years, and its prescribed arrangements are exceptional [?]. Scholars throughout the realm who enjoy reputations for civil and military accomplishments, loyalty and filial devotion, and who possess the Way that encompasses Heaven and Earth, would have no avenue for advancement apart from this. Moreover, throughout Fujian, the long-established traditions of the educated elite—initiated by forebears and carried on by descendants—are like a permanent patrimony. Their eminent lineages…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
傑奇瓌而蜚聲當世固自有
士然就諸子今日所能而觀
之叙大業則正君心而釐國
是語朝著則列忠義而黜奸
諛警郡邑則首循謹而屏苛
墨磨礱淹貫之抱雄渾宏富
之氣皆於文乎發之然諸子
===
豈徒致其才於文而已其將
有先天下而憂者焉矧我
國家養士之法復古庠序之制
郡縣鄉社莫不有學士于其
間藏脩而游息焉者無或他
技六藝之尊蓋百五十年于
茲未之或改也諸士子涵育
banxin: 福建鄉試錄後序三
punctuated: 傑奇瓌而蜚聲當世，固自有士。然就諸子今日所能而觀之，叙大業則正君心而釐國是，語朝著則列忠義而黜奸諛，警郡邑則首循謹而屏苛墨。磨礱淹貫之抱，雄渾宏富之氣，皆於文乎發之。然諸子豈徒致其才於文而已？其將有先天下而憂者焉。矧我國家養士之法，復古庠序之制，郡縣鄉社莫不有學。士于其間藏脩而游息焉者，無或他技。六藝之尊，蓋百五十年于茲，未之或改也。諸士子涵育
translation_en:
…outstanding and extraordinary, winning renown in their own age: there have certainly been such scholars. Yet, judging by what you gentlemen have demonstrated today, when discussing the great tasks of government, you speak of rectifying the ruler’s mind and setting national policy aright; when addressing the ranks at court, you advocate advancing the loyal and righteous and dismissing the treacherous and flattering; when admonishing prefectural and county administrations, you give priority to conscientious, circumspect officials and reject the harsh and corrupt. Your aspirations, honed through study and informed by comprehensive learning, and your vigorous, expansive spirit all find expression in your writing. Yet surely you gentlemen will not exercise your talents in writing alone? Among you there will be those who take the cares of the world upon themselves before others do.

Moreover, our dynasty’s method of nurturing scholars restores the ancient system of schools: prefectures, counties, townships, and local communities all have schools. The scholars who study and cultivate themselves, and take their leisure and rest within them, pursue no extraneous skills. The Six Arts have been held in esteem for some hundred and fifty years now, without any change. You scholars, nurtured…

title: 正德十一年福建鄉試錄
text:
聖化旣專且久行將進于春官敭
于
大庭而效其用於四方代工成
務以開太平於無窮者必有
眞才焉出無亦於九十人者
占之亨猥以文辭為職而濫
論士之請於卒事也因致望
===
焉
河南河南府洛陽縣儒學訓
導夏亨謹序
banxin: 福建鄉試錄後序 四
punctuated:
聖化旣專且久，行將進于春官，敭于大庭，而效其用於四方，代工成務，以開太平於無窮者，必有眞才焉出。無亦於九十人者占之？亨猥以文辭為職，而濫論士之請，於卒事也，因致望焉。
河南河南府洛陽縣儒學訓導夏亨謹序。
translation_en:
…by the sage influence, with undivided attention and over a long period. They will soon advance to the Ministry of Rites and distinguish themselves at the imperial court, putting their abilities to use throughout the realm, carrying out their appointed duties and accomplishing affairs, thereby inaugurating an age of peace without end. Surely men of genuine talent will emerge among them. May we not look to these ninety men for such promise? I, Heng, unworthily make literary composition my occupation and have presumptuously undertaken the request to assess scholars [?]. Now that the work is finished, I express these hopes for them.
Preface respectfully written by Xia Heng, Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan.
